title: Anywhere Girls
fact: 2nd Grade's "Anywhere Girls" is sung by Catherine Dwyer (also of Remember Sports) rather than the band's usual songwriter, Peter Gill - it comes from Girls and Boys, a 2026 album built as ten songs about girls followed by ten songs about boys.

title: Autosmile
fact: @ is the Philadelphia duo of Victoria Rose and Stone Filipczak, who built a cult following in the American underground with their acclaimed 2021 psych-folk debut Mind Palace Music. "Autosmile" is the title track of their first album for the label 4AD, a sprawling seven-minute ballad that leans into minimal acoustic guitar and the pair's intertwined vocal melodies rather than the electronic flourishes they're also known for.

title: Bird
fact: "Bird" is a single by the Philadelphia art-folk duo @ (Victoria Rose and Stone Filipczak), taken from their debut album Autosmile on 4AD. The duo says the song was inspired by dead birds that kept turning up on their deck and was written during a bike ride through Druid Hill Park in Baltimore; the lyrics lean on puns to lighten the subject matter.

Real Life
fact: "Real Life" is the third single from Melbourne trio Acopia's 2025 debut album, Blush Response, released on Scenic Route Records. The band - Kate Durman, Lachlan McGeehan, and Morgan Wright - built the song around a looping arpeggiated synth motif and recorded it in a rooftop studio inside a mostly abandoned office building in Melbourne's South Yarra neighborhood.

title: anything
fact: Adrianne Lenker's "Anything," from 2020's Songs, reframes love as something familial rather than dramatic - she sings "I don't wanna be the owner of your fantasy, I just wanna be a part of your family," less interested in early-relationship thrills than in just belonging.

title: blue and red horses
fact: "Blue and Red Horses" is a highlight from Adrianne Lenker's third solo album, abysskiss (2018), released on Saddle Creek Records. The ten songs were written while Lenker was touring with Big Thief, and the album was recorded at Panoramic House overlooking the Pacific in West Marin, California, with producer Luke Temple and engineer Gabe Wax. Most tracks, including this one, were captured in just one or two takes.

title: cradle
fact: "cradle" was the first single from Adrianne Lenker's 2018 solo album abysskiss. She recorded the album with Luke Temple of Here We Go Magic at Panoramic House in West Marin, California, shortly after two weeks spent traveling through the American South.

title: Fool
fact: "Fool" was one of the very first songs tracked for Adrianne Lenker's 2024 album Bright Future, recorded late at night with producer Philip Weinrobe. Weinrobe said the song shows "a different side" to Lenker's writing, since she's often associated with melancholy but "can do unbridled ecstatic happiness just as deftly as every other emotion." Lenker herself described it as "a buoyant questioning of creaturey loopiness," and on the recording she can be heard audibly laughing when she slips into the line "we could be friends."

title: Free Treasure
fact: Adrianne Lenker has called "Free Treasure" one of her all-time favorite songs she's written, and its title came about by accident: she was singing it on a friend's stoop when Big Thief bandmate James Krivchenia chimed in with the words "free treasure" during the last chorus, and it stuck. The song landed on her 2024 album Bright Future, which earned a Grammy nomination for Best Folk Album, with singer Mat Davidson joining her on vocal and guitar harmonies.

title: Indiana
fact: "Indiana" is track seven on Adrianne Lenker's second solo album, "Hours Were the Birds," recorded in 2013 at Terrarium Studios back in her hometown of Minneapolis with producer Rob Oesterlin. The stripped-down, all-acoustic-guitar record was self-released in January 2014 before Saddle Creek Records reissued it in 2018.

title: not a lot, just forever
fact: "not a lot, just forever" is from Adrianne Lenker's 2020 album songs, recorded in a cabin in Westhampton, Massachusetts, with engineer Phil Weinrobe. The pair recorded everything "AAA" (analog, analog, analog) with zero digital processing, and hit early setbacks with unreliable electricity and gear, at one point relying on Weinrobe's battery-powered Sony Walkman as their only working tape machine before an Otari eight-track recorder arrived. Most of the album's songs, including this one, were written right there during the sessions.

title: Once A Bunch
fact: 'Once A Bunch' started life as a bonus track tucked onto the Japanese CD release of Adrianne Lenker's solo album Bright Future before she gave it a proper standalone release. It was recorded during the same sessions as the album with producer Phil Weinrobe, featuring Mat Davidson and Josefin Runsteen. The country-tinged tune has a loose, warm feel that fits right alongside the rest of Bright Future.

title: Sadness As A Gift
fact: 'Sadness as a Gift' is a single from Adrianne Lenker's 2024 solo album Bright Future, recorded in fall 2022 at the rural analog studio Double Infinity and co-produced with Philip Weinrobe. The warm, strummed arrangement is colored by Josefin Runsteen's violin, and Lenker has described the song as being about the end of a relationship.

title: zombie girl
fact: "zombie girl" appears on Adrianne Lenker's 2020 album songs, which she recorded in a cabin in Westhampton, Massachusetts with producer Phil Weinrobe after a tour was cancelled. Lenker has said the song grew out of a sleep-paralysis-like state, using the eerie "zombie girl" image to capture the strange half-awake feeling of missing someone after a breakup.

title: American Dream
fact: "American Dream" marked Alabama Shakes' return in 2026 with their first new music in roughly a decade, following the massive success of 2015's Sound & Color. That earlier album topped the Billboard 200 and won four Grammy Awards, including Best Alternative Music Album, cementing the Athens, Alabama band led by Brittany Howard as one of the era's biggest rock breakouts before their long hiatus.

title: Future People
fact: "Future People" comes from Alabama Shakes' 2015 album Sound & Color and was co-written by the whole band - Brittany Howard, Heath Fogg, Zac Cockrell, and Steve Johnson - together with producer Blake Mills. The blues-rock track is built around a tricksy, fuzz-bass guitar part that climaxes in a wall of distorted, reverb-heavy sound.

title: Garden
fact: "Garden" is from Alabama Shakes' 2026 album I Must Be Dreaming (August 2026), their first since 2015's Sound & Color, after a hiatus that ended in late 2024. The song showcases the quieter, more sensual side of Brittany Howard's voice.

title: Gimme All Your Love
fact: "Gimme All Your Love," written by Brittany Howard for Alabama Shakes' 2015 album Sound & Color, builds its drama around a midsong tempo shift and vocal effects on Howard's voice. After debuting it on Saturday Night Live, the band later played the song live at Prince's Paisley Park studio in Minneapolis in June 2015, with Prince himself joining them onstage for an extended guitar solo.

title: How Love s Supposed To Go
fact: Alabama Shakes' "How Love's Supposed To Go," from 2026's I Must Be Dreaming, opens with a direct hip-hop beat and a heavy bassline hook - the album was produced by the band alongside six-time Grammy winner Shawn Everett.

title: I Ain't the Same
fact: Alabama Shakes started when Brittany Howard asked classmate Zac Cockrell to write songs together after discovering he played bass in an advanced psychology class at their Athens, Alabama high school.

title: Shoegaze
fact: Despite the name, Alabama Shakes' “Shoegaze” isn't about the genre - it's a song about restlessness and loneliness, pivoting on the line “It ain't no fun to be lonely.”

title: Sound & Color
fact: The title track that opens Alabama Shakes' 2015 album Sound & Color begins not with guitars but with a vibraphone, an instrument nobody expected from the raw Alabama blues-rock band after their stripped-down debut. Brittany Howard and keyboardist Ben Tanner both played vibraphone on the track, which gradually builds into a lush string arrangement. The unexpected instrumentation set the tone for an album that pushed the band into much more experimental territory.

title: Uninvited
album: City of Angels: Music from the Motion Picture

title: One Stop
fact: Recorded at the storied Rockfield Studios in Wales with longtime producer John Parish, 'One Stop' is built around little more than a single piano motif and Harding's own multi-tracked voice. It even name-drops art-rock legend John Cale in the lyrics — 'I met the real John Cale, he had no words, but I don't mind' — and served as the first single off her 2026 album Train on the Island.

title: Venus in the Zinnia feat. H. Hawkline
fact: "Venus in the Zinnia" is a duet between Aldous Harding and fellow songwriter H. Hawkline, who also plays bass and guitar on the track. Released in 2026 as the second single from Harding's album "Train on the Island," the song floats her voice over Wurlitzer piano and percussion, with surreal, dreamlike lyrical imagery.

title: Red Hook Rain
fact: Alex Cameron has a side career you might not expect: he's co-written songs for the Killers, including tracks on Wonderful Wonderful and Imploding the Mirage. 'Red Hook Rain,' from his 2026 album Late to Set, was pitched by his own camp as 'Barry Gibb meets Martin Rev' — a heartbroken, hopeful detour written, fittingly, on the edge of an actual hurricane.

title: Strangers Kiss with Angel Olsen
fact: This Springsteen-leaning duet with Angel Olsen comes from Alex Cameron's 2017 album Forced Witness, playing out as a couple trading barbed breakup advice. The music video, co-starring Girls' Jemima Kirke, follows two lonely strangers who find each other on a New York subway platform.

title: Afterlife
fact: Afterlife is a single from Alex G's 2025 album Headlights (RCA Records). It is driven by mandolin and airy, bagpipe-like keyboards, and has been compared to The Waterboys' Celtic-tinged anthems.

title: Change
fact: "Change" appears on Alex G's fourth album, Trick, which he self-released on Bandcamp in November 2012 while still a student at Temple University in Philadelphia. The lo-fi record was written, performed, and recorded entirely on his own, and it was later reissued with a professional remaster through Lucky Number in 2015. Early albums like Trick spread by word of mouth and built his cult following before he signed to a bigger label.

title: Gretel
fact: "Gretel" appears on (Sandy) Alex G's 2019 album House of Sugar and reworks the Brothers Grimm fairy tale from Gretel's point of view, giving it a darker, more cynical spin. The album's title itself was inspired by a short story called "The House Made of Sugar" by Argentine writer Silvina Ocampo, which Alex G said got stuck in his head while writing.

title: Harvey
fact: Harvey appeared on Alex G's 2014 album DSU and is often cited as a fan-favorite entry point into his catalog. The song is sung from the perspective of what sounds like a child or an imaginary friend, repeating the mantra 'success for my buddy, success for my friend,' giving it a disarmingly simple but emotionally layered feel. Critics have praised it as a perfect, airy-yet-angular pop song that still sounds sleepy and wide awake at once.

title: Immunity
fact: "Immunity" appears on Alex G's 2022 album God Save the Animals. Philadelphia songwriter Alex Giannascoli wrote and demoed the record alone during pandemic lockdown before bringing it into several studios around his hometown to finish. The song's piano shifts from a major key into a minor one near the end, and it closes out with an unexpected instrumental jam of wobbly guitars and staccato piano.

title: Mis
fact: "Mis" is track six on Alex G's self-released 2012 album Rules, which he recorded and produced entirely on his own and put out independently via Bandcamp — the cover art was even painted by his mother. The lo-fi record predates Alex G's wider breakthrough and was later remastered and reissued on vinyl and CD by Lucky Number in 2015.

title: Mission
fact: Alex G, born Alexander Giannascoli in Havertown, Pennsylvania, built his following recording tapes in his bedroom and posting them to Bandcamp. He briefly performed as "(Sandy) Alex G" after a naming conflict with another artist using the name Alex G.

title: Oranges
fact: "Oranges" appears on (Sandy) Alex G's eighth studio album, House of Sugar (2019), which the artist recorded across multiple cities including New York, Philadelphia, and St. Louis. The album's title comes from SugarHouse Casino in Philadelphia, now known as Rivers Casino.

title: Sarah
fact: Sarah was written around 2011-2012, the same era as Alex G's album Trick, but wasn't officially released until it appeared on a 2015 reissue and later as a standalone single in 2022. It found a huge new audience nearly a decade after it was written, going viral on TikTok and streaming platforms alongside another older track, "Mary."

Electric Sickness
fact: alexalone is Austin musician Alex Peterson (who also plays bass for Hovvdy and Lomelda). "Electric Sickness" was actually the very first alexalone song, originally written to score a documentary about Austin BBQ culture and highway gentrification.

title: Out Of Phase (feat. Lola Kirke)
fact: Hot Chip frontman Alexis Taylor's "Out of Phase" features actor-singer Lola Kirke and appears on his 2026 solo album Paris in the Spring (Night Time Stories). It was inspired by David Lynch, and the video, directed by Will Kindrick, was shot entirely on an iPhone.

title: I Can Love You Like That
I Don't Ever Wanna Leave California
Hunger Of The Pine
fact: Alt-J's "Hunger of the Pine" samples the line "I'm a female rebel" from Miley Cyrus's song "4x4," after drummer Thom Green worked on a remix of that track and folded the vocal sample into the band's new song. Cyrus gave her blessing to the use and later returned the favor by having Alt-J's "Fitzpleasure" played during her Bangerz tour.

title: Left Hand Free
fact: Alt-J has called "Left Hand Free" the "least alt-J song ever" — a Southern rock-flavored jam the trio wrote almost as a tongue-in-cheek joke around a guitar riff, after their label pushed them for a more radio-friendly single. It ended up becoming one of the biggest hits from their 2014 album This Is All Yours anyway.

title: Neredesin Sen
fact: Neredesin Sen opens Garip, the sixth album from Dutch band AltÄ±n GÃ¼n (February 20, 2026, ATO Records), a tribute to Anatolian folk giant NeÅŸet ErtaÅŸ. It reworks a Turkish folk standard with a throbbing bass line and an early-80s indie feel.

title: Angoisse
fact: ALVILDA is a Paris quartet — Nina, Mel, Eva and Sandra — who sing entirely in French and blend the melodic charm of 1960s girl-group pop with late-1970s power pop and punk energy. "Angoisse" was the bouncy, new-wave-leaning lead single from their debut full-length, C'est Déjà L'heure, released through UK punk label Static Shock Records.

title: Adult Diversion
fact: Adult Diversion was released October 28, 2013 as the second single from Alvvays' self-titled debut album, where it's the first track (July 22, 2014). Molly Rankin, Alec O'Hanley and Brian Murphy wrote it.

title: Archie, Marry Me
fact: "Archie, Marry Me" is from Alvvays' self-titled 2014 debut album. Songwriter Molly Rankin has said she chose the name "Archie" because it was uncommon but felt right, writing the song from the perspective of poking fun at being in your twenties and surrounded by engaged friends.

title: Not My Baby
fact: 'Not My Baby' comes from Alvvays' 2017 album Antisocialites, co-written by Molly Rankin and Alec O'Hanley, who also co-produced the record alongside John Congleton. The band actually road-tested the song live for a couple of years before it ever made it onto tape.

title: Saved By A Waif
fact: "Saved by a Waif" is track nine on Alvvays' 2017 album Antisocialites, written by Molly Rankin and Alec O'Hanley. The record was recorded across three studios — Kingsize Soundlabs in Los Angeles, Tarbox Road Studios in upstate New York, and Union Sound Studios in Toronto — with O'Hanley and John Congleton producing.

title: Tile By Tile
fact: Tile By Tile, written by Molly Rankin and Alec O'Hanley, is track nine on Alvvays' 2022 album Blue Rev. The band recorded the album with producer Shawn Everett at his Los Angeles studio, where they famously played through the entire record front-to-back twice in a single day to capture a live, unpolished energy.

title: Come with Me
fact: Come with Me opens Fading Lines (2016), the debut album by Dutch musician Annelotte de Graaf as Amber Arcades. She flew to New York to record it with producer Ben Greenberg, and members of Quilt and Real Estate served as her backing band.

title: Fading Lines
fact: "Fading Lines" is the title track and second single from Amber Arcades' 2016 debut album. Songwriter Annelotte de Graaf has said it was loosely inspired by her grandfather's death and the way memories blur together over time; its music video features a parachutist falling in reverse.

title: Goodnight Europe
fact: "Goodnight Europe" was released as a single in April 2018 ahead of Amber Arcades' second album, European Heartbreak, and arrived with a short film that formed part of a loose trilogy of videos telling a modern love story. The project was released through the UK label Heavenly Recordings.

title: It Changes
fact: "It Changes" followed Amber Arcades' 2016 debut, Fading Lines. The project is the work of Dutch multi-instrumentalist Annelotte de Graaf, who said the Stones-inspired song is about how you never really know how something new is going to turn out, no matter how sure you feel when you start it.

title: Oh My Love (What Have We Done)
fact: "Oh My Love (What Have We Done)" is the third track on European Heartbreak (2018), the second album by Amber Arcades, the project of Dutch singer-songwriter Annelotte de Graaf. The song stands out on the record for its use of horns, giving it a bittersweet, brass-flecked pop texture distinct from her jangly earlier work. De Graaf wrote and recorded the album while balancing her music career with law studies and human-rights work.

title: Right Now
fact: "Right Now" comes from Fading Lines (2016), the debut full-length by Amber Arcades, the recording project of Dutch singer-songwriter Annelotte de Graaf. She made the album in New York with producer Ben Greenberg of the band The Men, with musicians from Quilt and Real Estate filling out her backing band.

title: Simple Song
fact: 'Simple Song' is the sunny, horn-flecked opening track on Amber Arcades' 2018 album European Heartbreak. Its music video was released as the second installment of a trilogy that began with the clip for 'Goodnight Europe.'

title: Something's Gonna Take Your Love Away
fact: Amber Arcades is the project of Dutch musician Annelotte de Graaf, whose sound blends folky melodies and spaced-out guitars into what's sometimes called "dreamfolk." "Something's Gonna Take Your Love Away" comes from her 2018 album European Heartbreak.

title: Where Did You Go
fact: "Where Did You Go" is the fourth single from Dutch musician Annelotte de Graaf's (Amber Arcades) 2018 album European Heartbreak. In its music video, de Graaf and her partner pin a map of Europe to a wall and throw a dart to pick their next home, then blindfold each other to wander a forest when the dart lands on open grass.

title: Wouldn't Even Know
fact: "Wouldn't Even Know" comes from Dutch musician Annelotte de Graaf's 2017 EP Cannonball, released under her Amber Arcades project. The track was produced by Ben Greenberg and features additional vocals from Bill Ryder-Jones, formerly of the Coral.

title: Run Run Run
album: Ocean Child : Songs Of Yoko Ono

title: Honestly?
fact: "Honestly?" is the third track on American Football's self-titled 1999 debut (retroactively called LP1), recorded with producer Brendan Gamble at Private Studios in the band's college town of Urbana, Illinois. Mike Kinsella's lyrics capture the hazy uncertainty of looking back on teenage feelings. The album became a foundational text of the emo revival more than a decade after its release.

title: I'll See You When We're Both Not So Emotional
No Feeling
fact: 'No Feeling' comes from American Football's fourth self-titled album, released in 2026, and features guest harmony vocals from Brendan Yates, frontman of the hardcore band Turnstile. Mike Kinsella told NME that Yates was originally supposed to be just one of several voices on a call-and-response chorus part, but after Yates asked to try a higher harmony of his own, his voice was so distinctive the part became his alone. It's a rare genre-crossing cameo between two very different corners of the rock world.

title: Wake Her Up (feat. Wisp)
fact: "Wake Her Up" teams Midwest emo pioneers American Football with shoegaze artist Wisp, appearing on American Football's fourth self-titled album from 2026. Frontman Mike Kinsella has called it the band's "best Smiths impression to date." The music video, co-directed by skate filmmaker Ty Evans and Oscar-winning director Cord Jefferson, follows Kinsella and Wisp on nighttime bike rides through Los Angeles while dreamlike images of Paris are projected around them.

title: Why Don't We Fall in Love (Album Version)
Chewing Gum
fact: "Chewing Gum" was the lead single announcing Amyl and the Sniffers' 2024 album Cartoon Darkness. Frontwoman Amy Taylor said the song is about actively choosing fun and freedom over always being "right," summed up in the chorus line about choosing to be young and choosing bad decisions because life is short. Taylor described the song's outlook as neither pure nihilism nor pure hedonism, but "the chaos between the two."

title: Doing In Me Head
fact: Guitarist Dec Martens originally wrote 'Doing in Me Head' as a disco track inspired by the Gap Band, but once Amyl and the Sniffers got hold of it, it turned into a vocoder-laced punk song influenced by the Beastie Boys. It appears on the band's 2024 album Cartoon Darkness, which they recorded with producer Nick Launay at Dave Grohl's Studio 606 — on the very same mixing desk used for Nirvana's Nevermind and Fleetwood Mac's Rumours. Not bad company for an Australian punk band's growing catalog.

title: U Should Not Be Doing That
A Nervous Tic Motion of the Head to the Left
album: Andrew Bird & the Mysterious Production of Eggs
fact: Andrew Bird picked up the violin at age four and studied it formally at Northwestern University. His live shows are built entirely in real time with loop pedals - he'll pluck out a violin intro, loop it, bow the strings for another layer, whistle a melody, then pick up a guitar, building each song piece by piece on stage.

title: Anonanimal
fact: "Anonanimal," from Andrew Bird's 2009 album Noble Beast, showcases his signature technique of building songs out of layered, looped plucked violin combined with acoustic guitar. The song shifts through several distinct sections, including a jammy detour near the end that critics have compared to Wilco's extended live workouts. Bird is known for building these looped violin parts live on stage in real time rather than relying on pre-recorded tracks.

title: Eyeoneye
fact: Andrew Bird's "Eyeoneye," the first single from 2012's Break It Yourself, was recorded live in his West Illinois barn straight to 8-track tape with drummer Martin Dosh and guitarist Jeremy Ylvisaker - no studio, no overdubs, just the sound of the room.

title: Fake Palindromes
album: Andrew Bird & the Mysterious Production of Eggs
fact: "Fake Palindromes" is the most straightforwardly rock-oriented track on Andrew Bird's 2005 breakthrough The Mysterious Production of Eggs, built on thrumming bass, psychedelic guitar, and echo-drenched fiddle. It's a showcase for Bird's dual musical identity: a classically trained violinist who is equally famous for his operatic, full-bodied whistling, which he says is deliberately pitched to cut through his own mid-range instruments.

title: Fallorun
fact: Andrew Bird originally titled this My Finest Work Yet track "Fall of Throne," but when his wife misheard the phrase as "fall or run," he liked that better and renamed the song. Musically, Bird has said the track was inspired by New Order's "Ceremony," which he fell for after hearing it play in a public restroom.

title: Imitosis
fact: "Imitosis" started life as a slower, sparser song called "I" (performed live as "Capital I") on Andrew Bird's 2003 album Weather Systems. He reworked it into the more upbeat "Imitosis" for his 2007 album Armchair Apocrypha.

title: Left Handed Kisses
fact: 'Left Handed Kisses' is a duet between Andrew Bird and Fiona Apple from Bird's 2016 album Are You Serious. Bird said the song began as an internal dialogue about his struggle to write a simple, uncomplicated love song, and he realized it needed to become a duet when another 'voice' crept into the lyrics - leading him to recruit Apple as a sparring partner. The pair also performed it together on The Ellen DeGeneres Show.

title: Olympians
fact: "Olympians," from Andrew Bird's 2019 album My Finest Work Yet, grew out of an earlier instrumental called "Gotholympians" that first appeared on his 2013 live album Fingerlings before being reworked with new lyrics. The album itself was tracked with the full band playing together in the studio at once, letting the instruments' sound bleed across microphones rather than recording each part in isolation.

title: Pulaski at Night
album: I Want to See Pulaski at Night
fact: The title comes from an offhand remark: a visiting Thai exchange student once wistfully told a friend of Andrew Bird's, "I want to see Pulaski at night" — funny and absurd, since Pulaski is a gritty stretch of road running the length of Chicago's west side, not a sightseeing spot. The phrase stuck with Bird for two decades before he built this ambivalent, loving ode to his hometown around it.

title: Roma Fade
fact: "Roma Fade" was released as a single in March 2016 ahead of Andrew Bird's album Are You Serious, where it appears as the second track. The song opens with one of Bird's signature whistled melodies before building into full-band instrumentation, and the album overall features guest contributions from Fiona Apple and Blake Mills.

title: Sisyphus
fact: Andrew Bird's "Sisyphus," from 2019's My Finest Work Yet, retells the Greek myth of the trickster condemned to push a boulder uphill forever - midway through the song, the music itself pauses on the lyric "paused," a deliberate fermata built right into the arrangement.

title: Skin Is, My
album: Andrew Bird & the Mysterious Production of Eggs

title: Sovay
album: Andrew Bird & the Mysterious Production of Eggs

title: Tin Foiled
album: Things Are Really Great Here, Sort Of...

title: When That Helicopter Comes
fact: Andrew Bird's version of "When That Helicopter Comes" is a cover of a song written and originally performed by the Handsome Family's Brett and Rennie Sparks. Bird recorded it for Hands of Glory (2012), a companion album to his record Break It Yourself built around classic country and folk covers plus one new original. The backing group on the sessions took its name, Hands of Glory, directly from the record.

title: Thank You For Being A Friend
I Just Want To Be Your Everything
Call
fact: 'Call' appears on Andy Shauf's 2021 album Wilds, one of nine songs culled from roughly fifty tracks he recorded during the sessions for his 2020 concept album The Neon Skyline. Wilds functions as a companion piece to that record, revisiting the same pair of characters and their relationship from different angles and points in time.

title: Catch Your Eye
fact: "Catch Your Eye" is from Andy Shauf's 2023 album "Norm," which he wrote, performed, and self-produced entirely alone in his garage studio. The record's narrative concept, centered on a character named Norm, grew out of Shauf's fascination with David Lynch's "Mulholland Drive."

title: The Magician
fact: "The Magician" opens Andy Shauf's 2016 concept album The Party, which plays out as a series of vignettes set over the course of one house party. Shauf wrote, performed, engineered, and produced almost the entire record himself, with the sole exception of the string arrangements, which were composed and played by Colin Nealis.

title: The Moon
fact: Andy Shauf grew up in Saskatchewan, where his parents ran an electronics and music store - giving him early access to instruments including the clarinet, which is why woodwinds show up so often in his arrangements.

title: You're Out Wasting
fact: "You're Out Wasting" comes from Andy Shauf's 2012 album The Bearer of Bad News, which he wrote over four years and recorded almost entirely by himself in a home studio set up in his parents' basement in Saskatchewan. He played nearly every instrument on the record, leaning on his grandfather's old guitar and a clarinet he'd been given as a Christmas gift. The album built a cult following and was reissued in 2015 on Tender Loving Empire and Party Damage Records.

title: (We Are All Mirrors)
fact: This is the stripped-down solo version of the title track from Angel Olsen's 2019 album All Mirrors. Olsen originally planned to release a bare-bones solo record alongside a full-band version of the same songs, recording the intimate takes with producer Michael Harris in Anacortes, Washington, before building the orchestral title track with producer John Congleton and a 14-piece orchestra arranged by Jherek Bischoff.

title: Acrobat
fact: "Acrobat" opens Angel Olsen's 2012 debut full-length, Half Way Home, released on the small label Bathetic Records. The track is built around gentle acoustic guitar layered with a droning pump organ, a spare, lo-fi arrangement characteristic of Olsen's early era before her later, more fully produced band records.

title: All Mirrors
fact: Angel Olsen has said “All Mirrors” grew from the idea that “we are all mirrors to and for each other” - a song about how people and memories keep echoing each other over time.

title: All the Flowers
fact: All the Flowers comes from Olsen's 2022 album Big Time, which she co-produced with Jonathan Wilson at his Fivestar Studios in Topanga Canyon, California. Wilson played an array of instruments across the sessions, including lap steel, mellotron, zither and mandolin, and Nashville musician Spencer Cullum added pedal steel, giving the record its warm, Americana-leaning sound. The album marked a deliberate shift toward country and classic pop influences for Olsen.

title: Enemy
album: Burn Your Fire For No Witness
fact: 'Enemy' is track ten on Angel Olsen's 2014 breakthrough album Burn Your Fire for No Witness, which the singer recorded in an abandoned chapel. Described by critics as understated yet cathartic, the song includes one of the record's most direct lyrical moments, with Olsen singing plainly, 'You could be the only one who knows the truth of me.'

title: Forgiven - Forgotten
album: Burn Your Fire For No Witness

title: Ghost On
fact: "Ghost On" is track four on Angel Olsen's fifth studio album, Big Time, released in 2022 on Jagjaguwar. Olsen co-produced the record with Jonathan Wilson, who plays drums, guitar, and percussion on the song alongside bassist Emily Elhaj and guitarist Jake Blanton, with the whole album recorded at Wilson's Fivestarstudios in Los Angeles.

title: Hi-Five
album: Burn Your Fire For No Witness

title: Intern
fact: Angel Olsen's "Intern" opens 2016's My Woman with a total left turn into synthpop - she's described it as something of a joke aimed at expectations, made with friends who work in synth music because she wanted to do "something sarcastic" after her earlier, more traditional records.

title: Safety Dance
fact: Angel Olsen moved from St. Louis to Chicago at 20 and fell in with the city's DIY music scene. A friend passed her demos along to folk musician Bonnie "Prince" Billy (Will Oldham), who invited her to sing backing vocals on two of his albums before she launched her solo career.

title: Sister
fact: Angel Olsen's "Sister," from 2016's My Woman, stretches out past the eight-minute mark as the full band improvises and builds - one of several ways the album's back half deliberately loosens up after the tighter, poppier songs that open it.

title: Stars
album: Burn Your Fire For No Witness

title: Waving, Smiling
fact: "Waving, Smiling" is one of two new songs included on Angel Olsen's 2020 release Whole New Mess, a stripped-down companion album featuring alternate versions of songs that would later appear on All Mirrors. Built around a simple fingerpicking pattern with a classic-soul feel, Olsen described the song as capturing a peaceful, bittersweet sense of closure.

title: White Fire
album: Burn Your Fire For No Witness
fact: "White Fire" is the emotional centerpiece of Angel Olsen's 2014 album Burn Your Fire for No Witness, and its key lyric actually gave the record its title. Olsen told Billboard it was one of the last songs she wrote for the album and almost didn't share it, written from the perspective of an older version of herself looking back rather than addressed to a former partner like most of the record's other songs.

"27" was released as a double single with "Hologram" in November 2022, Angelo De Augustine's first new music after his 2021 collaborative album with Sufjan Stevens, A Beginner's Mind. Stevens returned the favor here, contributing synthesizer, drum machine, electric guitar, bass, Fender Rhodes, and background vocals to the track.

title: The Ballad of Betty and Barney Hill
Toil and Trouble
fact: The title track from Angelo De Augustine's 2023 album nods to the witches' chant in Shakespeare's Macbeth ('double, double, toil and trouble'), reimagined as a meditation on who's really steering a curated, filtered version of reality. De Augustine wrote, arranged, performed, and produced the entire album himself across 27 different instruments, and the song's stop-motion video centers on an animated singing cauldron.

title: Fabienk
fact: "Fabienk" is a 2026 song by Angine de Poitrine, a Quebec math-rock duo -- guitarist "Khn" and drummer "Klek" -- formed in Saguenay in 2019, known for performing in costume as a stage persona. The song and its parent album, Vol II, won the Polaris Music Prize's companion song prize the same year.

title: Sarniezz
fact: Sarniezz is from Vol. II (April 2026), the second album by the masked Quebec duo Angine de Poitrine. Their live KEXP performance of the song went viral and racked up millions of views.

title: Sherpa
fact: Sherpa comes from the first EP by Angine de Poitrine, an anonymous duo from Saguenay, Quebec who play microtonal rock in polka-dot costumes and giant papier-mache masks. Their KEXP performance went viral, and guitarist Khn plays a double-necked microtonal guitar.

title: Alvin Row
album: Spirit They're Gone Spirit They've Vanished

title: Did You See the Words
fact: "Did You See the Words" opens Animal Collective's 2005 breakthrough album Feels. The band had their guitars retuned to match a friend's out-of-tune piano, giving the whole record its warped, shimmering sound, and this opener's cascading, falsetto-heavy harmonies help kick off what many critics consider the band's turning-point album.

title: FloriDada
fact: Animal Collective's 'FloriDada' was the lead single from 2016's Painting With. Avey Tare has said the idea sparked from hearing a Los Angeles radio segment called 'Dumb Things People Are Doing in Florida,' though the song isn't really about the state - it's about resisting tidy geographic and cultural stereotypes. The title's Dada reference ties into the album's broader art-movement inspiration, with lyrics stacking up odd, mixed-up details like 'the fair hair of Sweden' and 'a dancer from Ghana.'

title: Grass
fact: "Grass" was released as a single off Animal Collective's 2005 album Feels. For the whole record, the band tuned their guitars to match a friend's piano, which happened to already be out of tune, giving the album -- and "Grass" in particular -- its distinctively warped, chiming guitar tone.

title: Jimmy Mack (Martha and the Vandellas Cover)
Summertime Clothes
fact: "Summertime Clothes," from Animal Collective's 2009 album Merriweather Post Pavilion, was originally titled "Bearhug" while the band was writing it. The record was written and recorded in about a month at Sweet Tea Recording Studio in Oxford, Mississippi, with Avey Tare and Panda Bear trading vocals over swirling synths and a bouncing low end meant to evoke a carefree summer feeling.

title: 2 Cool 2 Care
fact: "2 Cool 2 Care" opens Anna Burch's debut solo album, Quit the Curse, released in February 2018. The record grew out of Burch's scrappy phone demos, which Chicago musician Paul Cherry helped flesh out into full band arrangements.

title: Can't Sleep
fact: "Can't Sleep" opens Anna Burch's 2020 album "If You're Dreaming," setting a restless tone for the record. Burch has said the song grew directly out of a real bout of insomnia, part of a broader thread of anxious energy that runs through the album's lyrics.

title: Not So Bad
fact: Anna Burch wrote 'Not So Bad' just one day before heading into the studio to record her 2020 album If You're Dreaming, realizing the record needed one hopeful, escapist pop song to balance its more melancholy moments. Produced by Sam Evian, the track came together almost immediately, built around a light, jazzy chord progression and swirling saxophone. Burch has said her mom used to tease her for how sad her lyrics usually were — this one was the exception.

title: Party's Over
fact: Anna Burch wrote "Party's Over" after a night out that didn't go the way she'd hoped, and it became one of the first songs written for her album If You're Dreaming. The self-directed music video leans into dark comedy, casting Burch as a bride left at the altar when her groom goes on the run - from a sea monster.

title: Tea-Soaked Letter
fact: In the video for Anna Burch's “Tea-Soaked Letter,” she makes tea, makes toast, and reads tarot cards while waiting to hear from the person she's singing about - a song asking a love interest to actually follow through on better communication.

title: Tell Me What's True
fact: 'Tell Me What's True' comes from Anna Burch's 2018 album If You're Dreaming, recorded with producer Sam Evian at his home studio in New York's Catskill Mountains. Burch self-directed the song's music video, filmed in Hamtramck, Michigan, riffing on a scene from Martin Scorsese's 1974 film Alice Doesn't Live Here Anymore of someone auditioning in a cowboy bar.

title: What I Want
fact: "What I Want" is track eight on Anna Burch's 2018 debut album Quit the Curse. It's been described as an anti-breakup song, with Burch taking a level-headed, mature approach and singing that she "won't play the victim" just because she didn't get what she wanted. Burch, a Detroit songwriter, had previously sung with Frontier Ruckus and co-fronted Failed Flowers before going solo.

title: Don't Beat the Girl out of My Boy
God's Lonely Man (feat. Iggy Pop)
fact: This track opens Anna Calvi's 2026 EP Is This All There Is? on Domino Records, a four-song project where each track features a different collaborator: Iggy Pop, Matt Berninger, Laurie Anderson, and Perfume Genius. Calvi and Iggy Pop also star together in the music video, directed by Luigi Calabrese.

Ageispolis
fact: "Ageispolis" is the fourth track on Aphex Twin's 1992 debut Selected Ambient Works 85-92, clocking in at 5:23. The album compiles ambient and techno pieces Richard D. James made on cassette dating back to when he was just 13 or 14 years old. Released on Apollo, a subsidiary of Belgian label R&S Records, it's now regarded as a defining, genre-expanding work of ambient electronic music.

title: Xtal
fact: Xtal opens Aphex Twin's debut album, Selected Ambient Works 85-92 (November 1992, Apollo Records). Richard D. James recorded the tracks on cassette, some reportedly dating back to 1985 when he was 14.

Month of May
fact: Arcade Fire's Win Butler met founding bandmate Josh Deu in high school at Phillips Exeter Academy. They started the band in Montreal and met Regine Chassagne, now Butler's longtime bandmate, while rehearsing at McGill University.

title: Ready to Start
fact: Arcade Fire's "Ready to Start" was the very first song written for 2010's The Suburbs, which went on to win Album of the Year at the Grammys - the band played it live at the ceremony immediately after taking home the award.

title: Unconditional II (Race and Religion) (feat. Peter Gabriel)
Cornerstone
fact: "Cornerstone" was the second single from Arctic Monkeys' 2009 album Humbug. Its music video was directed by Richard Ayoade, the actor/comedian known for The IT Crowd, who filmed frontman Alex Turner performing solo in a plain white room. Ayoade had already directed the band's "Crying Lightning" video from the same album, and the two later worked together again on Ayoade's 2010 film Submarine.

title: Crying Lightning
fact: "Crying Lightning" was recorded for Arctic Monkeys' 2009 album Humbug at Rancho De La Luna and Pink Duck Studios with Queens of the Stone Age's Josh Homme producing. Homme pushed the band to try guitar solos, something they'd rarely attempted before, making the track one of the clearest examples of his influence on the record.

title: Old Yellow Bricks
fact: "Old Yellow Bricks," from Arctic Monkeys' 2007 album Favourite Worst Nightmare, was co-written by Alex Turner and Jon McClure of Reverend and the Makers - old flatmates from their Sheffield days. Its title nods to The Wizard of Oz's yellow brick road, and the song closes with the winking line "Dorothy was right though."

title: 2SIDED
fact: 2SIDED is a single from Arlo Parks' third album, Ambiguous Desire (2026, Transgressive), and swaps live instruments for synths and drum machines. The album was produced by Baird, who has worked with Brockhampton, and drew on influences like The Streets, Burial and LCD Soundsystem.

title: Blades
fact: Blades is a single from Arlo Parks' second album, My Soft Machine (2023). She wrote it with producer Paul Epworth, and it has a glitterball-disco feel.

title: Heaven
fact: "Heaven" is a single from Arlo Parks' upcoming album Ambiguous Desire, a notable change of direction for the Mercury Prize-winning British singer. The song's driving bassline was inspired by an early-morning DJ set she caught from her friend, electronic artist Kelly Lee Owens, marking Parks' deepest dive yet into dance-music production.

title: Hope
fact: "Hope" was released as the final single before Arlo Parks's debut album, Collapsed in Sunbeams, arrived in January 2021 — an album that went on to win that year's Mercury Prize. The song's video was Parks's third collaboration with director Molly Burdett, following "Black Dog" and "Hurt."

title: Pegasus (feat. Phoebe Bridgers)
fact: Arlo Parks' "Pegasus," featuring Phoebe Bridgers, comes from 2023's My Soft Machine - it was produced by Paul Epworth (Adele, Florence and the Machine) alongside Brockhampton's Romil Hemnani and producer Baird.

title: Softly
fact: "Softly," released in February 2022, was Arlo Parks' first new single following her acclaimed 2021 debut album, Collapsed in Sunbeams. She co-wrote the track with veteran producer Paul Epworth, pairing its bright, upbeat-sounding production with lyrics about the fragile, bittersweet final days of a relationship.

title: Too Good
fact: "Too Good," from Arlo Parks' 2021 debut album Collapsed in Sunbeams, was written during one of her first sessions with producer Paul Epworth, known for his work with Adele and Florence + the Machine. Parks has said the track came together after she shared her eclectic influences with him, from 1970s Zambian psych-rock to MF DOOM and Tame Impala.

title: Weightless
fact: 'Weightless' was the first single from Arlo Parks's second album, My Soft Machine, co-written and produced with Paul Epworth, the British producer behind hits for Adele, Florence and the Machine, and Coldplay. Parks said she wanted the track's faster tempo and bolder synths to 'throw people off balance,' a deliberate departure from the sparser sound of her debut.

title: Senses
fact: Senses pairs Arlo Parks with Mercury Prize winner Sampha and is from her 2026 album Ambiguous Desire, her follow-up to 2023's My Soft Machine.

Punish My Mind
fact: "Punish My Mind" is the second single from Autosmile, the 2026 album on 4AD by the Philadelphia electronic-folk duo @. It pairs mellow vocal harmonies with a calm acoustic guitar and woodwind arrangement that's interrupted by a monkey screech.

title: The Symbolic Tree (Animal Crossing: New Leaf)
It's Obvious
fact: "It's Obvious" was the second single by English post-punk band Au Pairs, later included on their 1981 debut Playing with a Different Sex. The song imagines a fantasy world where gender roles simply stop mattering, built around the repeated refrain "you're equal but different."

title: Anywayz
fact: "Anywayz" opens Austra's 2020 album HiRUDiN, named after a peptide from leeches that is the most potent anticoagulant known. It was the first Austra record made with outside producers, Rodaidh McDonald and Joseph Shabason, and was recorded in the Spanish countryside.

title: Happy Birthday
fact: "Happy Birthday" is the third track on Written into Changes (March 2026, Dead Oceans), the second album from Avalon Emerson & the Charm. Emerson, a DJ, road-tested the song in club sets at places like Berlin's Panorama Bar and Brooklyn's Nowadays before its release.

title: Jupiter and Mars
fact: Avalon Emerson's "Jupiter and Mars" is credited to the full band billing Avalon Emerson & the Charm, released via Dead Oceans in 2026.

title: Written into Changes
fact: Written Into Changes is the title track of the second album of electronic indie-pop songs credited to Avalon Emerson & the Charm (2026). Emerson first became known as a DJ and dance-music producer before moving toward songwriting.

title: You're My World
fact: You're My World features Montreal artist Priori and was released in July 2025 ahead of Avalon Emerson's electronic indie-pop album Written Into Changes, credited to Avalon Emerson & the Charm.

title: Raindrops Keep Fallin' On My Head
album: Raindrops Keep Fallin' on My Head

title: Inner Space
fact: "Inner Space" was released in September 2022 and opens Babe Rainbow's The Organic Album. The Byron Bay band trades some of its laid-back feel for a jet-propelled rhythm and spacey, hazy psychedelia.

title: Waterfall
fact: "Waterfall" is a single from Babe Rainbow's seventh album, Acid and Honey (2026). The psychedelic band is from Byron Bay, New South Wales, Australia.

title: Blue Around You
album: I See Them, I See Me
fact: "Blue Around You" is a single from Babehoven's album I See Them, I See Me, the Hudson, New York-based project of Maya Bon and Ryan Albert. The track leans into fiddle-heavy, country-tinged instrumentation and was produced by Phil Weinrobe, an engineer also known for his work with Big Thief, and released through Double Double Whammy Records.

title: Sick of Spiraling
fact: Bachelor pairs Melina Duterte (who records bedroom pop as Jay Som) with Ellen Kempner of the band Palehound. The two wrote their first song together in 2018 and recorded their debut album in just two weeks at a house in Topanga, California.

title: Sailin' On
fact: "Sailin' On" first appeared on Bad Brains' 1982 self-titled debut before being re-recorded for their 1983 follow-up, Rock for Light, which was produced by The Cars' Ric Ocasek.

title: In Your Eyes (feat. Charlotte Day Wilson)
Sister of Pearl
fact: Chris Baio, bassist of Vampire Weekend, wrote "Sister of Pearl" as a Bowie- and Bryan Ferry-referencing throwback pop song for The Names, his 2015 solo debut - its message, as he put it, boils down to "be who you want to be."

title: (Biding Time Is a) Boat To Row
album: Everything All The Time - 20th Anniversary Edition
fact: This fan favorite actually started out as a hard-to-find extra on Band of Horses' 2005 Tour EP before finally getting its due on the 20th-anniversary reissue of Everything All the Time. Its music video draws on the real story of the "52-hertz whale," whose calls are pitched differently from every other whale's, as a visual metaphor for the song.

title: The General Specific
fact: "The General Specific" actually comes from Band of Horses' second album, Cease to Begin, released on Sub Pop in October 2007, rather than the band's later album Infinite Arms. It sits as track five on that record, a lo-fi, foot-stomping pop tune that showcases frontman Ben Bridwell's gentler melodic side.

title: The Great Salt Lake
fact: Band of Horses' "The Great Salt Lake," from 2006's Everything All the Time, isn't really about the Great Salt Lake at all - frontman Ben Bridwell has said the imagery mostly pulls from Lake Murray, a reservoir in his home state of South Carolina, mixed with stories about friends from Salt Lake City.

title: omni shambles
fact: "omni shambles" is a two-minute rocker from bar italia's 2025 album Some Like It Hot on Matador Records. The London trio is Nina Cristante plus Jezmi Fehmi and Sam Fenton, who also play together in the band Double Virgo.

title: Dig
fact: Barrie is led by songwriter Barrie Lindsay, who was discovered almost by accident - a fan who'd heard her music online reached out and helped assemble the rest of the Brooklyn band around her.

title: Me and You
album: I Eat Kids and Other Songs for Rebellious Children
