title: Big Love
album: Look To The East, Look To The West
fact: "Big Love" was the lead single from Camera Obscura's 2024 album Look to the East, Look to the West, the Scottish band's first new album in over a decade. The jangly, country-tinged track features pedal steel guitar from Tim Davidson, giving the Glasgow group's signature guitar-pop sound an extra twang.

title: French Navy
fact: French Navy was the first single from Camera Obscura's fourth album, My Maudlin Career, released April 13, 2009. The Glasgow band is led by singer Tracyanne Campbell.

title: Honey in the Sun
fact: "Honey in the Sun" appears on Camera Obscura's 2009 album My Maudlin Career, written by frontwoman Tracyanne Campbell. The Glasgow band reunited with producer Jari Haapalainen, who had also helmed their earlier album Let's Get Out of This Country, recording in Stockholm with string and horn arrangements by Björn Yttling of Peter Bjorn and John.

The Scottish band worked fast, cutting 15 songs in about two weeks and keeping the best 10, giving the record a live, in-the-room energy.

The Opener
fact: The Opener is the first track on Camp Cope's second album, How to Socialise & Make Friends, released March 2, 2018. The Melbourne trio's album debuted at number 6 on the Australian ARIA chart.

title: Take the Skinheads Bowling
fact: Despite its provocative title, "Take the Skinheads Bowling" is a deliberately absurdist nonsense song — frontman David Lowery and co-founder David McDaniel spent weeks riffing on implausible, meaningless lyrics specifically to undermine any "real" interpretation. The band has said the joke was in the mundane image itself: taking feared skinhead figures bowling humanizes them into just "kids in odd clothing," and the throwaway track unexpectedly became the band's signature song.

fact: "Oh Messy Life" is the second track on Cap'n Jazz's only full-length album, Shmap'n Shmazz, recorded over five days between December 27-31, 1994. The Chicago band broke up shortly after the record's 1995 release, but its chaotic, melodic style is now widely credited with helping push emo out of the punk underground and into indie rock.

album: In a Tidal Wave of Mystery

title: Beast Monster Thing (Love Isn't Love Enough)
Cute Thing
fact: "Cute Thing" was first released on Car Seat Headrest's 2011 Bandcamp album Twin Fantasy, written and recorded entirely by Will Toledo on his own as a teenager. Seven years later, Toledo re-recorded the whole album with a full band for Twin Fantasy (Face to Face), giving "Cute Thing" a fuller, more polished studio treatment.

title: Devereaux
fact: "Devereaux" is track two on Car Seat Headrest's 2025 rock opera "The Scholars," a concept album set at the fictional Parnassus University that frontman Will Toledo built in the tradition of classic story-cycle records like The Who's "Tommy" and David Bowie's "Ziggy Stardust." The track rides a chugging, propulsive rhythm into a big singalong chorus.

title: Maud Gone
fact: Car Seat Headrest's "Maud Gone," from 2015's Teens of Style, is written from the perspective of Irish poet W.B. Yeats about his real-life muse, Maud Gonne - a revolutionary he was infatuated with for years and proposed to five times, always unsuccessfully.

title: Nervous Young Inhumans
fact: "Nervous Young Inhumans" appears on Car Seat Headrest's Twin Fantasy (Face to Face). Songwriter Will Toledo has said the title nods to "galvanism," the long-obsolete scientific theory — made famous through Mary Shelley's Frankenstein — that electricity flowing through the bloodstream powers life. He used that idea as a lens for writing about creating and inhabiting characters in his songs.

title: Not Just What I Needed
fact: This Car Seat Headrest track began life as 'Just What I Needed/Not Just What I Needed,' built around an interpolation of The Cars' 1978 hit, for the 2016 album Teens of Denial. After the record's release, The Cars' Ric Ocasek withdrew permission for the sample, forcing Matador Records to pull and destroy existing vinyl copies; Will Toledo then wrote an extended, fully original replacement version of the song for the revised pressing.

title: Overexsposed (Enjoy)
fact: 'Overexposed (Enjoy)' dates back to Car Seat Headrest's prolific Bandcamp years, appearing on the 2012 self-released album Monomania when Will Toledo was still a teenager recording dozens of albums alone in his bedroom. The track actually samples another one of his own songs, 'Sober to Death,' making it an early example of Toledo remixing himself years before he ever had a real audience. It's a neat piece of trivia for a songwriter who'd reach indie rock prominence a few years later with Teens of Denial.

title: Sober To Death
fact: Car Seat Headrest's "Sober to Death" is track four on Twin Fantasy - one of only three songs on the album that Will Toledo left lyrically untouched when he re-recorded the whole record from scratch for its 2018 re-release.

title: Stop Smoking
fact: Car Seat Headrest gets its name from Will Toledo's early recording setup - at 17, he'd record vocals sitting in his family's parked car for privacy and soundproofing. He self-released 12 albums on Bandcamp before signing to Matador Records.

title: The Catastrophe (Good Luck With That  Man)
fact: "The Catastrophe (Good Luck With That, Man)" was the third single from Car Seat Headrest's 2025 rock opera "The Scholars." Written from the perspective of several members of a fictional band, the five-and-a-half-minute power-pop track mixes acoustic and distorted guitars and packs in references ranging from the Roman Empire to the Old Testament to the Edsels' doo-wop hit "Rama Lama Ding Dong."

title: Vincent
fact: "Vincent" is the sprawling, nearly eight-minute second track on Car Seat Headrest's 2016 album "Teens of Denial," recorded at Soundhouse studio in Seattle with producer Steve Fisk, known for earlier work with Nirvana, Beat Happening, and Soundgarden. It was released as an advance single in February 2016, months ahead of the full album.

title: War Is Coming (If You Want It)
We Can't Afford (Your Depression Anymore)
fact: This song comes from Nervous Young Man, the sprawling two-hour double album Will Toledo self-released on Bandcamp in August 2013 under the name Car Seat Headrest, subtitled as "a collection of songs written between ages 17 and 21." It was Toledo's last release as a purely solo, self-recorded project before he assembled a full band and signed to Matador Records in 2015. A few of its songs, and the album's title, were reworked from an even earlier high school recording project called Nervous Young Men.

title: Climbing
fact: Climbing, from Caribou's 2024 album Honey (Merge and City Slang), samples Just Friends by the duo Rene & Angela from 1981. The track leans into playful disco-funk with glittering synth arpeggios.

title: Home
fact: Caribou's 2019 single "Home" is built around a sample of the song "Home" by Gloria Barnes, an obscure soul singer who released just one album, in 1971, before disappearing from the music industry. Dan Snaith found the track on YouTube and let the sample sit on his hard drive for over a year before finishing the song.

title: Odessa
fact: Dan Snaith's wife gave him swimming lessons as a Christmas gift a few years before making 2010's Swim, and that new hobby directly shaped the album's sound - he wanted the music to feel like water, full of waves flowing through the mix. 'Odessa,' the album's opener and first single, emerged from roughly 600 ideas Snaith worked through before settling on the final nine tracks.

title: Volume
fact: Volume, from Caribou's 2024 album Honey, samples the 1987 dance hit Pump Up the Volume by MARRS. Dan Snaith, who records as Caribou, released it as a single on July 31, 2024, ahead of the album's October 4 release.

title: You Can Do It
fact: Caribou's "You Can Do It" is built around a chopped-up, delirious vocal sample of its own title - Dan Snaith released it as a surprise one-off single after 2020's Suddenly, paired with a music video that's just dogs happily chasing frisbees through scenic landscapes. It earned a Grammy nomination for Best Dance Recording.

Dark blue
fact: "Dark Blue" opens the self-titled 2022 debut album by the London band caroline and was actually the very first song the group wrote together after forming in 2017. Built around one hypnotic, repeating guitar figure played by the eight-piece band, the track was first released as a single in 2020 before being reworked into the album version.

title: Tell me I never knew that (ft. Caroline Polachek)
fact: "Tell me I never knew that" pairs the eight-piece London band caroline with singer Caroline Polachek, who contributed production and songwriting to the track. The band has said they nicknamed the song "Backstreet Boys" during writing sessions because its catchy opening melody, built around a riff from bandmate Casper, reminded them of the boy band's sound.

title: Total euphoria
fact: "Total euphoria" was the London seven-piece caroline's first new song in three years when it arrived in March 2025 via Rough Trade, later appearing on their second album, Caroline 2. The track actually began as early as 2020, when members Mike, Casper, and Jasper played a rough version as a three-piece while writing their debut album; Jasper later built out the chords and topline before the full band layered in strings, brass, and interlocking guitar parts.

title: Blood and Butter
album: Desire, I Want To Turn Into You
fact: "Blood and Butter," from Caroline Polachek's 2023 album Desire, I Want to Turn Into You, features a bagpipe solo by Scottish musician Brighde Chaimbeul, whom Polachek approached specifically to contribute to the Danny L. Harle co-produced track. Chaimbeul later joined Polachek onstage to perform the bagpipe break live.

fact: Caroline Polachek originally wrote 'Welcome to My Island' during sessions for her 2019 album Pang but shelved it, feeling it was 'too bratty.' She revisited and finished it for 2023's Desire, I Want to Turn Into You, opening the song with an operatically trained scream and calling it the 'brattiest song' she's ever made.

title: Yip Yip Yow
fact: Caroline Rose wrote Yip Yip Yow about ten years ago and played it live for years before releasing a studio version on May 12, 2026, on a label Rose launched for the occasion. John Congleton produced it, Carla Azar played the live drums, and Zac Rae of Death Cab for Cutie played bass.

title: Lingua Franca
fact: Casper Skulls formed in 2015 when Toronto-based musicians (and partners) Neil Bednis and Melanie St-Pierre started writing together. "Lingua Franca" itself earned the band a SOCAN Songwriting Prize nomination in 2018.

Sacred Heart
fact: Cass McCombs is one of indie rock's most prolific songwriters, now well past ten albums, and has collaborated with artists including John Cale, Ariel Pink, and The Decemberists. He's also published a poetry collection and made a children's album with a San Francisco schoolteacher.

title: American Spirits
album: (An Overview on) An Overview on Phenomenal Nature

title: Hard Drive
fact: "Hard Drive" is a spoken-word centerpiece of Cassandra Jenkins' 2021 album An Overview on Phenomenal Nature, built around her recollections of brief encounters with strangers like a museum security guard, a bookmaker, and a driving instructor. One of those exchanges, a museum guard's offhand promise to give her the "overview" of an exhibit, ended up giving the whole album its title. Producer and guitarist Josh Kaufman and saxophonist Stuart Bogie fill out the track's hushed, looping arrangement.

title: Only One
fact: Only One was the lead single from Cassandra Jenkins' 2024 album My Light, My Destroyer. She wrote it with Stephanie Marziano, and it was inspired by a Groundhog Day feeling of repeating the same situation over and over.

title: Manhattan
fact: Cat Power is Chan Marshall, who named the project after a trucker cap reading "Cat Diesel Power" that she spotted while working at a pizza shop. She was discovered opening for Liz Phair in 1994 by Sonic Youth's Steve Shelley, and has since influenced artists like Mitski, Snail Mail, and Angel Olsen.

title: Metal Heart
fact: "Metal Heart" is a standout track from Cat Power's fourth album, Moon Pix (1998). Chan Marshall wrote much of the record in a short burst after a strange, unsettling night at a rural South Carolina farmhouse, then traveled to Melbourne, Australia, to record it with Mick Turner and Jim White of the band Dirty Three.

title: Werewolf
fact: Cat Power's 'Werewolf,' from her 2003 album You Are Free, is a cover of 'The Werewolf Song' by folk singer Michael Hurley, originally released on his 1964 debut, First Songs. Cat Power's version helped introduce a new generation of listeners, including fellow freak-folk artists, to Hurley's decades-spanning catalog.

title: (Remember the Days of the) Old Schoolyard
If You Want to Sing Out, Sing Out

Always The Same (Ft. St. Vincent)
fact: Always the Same was written during the sessions for Cate Le Bon's 2025 album Michelangelo Dying and released in January 2026 as a cousin to it. It reunited her with St. Vincent, whom she'd worked with on St. Vincent's 2024 album All Born Screaming.

title: Home to You
fact: Cate Le Bon's "Home to You," a 2019 single from her album Reward, came out of a year she spent almost entirely off the road, taking a daily furniture-making course in England's Lake District - by day she learned dovetail joints, and by night she wrote the songs that became the album.

title: Is It Worth It (Happy Birthday)?
fact: "Is It Worth It (Happy Birthday)?" is the sprawling, six-minute centerpiece of Cate Le Bon's seventh album, Michelangelo Dying (2025), which she produced herself alongside Samur Khouja. The track layers fluorescent synths and dazed guitar with saxophone from Euan Hinshelwood, piano from Paul Jones, and percussion from Dylan Hadley and Valentina Magaletti.

artist: Cate Le Bon feat. John Cale
title: Ride
fact: 'Ride' appears on Cate Le Bon's 2025 album Michelangelo Dying and features a guest vocal turn from John Cale, the Welsh musician and founding member of The Velvet Underground. The hypnotic, interlocking vocal performance between the two is considered one of the album's most striking moments, a notable pairing of two generations of Welsh experimental songwriting.

title: Bruises
fact: Chairlift recorded Bruises in keyboardist Patrick Wimberly's Brooklyn basement during all-night sessions after scrapping an earlier, more polished studio version they weren't happy with. The stripped-down version ended up being chosen by Apple to soundtrack a 2008 iPod Nano commercial, turning the then-unknown band into a sudden commercial breakout. It remains the trio's best-charting single.

title: I Belong In Your Arms
fact: Chairlift's "I Belong in Your Arms," from 2012's Something, was written by the duo of Caroline Polachek and Patrick Wimberly, who formed the band in Boulder, Colorado in 2005. Decades later, the '80s-influenced synthpop song found a whole new audience soundtracking the closing scene of the TV series Heartstopper.

artist: Chance the Rapper feat. Lil Wayne & 2 Chainz

fact: "Growth Sux" is a standalone single the Los Angeles trio Cheekface released in January 2025. It's built around a drum machine, marking the first time the band - Greg Katz, Amanda Tannen, and Mark Edwards - centered a song on programmed rather than live drums.

title: Hostile Street
fact: Cheekface's 2026 single "Hostile Street" was produced and mixed by Eric Palmquist at his Los Angeles studio and mastered by David Kutch. The track opens with real dog barks from bassist Amanda Tannen's dog Stubbs and includes a guest vocal sample from rapper McKinley Dixon.

title: I Don't Work Here
fact: I Don't Work Here is a 2026 single from Cheekface's sixth album, Podium. It was recorded at Palmquist Studios in Los Angeles with producer Eric Palmquist, and the video was shot in a grocery store.

title: Life in a Bag
fact: Cheekface's "Life in a Bag," from 2024's It's Sorted, was written by all three band members - Amanda Tannen, Greg Katz, and Mark Edwards - and produced by longtime collaborator Greg Cortez.

title: MFT
fact: "MFT" is the third single from Cheekface's 2026 album Podium. True to the deadpan L.A. trio's style, the title is a dry acronym play on "MFT" — shorthand for Marriage and Family Therapist. Formed in 2017, the band pairs Greg Katz's talky lead vocals with Amanda Tannen on bass and Mark Edwards on drums.

title: No Fly Zone
fact: "No Fly Zone" was the final pre-release single from Cheekface's 2026 album Podium (July 2026). The trio is Greg Katz, bassist Amanda Tannen (formerly of stellastarr*), and drummer Mark Edwards, and the track features horn arrangements by Jer Hunter and Emily Williams of Against All Authority.

title: Plastic
fact: Cheekface's "Plastic" started out as a much bongo-heavier demo before "cooler heads prevailed," according to frontman Greg Katz, who's described the song as being about "being an implacable people pleaser and the miracle of 3D printing."

title: Popular 2
fact: 'Popular 2' is a deadpan, upbeat single off Cheekface's 2024 album It's Sorted, built around the very modern itch to be noticed in a neighborhood full of doorbell cameras and porch security feeds. Frontman Greg Katz has described the album's running idea as the tug-of-war between wanting to belong to a community and wanting to stand out as an individual. It's classic Cheekface: a weird, hyper-specific observation turned into a genuinely catchy chorus.

title: The Fringe
fact: "The Fringe" opens Cheekface's 2022 album It's Sorted with the band's signature deadpan, sing-speak style. The lyrics playfully reference musique concrete, avant-garde sculpture, and skeptical art critics, poking fun at the pursuit of being seen as artistically unconventional.

title: There Is A God
fact: "There Is A God" opens Cheekface's 2026 album "Podium." True to the LA trio's deadpan, wordplay-heavy style, singer Greg Katz builds the song's title around a slant rhyme, landing on "Erewhon" (the LA grocery chain) paired with "there is a God."

title: We Need a Bigger Dumpster
fact: Cheekface's "We Need a Bigger Dumpster" pairs chipper pop-rock with singer Greg Katz's deadpan, non-sequitur-filled delivery - the Los Angeles trio (Katz, bassist Amanda Tannen, and drummer Mark "Echo" Edwards) built its whole style around that mismatch between upbeat music and wry, anxious lyrics.

fact: Cherry Glazerr's 'Big Bang' pairs a heavy emotional subject - the long, drawn-out end of a relationship - with deliberately euphoric production. Frontwoman Clementine Creevy said she wanted an early-2000s pop feel, blending acoustic guitar with bass synths and 808 hits, citing DJ Koze, Caribou, Yaeji, and Kaytranada as touchstones. The result turns heartache into something danceable rather than heavy.

title: Grilled Cheese
fact: Cherry Glazerr's “Grilled Cheese” is exactly what it sounds like - a whimsical garage-pop song about grilled cheese sandwiches, written when the band members were still in high school.

title: Had Ten Dollaz
fact: "Had Ten Dollaz" was the title track of a self-released, two-song digital EP Cherry Glazerr put out in 2014, while the band was still just starting out in Los Angeles. The EP's other song, "Nurse Ratched," was later re-recorded and included on the band's 2017 major-label debut album, Apocalipstick.

title: Ready For You
fact: "Ready For You" appears on Cherry Glazerr's 2023 album "I Don't Want You Anymore," built around a big, staticky guitar riff that leans into the record's harder rock sound. The band shot the song's music video, directed by Sarah Ritter, in the Joshua Tree desert using an old car and motel room, performing part of it inside a moving U-Haul truck in 118-degree heat.

title: Told You I'd Be With The Guys
fact: "Told You I'd Be With The Guys" opens Cherry Glazerr's 2017 album Apocalipstick, the band's major-label debut, and was written by frontwoman Clementine Creevy. The album was produced by Joe Chiccarelli and Carlos de la Garza, who polished up the band's garage-rock sound, with keyboardist Sasami Ashworth (later known as solo artist SASAMI) and drummer Tabor Allen rounding out the lineup.

title: Beanie
fact: When "Beanie" dropped in late 2023, Chezile was essentially homeless and facing serious financial struggles; then the song took off on Spotify and TikTok's global viral charts and turned him into a name everyone suddenly knew. Despite the title, the word "beanie" never actually appears anywhere in the lyrics. Chezile wrote and produced the track himself, building it around a sampled loop under his own dreamy, bedroom-pop production.

title: Bluebeard
fact: "Bluebeard," the second single from Cocteau Twins' 1993 album Four-Calendar Café, marked a notable turning point for singer Elizabeth Fraser: after years of singing largely wordless "mouth music," her vocals on this track became far more intelligible and lyric-driven than on the band's earlier dream-pop releases. It remains one of the clearest examples of the group's evolving vocal approach in the early '90s.

title: Crushed
fact: Cocteau Twins' "Crushed" was made for 4AD's 1987 various-artists compilation Lonely Is an Eyesore - like much of the band's catalog, Elizabeth Fraser's lyrics are deliberately abstract and largely untranslatable, prized more for their sound than any literal meaning.

title: Heaven or Las Vegas
fact: Cocteau Twins were famous for eccentric, invented-sounding song titles, and "Heaven or Las Vegas" was no exception — its working title in the studio was the nonsense phrase "Crispy Fiver Blue." The eventual title track ended up lending its name to the band's acclaimed 1990 album, after musician Lawrence of the band Denim/Felt suggested the phrase from the lyrics as the record's title.

title: Love's Easy Tears
fact: "Love's Easy Tears" was the title track of a 1986 EP released on 4AD -- the band's eighth EP overall and their last for that label until 1993. It marked Cocteau Twins' first full-trio recording without outside guests in some time, with bassist Simon Raymonde and guitarist Robin Guthrie crafting one of Guthrie's signature crystalline feedback washes for the chorus.

title: Sugar Hiccup
fact: "Sugar Hiccup" appeared on both Cocteau Twins' 1983 album Head over Heels and the companion EP Sunburst and Snowblind, released that same year on 4AD. It's notable within the band's catalog for having actual discernible English lyrics, unlike much of their famously abstract vocal style, and it ranked 14th on John Peel's 1983 Festive Fifty countdown.

The Seattle trio worked with engineer Nich Wilbur to make their three-piece setup sound as lush and full as possible.

Clarke says the song plays with pairs of opposites, mixing city and suburban imagery with ideas about public versus private selves. Musically it leans on jangly, heartache-laced guitars in the vein of The Replacements before dissolving into accordion and the sound of city sirens.

Tweedy made the offer after Cut Worms opened for Wilco on tour, and the resulting track channels the melodic urgency of power-pop forebears like Big Star. It's a full-circle moment for a songwriter who grew up on exactly that kind of jangly guitar pop.

Tweedy plays electric guitars and bass on the song and Wilco drummer Glenn Kotche adds percussion, after the band toured with Wilco in 2024.

Great Mass of Color
fact: Deafheaven's "Great Mass of Color" introduced 2021's Infinite Granite, an album that traded much of the band's earlier black-metal roar for shoegaze and clean vocals - it was produced by Justin Meldal-Johnsen (M83, Paramore, Wolf Alice) and mixed by Darrell Thorp, known for his work with Radiohead and Beck.

title: Shellstar
fact: "Shellstar" opens Deafheaven's 2021 album "Infinite Granite," the record on which the blackgaze band shifted toward shoegaze and dream pop, with vocalist George Clarke singing in a clean falsetto for the first time. The track moves from serene, bell-like guitar tones and choral backing vocals into a layered, wall-of-sound finale built on '90s alt-metal drum patterns.

title: Before You Hit the Ground
album: I Hope We Can Still Be Friends
fact: "Before You Hit the Ground" was the lead single from Seattle songwriter Dean Johnson's 2025 sophomore album, I Hope We Can Still Be Friends, released on Saddle Creek Records. The album was produced by fellow Pacific Northwest musician Sera Cahoone, following up Johnson's 2023 debut, Nothing For Me, Please.

title: Death of the Party
album: I Hope We Can Still Be Friends
fact: "Death of the Party" is a single from singer-songwriter Dean Johnson's 2025 debut album for Saddle Creek Records, I Hope We Can Still Be Friends. The wry, wordy track skewers "energy vampires" - the exhausting motormouths who trap you in one-sided conversations at parties - set against brushed drums, bright acoustic strumming, and warm keys. Johnson spent years as a bartender before his music career took off, and the song draws on that experience of people-watching from behind the bar.

Pep Talk
fact: "Pep Talk" is track three on Death Cab for Cutie's 2025 album I Built You a Tower, the band's 11th studio album and first release on ANTI- Records after two decades on Atlantic. The record was produced by John Congleton and is the group's first full-length of new material since 2022's Asphalt Meadows.

title: Punching The Flowers
fact: Punching the Flowers is from Death Cab for Cutie's eleventh album, I Built You a Tower (June 2026). It followed the singles Riptides and preceded Stone Over Water, and the album has a heavier rock feel than their recent records.

title: Riptides
fact: "Riptides" was the first single from Death Cab for Cutie's eleventh album, I Built You a Tower (June 2026, Anti- Records). It was released in March 2026 and is track nine on the album.

title: Stone Over Water
fact: "Stone Over Water" is a 2026 single from Death Cab for Cutie's album I Built You a Tower, written by frontman Ben Gibbard. The record was produced by John Congleton and pieced together partly at Animal Rites studio in Los Angeles, with additional sessions recorded at band members' own homes in Seattle, Bellingham, Los Angeles, and Portland.

Billboard Heart
fact: Jessica Dobson wrote the title track of 2024's Billboard Heart after a songwriting session with bandmate (and husband) Peter Mansen hit a wall and the two started bickering; once he stepped out, she kept playing and the song took shape. Dobson has cited the simplicity of Tom Petty's songwriting and the mood of Wim Wenders' film Paris, Texas as inspirations for the track.

title: Shovel
fact: "Shovel" is a single by Seattle indie-rock band Deep Sea Diver, led by singer-guitarist Jessica Dobson, from their 2025 album Billboard Heart on Sub Pop Records. The song blends grunge grit with synth-pop, and its one-shot music video, co-directed by Dobson, was inspired by David Lynch, the Coen brothers, Nick Cave, and Kate Bush's dance moves.

title: Teardrop
fact: This is Deep Sea Diver's cover of Massive Attack's "Teardrop," the 1998 single from the album Mezzanine that featured Elizabeth Fraser of Cocteau Twins. The Seattle band released it in July 2026, produced by singer-guitarist Jessica Dobson and drummer Peter Mansen at their High Beam Studio, and Dobson says the original stopped her in her tracks as a kid.

title: The Dream's In The Ditch
fact: Deer Tick got its name from a real deer tick - frontman John McCauley found one on his scalp during a camping trip, panicked for a bit, then decided it made a good band name once he calmed down.

title: Your Dystopic Creation Doesn't Fear You
Memory Boy
fact: Deerhunter's "Memory Boy" comes from 2010's Halcyon Digest, an album frontman Bradford Cox has described as noise rock colliding with baroque pop - it was released as a single paired with "Nosebleed" the following year.

title: Nothing Ever Happened
fact: The lead single from Deerhunter's 2008 album Microcastle, this nearly six-minute track stretches into an extended, motorik groove clearly inspired by the German band Neu! It marked a shift toward a more accessible, guitar-driven rock sound compared to the hazier Cryptograms. The song is widely regarded as the album's centerpiece.

title: Have You Ever Needed Someone So Bad
Dog Days
fact: Dehd is a Chicago trio formed in 2015 by Jason Balla and Emily Kempf, who brought in friend Eric McGrady on drums; the band is known for its stripped-down, reverb-soaked pop sound. The one-take music video for "Dog Days," the opening track from their 2024 album Poetry, was filmed in a single unedited shot inside Bernice's Tavern in Chicago.

title: Light On
fact: Light On is the second single from Poetry, the fifth album from Chicago trio Dehd (May 10, 2024, Fat Possum). Ziyad Asrar of Whitney co-produced it with Jason Balla, recording at Palisade Studios in Chicago.

title: Black Celebration
fact: Depeche Mode's title track "Black Celebration" opens their 1986 album of the same name - the band built its unique sound entirely from their own samples rather than outside sources, and at one point considered sampling a Winston Churchill speech before scrapping the idea. Engineers later said they could barely remember how they'd made some of the sounds when they went back to remaster it in 2006.

title: Blue Eyes
fact: Destroyer's "Blue Eyes," from 2011's Kaputt, is one of the album's more overtly poetic detours - Dan Bejar repeats the line "I write poetry for myself" over the record's blend of synth-pop, soft rock, and mellow jazz.

title: Bologna (feat. Fiver)
fact: "Bologna" features Simone Schmidt of the band Fiver on co-lead vocals, and Dan Bejar has said it's the first Destroyer song where he cast himself as a supporting character while Schmidt's part drives the narrative. It's the lead single from Destroyer's 2025 album Dan's Boogie, with a video directed by David Galloway starring Bejar and Schmidt.

title: Chinatown
fact: "Chinatown" opens Destroyer's 2011 album Kaputt, recorded over roughly two years by Dan Bejar with producers John Collins and David Carswell at their JC/DC studio in Vancouver. The track's warm, sax-and-trumpet-soaked sound (trumpet courtesy of JP Carter) marked a dramatic left turn from Destroyer's earlier guitar-rock records toward a smoky, late-night jazz-pop feel reminiscent of Roxy Music. The song became many critics' entry point into the album, which was widely named one of the best records of 2011.

title: Cover From the Sun
fact: "Cover from the Sun" is track four on Destroyer's 2017 album ken. Unlike the full-band approach of its predecessor, Poison Season, ken was produced by the band's own drummer, Josh Wells (also of Black Mountain), and recorded in a rehearsal space nicknamed the Balloon Factory. Dan Bejar still brought in bandmates for guest appearances throughout the sessions.

title: Cue Synthesizer
fact: For Destroyer's 2020 album Have We Met, Dan Bejar recorded all his vocals alone at night at his kitchen table, singing into a laptop microphone, then sent the files to longtime collaborator John Collins in Seattle to build the music around them. On "Cue Synthesizer," Bejar literally narrates the arrangement into being, calling out cues like "cue synthesizer" as if directing the song from the booth.

title: Dream Lover
fact: "Dream Lover" was the lead single from Destroyer's 2015 album Poison Season. Dan Bejar built the track as a deliberate homage to Bruce Springsteen's "Born to Run" era, complete with a saxophone line that echoes Clarence Clemons, before the song eventually dissolves into a squall of noise.

title: Eat the Wine, Drink the Bread
El Rito
fact: 'El Rito' is Destroyer's cover of a song by Spanish songwriter Antonio Luque of the band Sr. Chinarro, featured on the 2013 EP Five Spanish Songs. Dan Bejar said the original was one of Luque's most traditional flamenco-style songs, so he deliberately reworked it into a glammy, four-on-the-floor rock arrangement with fuzz guitar instead.

title: Hydroplaning Off The Edge Of The World
fact: "Hydroplaning Off the Edge of the World" was the second single from Destroyer's 2025 album Dan's Boogie, the band's fourteenth studio record, produced by longtime collaborator John Collins. Across the album's nine songs, frontman Dan Bejar plays with characters like a lounge singer and a hustler.

title: June
fact: Destroyer's "June" arrived as a single from 2022's Labyrinthitis, and its video took the step-by-step "process video" format somewhere strange: it's a tutorial on making a burrito, which then gets delivered to frontman Dan Bejar by a figure in a full metallic suit. Bejar co-directed the clip himself with David Galloway. He's also said the song's sprawling back half includes passages that would never have made it onto earlier Destroyer records.

title: Kaputt
fact: The title track of Destroyer's 2011 breakout album Kaputt, written by Dan Bejar, name-checks a run of real British music magazines in its lyrics -- "Sounds, Smash Hits, Melody Maker, NME" -- as part of its hazy, sophisti-pop meditation on the music press. The Merge Records album became the project's most critically celebrated release to date.

title: Savage Night At The Opera
fact: Destroyer's "Savage Night at the Opera," from 2011's Kaputt, rides the same smooth, sax-and-synth "yacht rock" sound Dan Bejar built across the whole album while obsessing over Roxy Music's Avalon - Kaputt went on to become the unexpected commercial peak of his career.

title: Times Square
fact: "Times Square" comes from Dan Bejar's 2015 Destroyer album Poison Season, where the song is so central to the record's structure that it's split into three separate parts, with two versions bookending the album and a third placed at its center. It was released as the album's lead single in August 2015.

title: Tinseltown Swimming In Blood
fact: Despite its dark-sounding title, "Tinseltown Swimming in Blood" is Dan Bejar's gauzy, synth-driven satire of Hollywood's manufactured glamour, built on the dreamy, '80s-influenced production that defines Destroyer's 2017 album ken. The track closes with Bejar repeating the line "I was a dreamer, watch me leave," a wink at making it as a musician on his own terms. Destroyer performed the song live in the studio for NPR shortly after the album came out.

title: (I Can't Get No) Satisfaction
album: Q: Are We Not Men? A: We Are Devo!
fact: DEVO's herky-jerky remake of the Rolling Stones' Satisfaction was their 1977 second single. Because their label worried about permission, Gerald Casale and Mark Mothersbaugh flew to New York to play it for Mick Jagger, who approved. Brian Eno produced their 1978 debut album.

title: Gates of Steel
fact: "Gates of Steel" began as an instrumental demo Mark Mothersbaugh recorded with Debbie Smith and Sue Schmidt of the band Chi-Pig, before Gerald Casale added lyrics he'd written separately. It was released as a single on October 6, 1980 from DEVO's album Freedom of Choice.

title: Girl U Want
fact: Girl U Want was the first single from DEVO's third album, Freedom of Choice (1980), which was produced by Bob Margouleff and also included Whip It. Mark Mothersbaugh and Gerald Casale, who founded the band in Akron, Ohio, wrote it.

title: Gut Feeling / (Slap Your Mammy)
album: Q: Are We Not Men? A: We Are Devo!

title: Jocko Homo
album: Q: Are We Not Men? A: We Are Devo!
fact: DEVO's 'Jocko Homo' takes its title from a 1924 anti-evolution pamphlet called 'Jocko-Homo Heavenbound,' which fit the band's running concept of 'de-evolution.' Its famous call-and-response chorus, 'Are we not men? We are Devo!,' is a direct reference to a line from the 1932 film Island of Lost Souls, itself based on H.G. Wells' novel The Island of Doctor Moreau.

title: Mongoloid
album: Q: Are We Not Men? A: We Are Devo!

title: Out of Sync
fact: DEVO's "Out of Sync," from 1982's Oh, No! It's DEVO, was written by Mark Mothersbaugh and Gerald Casale and built around a riff that nods to The Kinks' "You Really Got Me."

title: S.I.B. (Swelling Itching Brain)
fact: "S.I.B. (Swelling Itching Brain)" is track seven on DEVO's 1979 sophomore album Duty Now for the Future. It's one of several songs on the record where the band leaned further into blending synthesizers with guitar, a sonic shift that helped pave the way toward their more keyboard-driven, new-wave sound of the early 1980s.

title: Uncontrollable Urge
album: Q: Are We Not Men? A: We Are Devo!
fact: "Uncontrollable Urge," the opening track on DEVO's 1978 debut Q: Are We Not Men? A: We Are Devo!, was written and sung by keyboardist Mark Mothersbaugh and plays as a knowing homage to the Beatles, sharing a chord progression with "I Want to Hold Your Hand" and echoing the "yeah yeah yeah"s of "She Loves You." Mothersbaugh has also said John Lennon caught DEVO performing the song live at Max's Kansas City in New York in 1977, before it was officially released.

fact: Everyone Out is the sixth track on DIIV's 2024 album Frog in Boiling Water. It swaps their usual guitar wash for acoustic guitar, layered tape loops and synthesizers, in a sound some critics compared to early Smashing Pumpkins.

title: Kid
fact: DIIV's "Kid" comes from 2012's Oshin, the band's shoegaze-leaning debut - frontman Zachary Cole Smith has said Malian guitarist Baba Salah's record Borey shaped how he approached melody on the album.

title: The Fountain
fact: "The Fountain" introduced DIIV's 2026 album ZIRP!, produced by A.G. Cook, best known for his work with Charli XCX and Caroline Polachek. Cook originally planned to chop up and rebuild the band's demos, but he scrapped that approach once he got obsessed with DIIV's live sound, insisting on tracking real drums before some songs were even finished. The result keeps DIIV's hazy, guitar-driven signature while pushing the production in a sharper direction.

title: Trillions
fact: "Trillions" is a single from DIIV's fifth album, ZIRP!, released via Fantasy Recordings in 2026. The album's title refers to "zero interest rate policies," the economic backdrop the band says shaped a culture of financial speculation and startup excess over the past decade. The track continues DIIV's collaboration with producer A. G. Cook, known for his work with Charli XCX and Caroline Polachek, and is among the most overtly pop-leaning songs the band has released.

title: Blowin' Up
fact: "Blowin' Up" comes from Dinosaur Jr.'s 2026 album There Near and is notably written and sung by bassist Lou Barlow rather than frontman J Mascis, a rarity for a Dinosaur Jr. single. The album was recorded almost entirely by the trio themselves at Amherst's Bisquiteen Studio, with local musician Ken Mauri contributing extra piano and organ.

title: In a Jar
fact: In a Jar is from Dinosaur Jr.'s 1987 album You're Living All Over Me. Lou Barlow's distorted, chunky bass is a huge part of the song, and J Mascis played it when the band later revisited their 1988 album Bug live.

title: Several Got Away
fact: This one marked Dinosaur Jr.'s return with their classic three-piece lineup — J Mascis, Lou Barlow and Murph — recording in short, intense bursts over about a year at a home studio in Amherst. It's the lead single off There Near, their first full album in five years.

title: Watch The Corners
fact: "Watch the Corners" was released as the lead single from Dinosaur Jr.'s tenth studio album, I Bet on Sky, which came out in September 2012. The band gave the track away as a free download alongside its music video to introduce fans to the record ahead of release.

title: That's A Lifestyle
fact: Dirty Projectors' "That's a Lifestyle," from 2018's Lamp Lit Prose, features guest vocals from HAIM - the song's sound recalls the band's earlier Bitte Orca era, with acoustic 12-string guitar bursting into distorted electric squalls.

Decades later, their unreleased original recordings are finally surfacing through a series of archival single releases.

title: Black And White Town
fact: 'Black and White Town' was the lead single from Doves' 2005 album Some Cities, giving the Manchester-area band their second UK top-10 hit, peaking at No. 6. Frontman Jimi Goodwin has described its loose theme as cities changing over time - old, loved buildings torn down and replaced by generic new developments. It captures a restless feeling tied to watching a hometown's character disappear.

The song eases from bluesy sludge into a more stately arrangement as it closes.

title: Cruise Ship Designer
fact: "Cruise Ship Designer" was the second track revealed from Dry Cleaning's Cate Le Bon-produced 2026 album "Secret Love." Vocalist Florence Shaw says the song follows a well-paid, skilled cruise-ship and hotel designer who privately doubts his work has any real worth, but throws himself into the job's challenges anyway.

title: Joy
fact: Joy closes Dry Cleaning's third album, Secret Love (4AD, January 2026), which was produced by Welsh musician Cate Le Bon. The band made demos at Wilco's studio, The Loft, in Chicago, then re-recorded the album at Black Box Studios in France's Loire Valley.

title: Deleted Scenes
fact: Toronto duo Tom McGreevy and Evan Lewis originally performed as "Ducks Unlimited," but shortened their name to Ducks Ltd. in 2021 to avoid any legal tangle with the real-life wetlands conservation group of the same name. "Deleted Scenes" comes from the duo's 2024 album Harm's Way, released on Carpark Records.

title: Train Full of Gasoline
fact: Train Full of Gasoline is track 4 on Harm's Way, the 2024 album from Ducks Ltd. on Carpark Records. Backing vocals come from Julia Steiner of Ratboys and Margaret McCarthy of Moontype, and Ratboys' Marcus Nuccio plays drums.

title: Under The Rolling Moon
fact: Ducks Ltd.'s "Under the Rolling Moon," from their 2021 debut album Modern Fiction, features backing harmonies from members of the New Zealand band The Beths - bandmember Tom McGreevy has said the song is about trying to be there for a friend going through a hard time.

title: Just Say No!
fact: "Just Say No!" is the second track on British singer-songwriter Eaves Wilder's 2026 debut album, Little Miss Sunshine, released via Secretly Canadian. Wilder's sound on the record blends airy, ethereal vocals with fuzzed-out, shoegaze-adjacent guitars.

title: Come Alive
fact: Ebbb's "Come Alive" opens the British trio's debut album Shallow Hits (2026) - a calypso-tinged burst of electronic pop that blends synth textures with live drumming.

title: Obrigado
fact: "Obrigado" closes Ed O'Brien's 2026 album Blue Morpho, his first release under his own name after his 2020 debut Earth, which came out under the moniker EOB. The nearly ten-minute closer travels from a sunny, Balearic-tinged opening through a chillwave midsection into a proggy, Pink Floyd-style guitar finale.

title: I Like Birds
fact: "I Like Birds" appears on Eels' 2001 album Souljacker, released on DreamWorks Records. The track pairs close-harmony backing vocals and a chirpy whistled hook with grumbling lyrics about "mean little people," a wry contrast that makes it one of the record's most purely buoyant, playful moments despite frontman E's often downbeat songwriting reputation.

title: Last Stop: This Town
fact: "Last Stop: This Town" is a single from Eels' 1998 album Electro-Shock Blues, co-written and co-produced by frontman E with Michael Simpson of the Dust Brothers. Its offbeat music video, directed by Garth Jennings' company Hammer & Tongs and featuring vegetables strewn around the set, earned a Breakthrough Video nomination at the 1999 MTV Video Music Awards. The single reached number 23 on the UK charts.

title: devorah
fact: Devorah is a six-minute song from Ekko Astral's debut album, pink balloons (April 17, 2024, Topshelf Records). The Washington, D.C. post-punk band's video for it was made by Kate the Cursed.

Stutter
fact: Elastica's debut single "Stutter" sold out its limited 1,500-copy pressing in a single day and shot to #1 on the UK indie charts - on the strength of just that one single and a couple of gigs, the band was voted Best New Band in Melody Maker's year-end readers' poll.

title: Asleep In The Back
fact: "Asleep in the Back" became Elbow's first UK Top 20 single, and oddly wasn't on the original 2001 release of the album of the same name -- it was written and added only after the record was already finished, then included as a bonus track on later pressings. Singer Guy Garvey called it "sonically one of the most interesting" tracks the band made with producer Ben Hillier, and Australian band Gang of Youths later covered it for their 2021 EP Total Serene.

title: Station Approach
fact: "Station Approach" comes from Elbow's 2005 album Leaders of the Free World and is a love letter to the band's hometown of Manchester, describing the rush of familiarity felt walking the road toward the city's Piccadilly train station after time away. It has become a fan-favorite live staple for exactly that homecoming feeling.

fact: "Ballad of Big Nothing" is from Elliott Smith's third album, Either/Or (February 1997, Kill Rock Stars). It was recorded mostly in Portland, Oregon while Smith was still a member of the band Heatmiser, and was produced by Smith with Tom Rothrock and Rob Schnapf.

title: Bled White
fact: 'Bled White' is track seven on Elliott Smith's 1998 album XO, his first release on a major label (DreamWorks) after years on indie Kill Rock Stars. Drummer Joey Waronker, known for his work with R.E.M. and Beck, played on the track. The song nods to Smith's adopted hometown of Portland, Oregon, and it was later covered by the UK band Yuck.

title: Coming Up Roses
fact: "Coming Up Roses" is the sixth track on Elliott Smith's self-titled 1995 album, running 3:10. It got its own music video that year, directed by Ross Harris. The self-titled record built on Smith's debut Roman Candles and cemented his reputation for stark, intimate songwriting.

title: No Name No. 5
fact: Tucked into Elliott Smith's 1997 breakthrough "Either/Or," "No Name No. 5" is a showcase for his one-man-band chops — Smith played the drums, acoustic guitar, and bass himself, with Rob Schnapf and Tom Rothrock producing alongside him.

title: Pictures of Me
fact: "Pictures of Me" is track five on Elliott Smith's 1997 album Either/Or. Like his earlier records, it was recorded in various apartments around his adopted hometown of Portland, Oregon, with Smith playing every instrument himself, and the album was produced by Smith along with Tom Rothrock and Rob Schnapf. An unreleased live recording of the song from a July 1997 YoYo A Go Go festival performance later appeared on the album's 20th-anniversary expanded edition in 2017.

title: Say Yes
fact: "Say Yes" closes Elliott Smith's 1997 album "Either/Or" and was written about his then-girlfriend Joanna Bolme; Smith even left in the sound of himself clearing his throat at the start of the take for an unpolished, intimate feel. The song later gained wider recognition after director Gus Van Sant used it, along with two other Either/Or tracks, in the "Good Will Hunting" soundtrack.

title: Somebody That I Used To Know
Son of Sam
fact: Despite its ominous title, Elliott Smith was explicit that 'Son of Sam,' from his 2000 album Figure 8, is not about the real-life serial killer of that nickname. The title instead plays on a kind of internal duality, with the song riding a sunny, Beach Boys-meets-Beatles arrangement that contrasts with its wordplay. Its music video, directed by Autumn de Wilde, followed Smith chasing a self-moving red balloon through black-and-white freeze frames inspired by the 1962 French film La Jetee.

Ballad of the Dying Man
fact: "Ballad of the Dying Man" was the second single from Father John Misty's 2017 album Pure Comedy. Josh Tillman tracked the album's lead vocals and basic instrumentation live, often in just one or two takes, at United Recording Studios in Los Angeles, then brought in composer Gavin Bryars to write orchestral string, horn, and choral arrangements, with additional contributions from Nico Muhly and Thomas Bartlett.

title: Bored In the USA
fact: Father John Misty — real name Josh Tillman — built an actual canned laugh track right into the studio recording of 'Bored in the USA,' timing the laughs to land right after some of the song's bleakest lines, a trick he said was meant for 'neutralizing uncomfortable ideas.' When he performed it live on Late Show with David Letterman in 2014, his organ player cued the laughter in real time, leaving the TV audience unsure whether it was a real crowd laughing or part of the act. It remains one of the stranger production gags in modern singer-songwriter music.

title: Chateau Lobby #4 (in C for Two Virgins)
Funny Girl
fact: "Funny Girl" was the lead single off Father John Misty's 2022 album Chloë and the Next 20th Century, released in January of that year with a music video directed by Nicholas Ashe Bateman. Musically it's a string-laden, swing-era throwback that tells the story of a rising Hollywood starlet. The album was recorded at Jonathan Wilson's Five Star Studios with additional strings, brass, and woodwinds tracked at United Recordings.

title: Hollywood Forever Cemetery Sings
fact: 'Hollywood Forever Cemetery Sings' was the first single from Fear Fun, the 2012 debut album released under Josh Tillman's Father John Misty moniker. Its music video, which premiered on Entertainment Weekly's Music Mix blog, stars actress Aubrey Plaza of Parks and Recreation.

title: I Guess Time Just Makes Fool of Us All
I Love You, Honeybear
fact: The title track opens Father John Misty's second album, I Love You, Honeybear (February 2015, Sub Pop). Josh Tillman produced it with Jonathan Wilson, Phil Ek mixed it, and the album reached number 17 on the Billboard 200.

title: I'm Writing a Novel
fact: "I'm Writing a Novel," from Father John Misty's 2012 debut Fear Fun, is a surreal, Dylan-esque romp that mythologizes the writing of the album itself, complete with a tongue-in-cheek alternate title tacked onto the song. Josh Tillman wasn't writing a novel at all; he was busy finishing the twelve songs that made up Fear Fun, produced with the help of Jonathan Wilson and Phil Ek.

title: Pure Comedy
fact: Father John Misty's title track "Pure Comedy" first previewed live at a December 2016 benefit concert for Seattle Children's Hospital - its opening verse is an almost direct paraphrase of an unplanned rant he delivered on stage at a festival earlier that year.

title: Q4
fact: 'Q4' appears on Father John Misty's 2022 album Chloe and the Next 20th Century, and it tells a satirical story about a fictional novelist, Simone Caldwell, whose own literary work keeps getting passed over by publishers while flashier, lesser books get showered with praise. The title refers to the fourth financial quarter - the song is a dry commentary on how the publishing and entertainment industries commodify art, framing a writer's worth in the cold language of business and sales projections.

title: So I'm Growing Old on Magic Mountain

The Old Law
fact: Before it had its final title, this song was known as 'God's Trash' when Josh Tillman started slipping it into his live sets back in late 2024. It finally got a proper studio release as a standalone Sub Pop single, produced by Tillman with Drew Erickson, bridging the gap between his albums Chloe and the Next 20th Century and Mahashmashana.

title: The X-panded Universe
fact: The title of Father John Misty's 'The X-panded Universe' plays on 'expanded universe,' the term used for the sprawling side-stories built around franchises like Star Wars or classic comic books. True to that idea, Josh Tillman fills the song with a comic-book-style plot -- a scientist, a hidden weapon, a far-off resistance camp -- told in his usual sweeping, orchestral style. It continues his run of genre-bending, theatrically arranged songwriting under the Father John Misty name.

title: Things It Would Be Helpful to Know Before the Revolution
True Affection
fact: "True Affection" marked a notable departure for Father John Misty, built entirely around drum machines and pulsing synthesizers rather than his usual folk-rock arrangements. Produced by Josh Tillman with Jonathan Wilson for 2015's "I Love You, Honeybear," the electronic-heavy track has drawn comparisons to Sufjan Stevens's "Age of Adz" and Beck.

title: Lego Ring (feat. Lil Yachty)
fact: Faye Webster enlisted Lil Yachty — a friend since middle school — for "Lego Ring," a standout from her 2024 album Underdressed at the Symphony. The track pairs Webster's airy delivery with Yachty's Auto-Tuned harmonies over distorted bass and piano.

title: Dior
fact: Dior is from bitknot, the third album by Pittsburgh band feeble little horse. It came out May 26, 2026, just five days after it was announced, and follows their 2023 album Girl with Fish.

title: Doorway
fact: "Doorway" opens feeble little horse's album bitknot, and it exists because of a happy accident: band members were driving when a scratched CD kept skipping between the same two seconds of audio, and they decided to build a song that sounded just like that glitch. It starts with a blast of feedback before settling into murmured vocals over drum machines and keyboards. One of the band's members has called making it one of his favorite memories from the record.

title: Rewind
fact: Rewind, which runs only about two minutes, is one of 11 songs on bitknot, the third album from the Pittsburgh band feeble little horse. They announced it on May 21, 2026 and released it just five days later.

fact: "I Feel It All" was the third single from Feist's 2007 album The Reminder, reaching No. 47 on the Canadian Hot 100. For a performance on Jimmy Kimmel Live!, Feist played the song acoustically aboard a moving tour bus, with a hand bell set standing in for the studio version's piano.

title: So Sorry
fact: "So Sorry" opens Feist's 2007 album The Reminder, recorded in a fast two-week session at La Frette Studios outside Paris in March 2006. It was produced by Feist, Gonzales, and Renaud Letang, with Gonzales himself playing piano, organ, vibraphone, and drums on the track.

title: Anything We Want
fact: "Anything We Want" closes out Fiona Apple's 2012 album The Idler Wheel..., paired with "Hot Knife" to end the record on a hopeful note after its heavier songs. The song imagines an idealized moment of connection with a loved one, and Apple performed it with The Roots on Late Night with Jimmy Fallon just before the album's release.

title: Better Version of Me
fact: "Better Version of Me" appears on Fiona Apple's 2005 album Extraordinary Machine, which was Grammy-nominated for Best Pop Vocal Album. The album was actually recorded twice: an initial version produced by Jon Brion was shelved, and Apple re-recorded most of the songs, including this one, with producer Mike Elizondo for the final release.

title: Cosmonauts
fact: Fiona Apple wrote "Cosmonauts" for Judd Apatow's 2012 film This Is 40, recording it first with Jon Brion, who ultimately didn't use it in the movie - she later re-recorded it for her own album instead. Apatow had asked for a song about two people staying together forever, which Apple found a strange assignment since she wasn't sure she believed in that herself.

title: Drumset
fact: "Drumset" closes out Fiona Apple's 2020 album Fetch the Bolt Cutters, which she recorded mostly at her own home in Venice, California, with percussionist Amy Aileen Wood, bassist Sebastian Steinberg, and multi-instrumentalist Davíd Garza. The homemade, lived-in feel was intentional; Apple wanted the whole album to sound like it was made in a room rather than a polished studio.

title: Every Single Night
fact: "Every Single Night" was the only single released from Fiona Apple's 2012 album "The Idler Wheel...," built around a music-box toy piano and Apple's own layered vocal textures. Its opening line, "I just want to feel everything," became something of a thesis statement for the record.

title: Fetch the Bolt Cutters
fact: The title track that opens Fiona Apple's 2020 album Fetch the Bolt Cutters ends with the sound of her own dogs barking into the microphone, and several of her pets are individually credited by name in the album's liner notes. Apple recorded much of the record by jamming around her Venice, California home with her band, turning household objects into makeshift percussion instruments.

title: Hot Knife
fact: "Hot Knife" closes Fiona Apple's 2012 album The Idler Wheel... as a joyful, round-like vocal duet, with Apple pounding out the rhythm on drums rather than a drum kit. The music video, directed by Paul Thomas Anderson, uses split-screen effects to pair Apple with her real-life sister, singer Maude Maggart.

title: I Want You to Love Me
fact: "I Want You to Love Me" opens Fiona Apple's 2020 album Fetch the Bolt Cutters, which she recorded in her own home studio instead of a commercial facility, with a band that included drummer Amy Aileen Wood, bassist Sebastian Steinberg, and multi-instrumentalist David Garza. About a minute in, Apple holds a single note far longer than expected, then holds it longer still, before the song builds into its full piano-driven swell.

title: Left Alone
fact: Fiona Apple has said her favorite lyric she's ever written is "the ants weigh more than the elephants," from "Left Alone" on 2012's The Idler Wheel. She's credited the line to a David Attenborough nature documentary she saw about how, collectively, ants' total biomass actually outweighs that of elephants worldwide.

title: Tymps (The Sick in the Head Song)
Valentine
fact: 'Valentine' is the third track on Fiona Apple's 2012 album The Idler Wheel Is Wiser Than the Driver of the Screw and Whipping Cords Will Serve You More than Ropes Will Ever Do. Apple recorded the whole album in secret without even telling her label, choosing to produce it herself with her touring drummer Charley Drayton rather than longtime collaborator Jon Brion - the result has no electric instruments on it at all. Despite the romantic-sounding title, Apple has said the song isn't about a lover but about a girl she admired and wished she could be more like.

title: Werewolf
fact: "Werewolf" appears on Fiona Apple's 2012 album The Idler Wheel Is Wiser Than the Driver of the Screw and Whipping Cords Will Serve You More Than Ropes Will Ever Do. Apple has described it as a song about realizing you can still choose to stay friends with someone from a past relationship even after things didn't work out. The arrangement starts out spare before growing more complex, and the track closes with the sound of children playing.

title: A Long Way Past the Past
fact: A Long Way Past the Past is track 6 on Fleet Foxes' 2020 album Shore, which Robin Pecknold produced. It was recorded between September 2018 and September 2020 in Hudson NY, Paris, Los Angeles and New York City with engineer Beatriz Artola, and the album was released on the autumnal equinox.

title: Blue Ridge Mountains
fact: "Blue Ridge Mountains," written by frontman Robin Pecknold, appears on Fleet Foxes' self-titled 2008 debut album. It's a narrative song built around a missed connecting flight to the mountains near Asheville, North Carolina, layered over the band's harmony-heavy folk arrangements.

title: Grown Ocean
fact: Closing out "Helplessness Blues" (2011), "Grown Ocean" holds a neat bit of trivia: it's the only Fleet Foxes studio track to feature drummer Josh Tillman, who left the band the following year to launch his solo career as Father John Misty.

title: I Am All That I Need / Arroyo Seco / Thumbprint Scar
fact: This nine-minute medley opens 2017's Crack-Up and picks up musically right where Helplessness Blues left off six years earlier -- that album's closer ends in the key of F without resolving, and this one begins exactly there. Its title references Arroyo Seco, a dry-stream tributary of California's Salinas River, and the track closes with a swirl of field recordings: ocean waves, a passing train, the band's own lawyer's voice, and a Brooklyn high school choir's cover of 'White Winter Hymnal.'

title: I'm Not My Season
fact: "I'm Not My Season" appears on Fleet Foxes' 2020 album Shore. Its music video was filmed inside St. Ann and the Holy Trinity Church in Brooklyn and directed by Sean Pecknold, the older brother of Fleet Foxes frontman Robin Pecknold, who has directed several of the band's videos.

title: If You Need To, Keep Time on Me
Montezuma
fact: "Montezuma" opens Fleet Foxes' 2011 album Helplessness Blues. The band dressed up the minimal, elegiac arrangement with unusual instrumentation for an indie-folk record, including zithers, tamburas, Tibetan singing bowls, and a Moog synthesizer.

title: Sunblind
fact: "Sunblind" opens Fleet Foxes' 2020 album Shore and works as a thank-you note from frontman Robin Pecknold to the musicians who shaped his songwriting. He told Apple Music he wanted the track to feel like "a mission statement for the record -- kind of cite-your-sources energy," weaving in nods to artists like Richard Swift, Judee Sill, and Jimi Hendrix. Shore itself was announced only a day before its surprise release, timed to land on the 2020 autumnal equinox.

title: Third of May - Odaigahara
fact: 'Third of May / Odaigahara' was the lead single from Fleet Foxes' 2017 album Crack-Up, their first new music in six years. Frontman Robin Pecknold wrote it as a time-traveling meditation on his long friendship with guitarist Skyler Skjelset, whose birthday falls on May 3 - the same date their 2011 album Helplessness Blues was released. The title and some imagery also nod to Francisco Goya's 1814 painting The Third of May 1808, and each verse jumps to a different year in the band's history.

title: Tiger Mountain Peasant Song
fact: Fleet Foxes' 2008 debut is full of layered vocal harmonies, but "Tiger Mountain Peasant Song" strips all that away for a solo showcase of frontman Robin Pecknold over a single spare guitar part.

title: Your Protector
fact: "Your Protector" is on Fleet Foxes' self-titled debut album (June 2008, Sub Pop), which many critics ranked among the best albums of the 2000s. It was released as a single in 2009 and features flute alongside the band's signature vocal harmonies.

title: Keep Me in the Dark
fact: "Keep Me in the Dark" is track two on Flock of Dimes' 2025 album "The Life You Save," produced by Jenn Wasner and recorded at Betty's studio in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, and Montrose Recording in Los Angeles with additional production from Nick Sanborn. Its music video, directed by frequent collaborator Spencer Kelly, surrounds Wasner with projections of her younger self.

title: Olympic Airways
fact: Foals' "Olympic Airways," the fourth and final single from 2008's Antidotes, is about the pull of wanting to stay home rather than go out into the world, according to frontman Yannis Philippakis - it later turned up on the FIFA 09 soundtrack and on a Forza Horizon game's in-game Sub Pop Records radio station.

title: Strange Neighbour
fact: Strange Neighbour was released August 7, 2023 as London band Folly Group's first new music in over a year, described as a motorik slice of paranoid funk. It later became track 5 on their debut album, Down There! (January 12, 2024).

title: Hey Kekule
fact: Hey KekulÃ© was the first single from Strange Burden, the debut album from Austin five-piece Font (Acrophase Records). It draws on early-90s Manchester rave music and was inspired by a Cormac McCarthy essay about a German chemist of the same name.

title: A Hero's Death
fact: The title track and lead single from Fontaines D.C.'s second album takes its name from Brendan Behan's 1958 play "The Hostage," which contains the line "You're all in the running for a hero's death." Released in May 2020, it became the Dublin band's first song ever to chart in the UK and Scotland.

title: Cello Song
album: The Endless Coloured Ways: The Songs Of Nick Drake
fact: Fontaines D.C.'s cover of Nick Drake's 1969 "'Cello Song" (from Drake's Five Leaves Left) served as the lead single for the 2023 tribute album The Endless Coloured Ways – The Songs of Nick Drake. The band swapped Drake's cello-led acoustic arrangement for a driving backbeat and layered guitars, part of a 32-artist project that asked contributors to reinvent the songs rather than replicate them.

title: In the Modern World
fact: "In the Modern World," from Fontaines D.C.'s 2024 album Romance, was inspired by frontman Grian Chatten's love of the 1988 anime film Akira — he wanted to capture the kind of romance that blossoms even as the world around it falls apart. Bassist Conor Deegan's line "Come away with me and Sal" nods to Sal Paradise, the narrator of Jack Kerouac's On the Road.

title: Marianne
fact: Fontaines D.C.'s "Marianne," the lead single from 2026's Dopamine Chamber, borrows its glamorous, high-stakes aesthetic from Netflix's psychological thriller Ripley - the track was produced by James Ford, and its music video came from director Dave Meyers, known for Kendrick Lamar's "HUMBLE." and Travis Scott's "Sicko Mode."

title: Starbuster
fact: 'Starburster' was the lead single from Fontaines D.C.'s 2024 album Romance, with frontman Grian Chatten writing it after an anxious moment he experienced at London's St Pancras train station. He's said he initially wrote the rapid-fire, hip-hop-and-electronica-tinged verses almost as a joke, but when the band heard it they took it seriously, and it became the band's first entry on the UK Singles Chart.

title: Televised Mind
fact: Fontaines D.C. formed after its members met studying at Dublin's BIMM Institute, bonding over a shared love of poetry - though the five of them actually grew up in different parts of Ireland (and one in Spain).

title: Tongue
fact: "Tongue" is a single from Fontaines D.C., showing the Irish band pushing into more experimental production. Bassist Conor Deegan manipulated tape speed using a technique associated with Prince, while guitarist Carlos O'Connell ran Grian Chatten's vocals through a sampler to warp them into an unsettling, pitch-shifted register.

title: Too Real
fact: Fontaines D.C.'s "Too Real" comes from their 2018 debut album Dogrel - critics called it the first sign the Dublin band had more range beyond straightforward punk.

The short, bossa-nova-tinged track layers seagull sounds and oblique strings under a soft lead vocal, and arrived with an animated video by artist Meghan Fenske.

title: Higher
fact: "Higher" comes from Francis of Delirium's 2026 album Run, Run Pure Beauty, and it has a real personal story behind it: singer Jana Bahrich wrote it while recovering from neck surgery. For the choir vocals on the track, she brought in her own speech therapist, who happens to sing in a choir herself.

title: It's A Beautiful Life
fact: Francis of Delirium built “It's a Beautiful Life” out of small real moments - coffee with a pianist about to play a Philip Glass piece, and watching a choir rehearse in a basement - finding beauty alongside everyday loneliness.

title: Futurephobic
fact: "Futurephobic" appears on Frankie and the Witch Fingers' 2023 album Data Doom. Its main riff was actually written years earlier during sessions for the band's previous record, Monsters Eating People Eating Monsters, then shelved until it resurfaced and fit the new album's vintage sci-fi concept; the band finished the track's overdubs while touring through France and Amsterdam.

title: Abigail
fact: Frankie Cosmos' "Abigail," from 2022's Inner World Peace, is named for a dog Greta Kline became obsessed with years earlier after spotting it on Petfinder - the album art is even her own drawing of a real text conversation about the dog.

title: Aftershook
fact: "Aftershook" is a single from Frankie Cosmos' 2022 album Inner World Peace, the band's fifth LP for Sub Pop, blending 70s folk-pop with ambient and psychedelic touches. Bandleader Greta Kline has said the song is about processing the past while trying to hold onto "a balanced ratio of emotional awareness and hopefulness."

title: Apathy
fact: Apathy is on Frankie Cosmos's 2018 album Vessel. Greta Kline began as a solo bedroom-recording artist, and Vessel showed the project growing into a full-band DIY indie-pop sound.

title: Empty Head
fact: "Empty Head" is a 2019 single by Frankie Cosmos, the project of prolific New York singer-songwriter Greta Kline. The breezy, lo-fi indie-pop track is built around the idea of quieting an overactive mind, with Kline singing that it's okay not to have something profound to say all the time. It's a good example of the deceptively simple, diary-style songwriting that has made Kline one of indie rock's most prolific tunesmiths.

title: Jesse
fact: "Jesse" was the first single from Frankie Cosmos' 2018 album Vessel, their debut for Sub Pop. Songwriter Greta Kline has described the song as coming out of turning dreams and half-conscious realizations into lyrics, working through sudden personal epiphanies as they happened.

title: On the Lips
fact: "On the Lips" originally appeared on Greta Kline's 2013 self-released collection im sorry im hi lets go. She rerecorded it and issued it as a single in March 2016 ahead of her second studio album, Next Thing.

title: One of Each
fact: One of Each is from Different Talking, the sixth studio album by Frankie Cosmos, released June 27, 2025 on Sub Pop in LP, CD, cassette and digital formats.

title: One Year Stand
fact: "One Year Stand" appears on Frankie Cosmos' 2022 album Inner World Peace, released via Sub Pop. Greta Kline's band recorded it with producers Nate Mendelsohn and Katie Von Schleicher at Figure 8 Recording in Brooklyn, trimming the tracklist down from more than 100 songs Kline had written during the pandemic; bandmate Lauren Martin's Hammond organ and synth drones give the song its intimate glow.

title: Pressed Flower
fact: Pressed Flower opens Frankie Cosmos's 2025 album Different Talking (Sub Pop). Its video, directed by Adam Kolodny, stars comedy legend Tracey Ullman alongside the band.

title: Vanity
fact: "Vanity" was the lead single from Frankie Cosmos' sixth album, Different Talking (June 2025, Sub Pop). Greta Kline started writing it while walking about six and a half miles from Tompkins Square Park to Sunset Park in New York City.

title: Young
fact: "Young" appears on Frankie Cosmos' 2015 EP Fit Me In, which Greta Kline recorded with Aaron Maine of Porches using mostly electronic instrumentation, a departure from her earlier lo-fi guitar records. Kline has said the song was one of the first things she wrote in reaction to having her music - and herself - suddenly open to public scrutiny after her debut album Zentropy's success.

title: Why Do Fools Fall In Love
Anything
fact: "Anything" was Frankie Rose's first new single in six years when it arrived in 2023, previewing her album Love As Projection. Rose described the bright, synth-pop track as feeling "like a prom scene in a John Hughes movie" — a hopeful song about letting go of fear even when the world feels chaotic, built around comparisons to '80s acts like Strawberry Switchblade and Altered Images.

title: Best of Times
fact: "Best of Times" is the eighth track on Frankie Rose's 2026 album Hila, her sixth solo record and first in three years, made after she toured with The Jesus and Mary Chain in 2024. The song's flowing saxophone part, played by Jeff Tobias, gives it an '80s, cinematic feel that reviewers compared to a Michael Mann film score.

title: Can't Be Wrong
fact: Can't Be Wrong is a single from Frankie Rose's sixth solo album, Hila (September 18, 2026, Born Losers / Night School). It has 80s new wave and funk-inspired rhythms, and the record features drummer Justin Welch of Elastica and saxophonist Jeff Tobias.
