title: Night Or Day
fact: "Night or Day" is a single from Franz Ferdinand's 2025 album The Human Fear. The Scottish band broke through with their self-titled 2004 debut album, which was led by "Take Me Out."

title: Take Me Out
album: You Could Have It So Much Better
fact: Alex Kapranos got the idea for "Take Me Out" the night after watching the WWII film Enemy at the Gates, where a tense standoff between two snipers stuck with him as a metaphor for romantic tension. He wrote the song with bandmate Nick McCarthy while the two were roommates, and the song's signature guitar hook was inspired by the way blues legend Howlin' Wolf used to sing along to his own guitar playing. It became the second single from Franz Ferdinand's self-titled 2004 debut album.

title: If I Could
fact: "If I Could" is the third track on Manchester-born artist and producer Freak Slug's second album, Amulet (September 2026, Future Classic). Its video was directed by St Clair Bryant with Pulse Films, and the track adds anthemic horns and an upbeat drum pattern to the record's hazy guitars.

title: Miss June
album: Loose Tooth And A Short Skirt
fact: "Miss June" is by English musician Xenya Genovese, who performs as Freak Slug — a self-taught, Manchester-born visual artist turned indie rocker who cites Ride, Mazzy Star, and Pavement as touchstones. The song appears on her 2025 EP "Loose Tooth and a Short Skirt" and was co-written with John DeBold.

title: Muse
fact: "Muse" closes out Amulet, the second album by Freak Slug — the project of Manchester, UK singer-songwriter and visual artist Xenya Genovese — released September 18, 2026. It follows her 2024 debut album I Blow Out Big Candles and marks a sonic evolution for the project, which draws comparisons to Elliott Smith's intimate, double-tracked vocal style.

title: Talking Quiety Of Anything With You
album: Talking Quietly Of Anything With You

title: I Know There's Something Going On
Free Association
fact: "Free Association" is the lead single from Friendship's album Caveman Wakes Up on Merge Records, with a video the band shot on Super 8 film on a closed boardwalk in Seaside Heights, New Jersey. Singer Dan Wriggins said he was inspired by folk singer Kath Bloom, and even borrowed the line "born with a weak heart" from David Byrne; the band also said the Mellotron sax and voice sounds on the track started as studio jokes they ended up keeping.

title: Swim Until You Can't See Land
Choo Choo
fact: Choo Choo was a single ahead of Friko's second album, Something Worth Waiting For (2026). The Chicago duo of Niko Kapetan and Bailey Minzenberger first broke out with their 2024 debut, Where we've been, Where we go from here.

title: Crimson to Chrome
album: Where we've been, Where we go from here
fact: 'Crimson to Chrome' was the breakout single from Chicago band Friko, later included on their 2024 debut album Where We've Been, Where We Go From Here. It spent three weeks at No. 1 on the SiriusXMU chart and drew praise from outlets like Pitchfork and Brooklyn Vegan.

title: Seven Degrees
fact: Seven Degrees previewed Friko's second album, Something Worth Waiting For. The Evanston, Illinois band's Niko Kapetan says he'd misremembered the famous saying as "seven degrees of separation" instead of six, and the song is about staying close to people.

title: Something Worth Waiting For
fact: "Something Worth Waiting For" is the title track of Friko's second album, released in April 2026 on ATO Records and produced by John Congleton. It's the follow-up to their acclaimed 2024 debut, Where We've Been, Where We Go From Here; the core duo of drummer Bailey Minzenberger and vocalist Niko Kapetan expanded to a four-piece, adding guitarist Korgan Robb and bassist David Fuller for this album cycle.

title: Still Around
fact: Still Around is from Friko's second album, Something Worth Waiting For (April 2026), which was produced by John Congleton. The album stretches into noise-rock, avant-garde classical touches and 1970s-style symphonic ballads.

title: Where We've Been
album: Where We've Been, Where We Go From Here
fact: "Where We've Been" opens Chicago band Friko's 2024 debut album Where We've Been, Where We Go From Here, and has become the group's de facto theme song. Songwriters Niko Kapetan and Bailey Minzenberger have said the track's live performances typically close their shows, but they deliberately moved it to the album's opening slot so first-time listeners would get the full scope of the band right away.

title: From A Soon to Be Ghost Town
Rushin' River Valley
album: A River Running To Your Heart

title: Repeater
fact: "Repeater" is the title track and opener of Fugazi's 1990 debut full-length, written not long after guitarist-vocalist Guy Picciotto joined the band, bringing his trebly Rickenbacker guitar sound into the mix. The song's driving riff and drum attack were partly inspired by Public Enemy's "Rebel Without a Pause." Self-released on Ian MacKaye's Dischord Records with no major-label push, Repeater sold over 300,000 copies through constant touring and word of mouth.

title: Waiting Room
fact: "Waiting Room" was recorded in June 1988 at Inner Ear Studios in Arlington, Virginia, and first appeared on Fugazi's self-titled debut EP before being compiled onto 1989's "13 Songs." Ian MacKaye wrote it about being determined not to repeat the mistakes of his short-lived previous band, Embrace, and its funk-, reggae- and hip-hop-inflected groove made it one of Fugazi's most widely covered songs despite never being released as a single.

title: Standing On The Verge Of Getting It On
album: Standing on the Verge of Getting It On

title: Cave
fact: "Cave" is a track from Future Islands' fifth studio album, The Far Field, released on April 7, 2017 — not from their earlier breakthrough record Singles, as is sometimes assumed. The band supported the album with a notable touring run following their star-making 2014 Letterman performance of a different song, "Seasons (Waiting on You)."

title: For Sure
fact: For Sure was Future Islands' first new music since 2017's The Far Field, and the lead single from their 2020 album As Long as You Are. It features Jenn Wasner of Wye Oak, and it was the first release with longtime touring drummer Mike Lowry as an official fourth member.

title: Ran
fact: "Ran" was the lead single from Future Islands' 2017 album The Far Field, produced by John Congleton. Its music video, directed by Albert Berney, takes the title literally — following frontman Samuel T. Herring on a run that starts in a Baltimore suburb in daylight and ends in the Maryland countryside after dark.

title: Sail
album: From a Hole the Floor to a Fountain of Youth
fact: "Sail" started life as a tour-only 7-inch single before landing on Future Islands' 2026 rarities collection, From a Hole in the Floor to a Fountain of Youth, released to mark the band's 20th anniversary. Bassist William Cashion put together the compilation's tracklist and picked its title. It gives longtime fans a chance to finally hear a batch of songs that had never been on streaming services before.

title: The Fight
fact: "The Fight" was released as the fifth single from Future Islands' 2024 album People Who Aren't There Anymore. It pulls back from frontman Samuel T. Herring's usual explosive stage energy in favor of a more delicate, introspective vocal delivery, set against Gerrit Welmers' shimmering synth textures.

title: The Fountain
album: From a Hole in the Floor to a Fountain of Youth
fact: "The Fountain" started out as a non-album single, released on a 2012 7" paired with "Tomorrow," years before Future Islands broke through with Singles. It finally found a home on 2026's From a Hole in the Floor to a Fountain of Youth, a career-spanning compilation the band released for its 20th anniversary.

title: The Great Fire
fact: The Great Fire is a duet from Future Islands' 2011 album On the Water, pairing frontman Samuel T. Herring's vocals with Jenn Wasner of the band Wye Oak. It's one of several notable Future Islands tracks built around a guest vocal trade-off, a formula the band would return to years later with Debbie Harry on "Shadows."

title: The Ink Well
album: From a Hole in the Floor to a Fountain of Youth
fact: The Ink Well first came out in 2010 as one side of a split 7-inch single with Lonnie Walker on Friends Records, produced and mixed by Chester Endersby Gwazda. In 2026 Future Islands revived it for their rarities compilation From a Hole in the Floor to a Fountain of Youth.

title: The Tower
fact: Future Islands' “The Tower” takes its name and theme from W.B. Yeats' 1928 poem of the same name, about aging and the passage of time, built around the image of a lighthouse cutting through darkness.

title: Vireo's Eye
fact: "Vireo's Eye" comes from Future Islands' 2010 album In Evening Air, which the band recorded at a house in Baltimore's historic Marble Hill neighborhood between July 2009 and January 2010. The album's title was borrowed from a poem of the same name by American poet Theodore Roethke.

title: Easy Company (feat. Waxahatchee)
fact: Easy Company is the title track of Futurebirds' fifth album (August 9, 2024, Dualtone), on which Waxahatchee's Katie Crutchfield trades verses with Carter King. The Athens, Georgia band recorded it with producer Brad Cook in the border town of Tornillo, Texas.

title: Isn't It a Pity
fact: Galaxie 500 closed out their 1989 album On Fire with a hazy, reverb-soaked cover of George Harrison's "Isn't It a Pity," originally from his sprawling 1970 triple album All Things Must Pass. Producer Kramer gave it the same slow-motion, dream-pop treatment that defined the band's whole sound.

title: Strange
fact: "Strange" appears on Galaxie 500's 1989 album On Fire, recorded at Noise New York and produced by Kramer, who became known for shaping the trio's hazy, reverb-heavy guitar sound. All three members, Dean Wareham, Damon Krukowski, and Naomi Yang, share the songwriting credit.

title: Tell Me
fact: "Tell Me" appears on Galaxie 500's 1988 debut Today, which producer Kramer recorded for the famously tiny budget of about $750. The band tracked the record in just three days at Noise New York, cutting basic tracks in roughly four hours on day one and most vocals and leads in single takes on day two.

title: At Home He's a Tourist
fact: "At Home He's a Tourist," from Gang of Four's 1979 debut Entertainment!, peaked at No. 58 on the UK singles chart — still the highest chart position any Gang of Four single has reached. According to singer Jon King, guitarist Andy Gill recorded the song's jagged, scraping guitar part in a single take.

title: I Love A Man In Uniform
Outside the Trains Don't Run on Time
Paralysed
fact: Gang of Four's "Paralysed" opens 1981's Solid Gold, recorded at Abbey Road Studios in London - written by Andy Gill and Jon King, it's built around the memorable line "Paradise, if you can earn it."

title: We Live as We Dream, Alone
fact: "We Live as We Dream, Alone" comes from Gang of Four's 1982 album Songs of the Free, on which the famously angular post-punk band traded their jagged attack for a straighter, funkier dance groove built on clacking percussion and soulful backing vocals. It was written by guitarist Andy Gill and singer Jon King.

title: Count Me In
album: A Session with Gary Lewis and the Playboys

title: This Girl Is A Woman Now
album: The New Gary Puckett and the Union Gap Album

title: And Then I Kissed Your Lips
album: You Think You Really Know Me

title: You Keep on Looking
album: You Think You Really Know Me

title: 100 Horses
fact: Geese, the band behind "100 Horses" from their 2025 album Getting Killed, actually formed back in 2016 while its members were still in high school at Brooklyn Friends School and Little Red School House. They rehearsed and recorded in drummer Max Bassin's basement, and the band's name comes from guitarist Emily Green's childhood nickname, "Goose." The group planned to split up after graduating in 2020 but stuck together once Partisan Records signed them.

title: Long Island City Here I Come
fact: "Long Island City Here I Come" closes out Geese's 2025 album "Getting Killed" as its final track, a piano-driven high point where frontman Cameron Winter's voice builds into a fevered, repeated delivery of the title line before the record ends.

title: Low Era
fact: Geese's "Low Era," from their 2021 debut album Projector, was recorded in drummer Max Bassin's basement, a space the band nicknamed "the Nest" - the band has said four-on-the-floor songs like this one used to feel like poison to them, until they deliberately challenged themselves to write something more danceable.

title: Taxes
fact: Taxes was the lead single from Geese's fourth album, Getting Killed, released July 8, 2025 ahead of the album (September 26, 2025). The band recorded the album in Los Angeles over a month with producer Kenny Beats.

title: Bounce House
fact: "Bounce House" was Gelli Haha's debut single, released in March 2025 and later included on her album Switcheroo. The track was produced by Sean Guerin, and its music video was filmed inside a colorful indoor playground.

title: Johnny
fact: "Johnny" appears on "Switcheroo," the 2025 album from Gelli Haha -- the stage persona of LA artist Angel Abaya, built in collaboration with producer Sean Guerin. On the track, Gelli plays a torch singer leaning against a Casio keyboard, repeating the apology "sorry for acting cold (like ice cream)" until it starts to feel earned.

title: Klouds Will Carry Me To Sleep
fact: "Klouds Will Carry Me To Sleep" was released in March 2026 and added to the end of Gelli Haha's 2025 album Switcheroo on streaming services. The video was conceived by Gelli Haha and Sean Guerin and directed by David Gutel, and the song pairs singsong hooks with laser synths and a heavy low end.

title: RUNNIN OUTTA TIME
fact: By the time 'RUNNIN OUTTA TIME' came out, Genesis Owusu already had serious hardware on the shelf — his 2023 album Struggler won Album of the Year at the ARIA Awards. This track, from 2026's REDSTAR WU & THE WORLDWIDE SCOURGE, folds in New Order-style dance rhythms, turning one of the album's most exhausted stretches into one of its most danceable.

title: STAMPEDE
fact: 'STAMPEDE' is a standalone 2026 single from Ghanaian-Australian artist Genesis Owusu, released between his albums Struggler and Redstar Wu & the Worldwide Scourge. For the music video, Owusu returned to his home country of Ghana for the first time in eleven years, filming in the streets of Accra to spotlight local youth culture. He later performed the song as part of a cameo appearance on the TV series Heartbreak High.

title: Give Me Love (Give Me Peace On Earth)
Got My Mind Set On You
Saltwater
fact: "Saltwater" was the song that introduced the world to Geowulf, the dream-pop duo of Star Kendrick and Toma Banjanin, who formed on Australia's Sunshine Coast in 2016 before relocating to London. The track blends Hawaiian slack-key guitar with woozy, '90s-slacker-pop production.

title: SPLAT!
fact: "SPLAT!" marked London singer-songwriter Ella Smoker's first new release under her gglum moniker since her 2022 debut LP Weak Teeth, arriving alongside the announcement that she'd signed to the label Secretly Canadian. Her lo-fi, guitar-driven sound has drawn comparisons to Alex G, Phil Elverum, and Adrianne Lenker.

title: Home Is Where the Hatred Is
The Revolution Will Not Be Televised
Alogia
fact: "Alogia" comes from Dublin noise-rock outfit Gilla Band's album Pugnello, a band that actually performed for years as Girl Band before all four members renamed themselves in 2021. They chose "Gilla," an old Irish given name, and apologized for not having thought through their original name sooner.

title: Til I Hear It From You
Can You See Me
fact: "Can You See Me" appears on "We're Here, My Dear," the 2022 debut album released under the name Ging -- the recording identity Adam King Feeney adopted after retiring his longtime producer alias Frank Dukes, under which he'd made hits for Lorde, Camila Cabello, Post Malone, and The Weeknd. The album marked Feeney's shift from writing and producing for others to releasing music under his own voice.

title: Loneliness
fact: "Loneliness" comes from Ginger Root's 2022 EP Nisemono (Japanese for "fake" or "fraud"), a project built around a fictional premise: mastermind Cameron Lew imagined being hired to secretly write songs for a fabricated up-and-coming Japanese idol from 1983, filtering 1980s city pop through his own lens.

title: No Problems
fact: Ginger Root's Cameron Lew wrote "No Problems" without any particular plan for how it should sound, and the result ended up as one of his most quintessentially "Ginger Root" tracks, leaning hard into his city-pop influences with lush string arrangements. It's the second song on his 2024 concept album Shinbangumi.

title: Hello
fact: Girl and Girl formed in Queensland, Australia, after singer Kai James and guitarist Jayden Williams started jamming in Williams's mom's garage after school. James's aunt, nicknamed "Aunty Liss," stopped by one day after walking her dog, asked to sit in on drums, and stuck around for good; bassist Fraser Bell then rounded out the lineup. "Hello" comes from the band's 2024 Sub Pop debut album, Call a Doctor.

title: We Fell In Love In October
fact: Girl in Red is Marie Ulven, a Norwegian musician who taught herself piano, guitar, and production from her bedroom as a teenager. Her breakout song, "I Wanna Be Your Girlfriend," made the New York Times' best songs of 2018 list before she'd even released an album.

title: I Like That You Can See It
Born Yesterday
album: Don't Know What You're In Until You're Out

title: Nothing
album: Don't Know What You're In Until You're Out

rare animal
fact: "rare animal" appears on glass beach's 2024 album plastic death, produced by Will Yip. The song's explosive gang-vocal section was recorded by every member of the band plus a friend they call their "secret fifth member," Daxe — frontperson J McClendon compared the effect to "a Greek chorus arguing with me."

title: By The Time I Get To Phoenix
album: By the Time I Get to Phoenix

title: Don't Let Me Stop You
fact: Glenn Branca's "Don't Let Me Stop You" is an early recording collected on the 1997 compilation Songs '77-'79 - Branca, credited alongside collaborators from Theoretical Girls and The Static, later became known as an avant-garde composer famous for building symphonies out of massed, alternately-tuned electric guitars.

title: Plastic
fact: Glitterer is the project of Ned Russin, also known as the bassist and vocalist of the band Title Fight. "Plastic" was the first song Glitterer ever wrote as a full band rather than a solo studio project, and it appears on the 2024 album Rationale, released via ANTI- Records.

album: Hold Me, Thrill Me, Kiss Me

Better Off Dead
fact: Better Off Dead is from sook, a 2025 album by Good Dear Good, an indie pop-rock band from Halifax, Nova Scotia.

title: Slick
fact: Slick is from sook, a 2025 album by Good Dear Good, an indie pop-rock band from Halifax, Nova Scotia.

title: Self-destructor
fact: "Self-destructor" is a Good Looks song about frontman Tyler Jordan parting ways with a former bandmate after they couldn't get past creative differences, despite still caring about each other personally. It appears on Lived Here for a While, the band's follow-up to their 2022 debut album Bummer Year.

title: Ahhhh (This Isn't Ideal)
fact: "Ahhhh (This Isn't Ideal)" appears on Good Morning Seven, the seventh record from Australian duo Liam Parsons and Stefan Blair, who built their own studio and spent about a year and a half writing and recording the album. The song was inspired by Nina Simone and MGMT, and lyrically grew out of Blair reflecting on his feelings about being in the band at that point in time.

title: Good Times // End Times
fact: Tucked away as track 13 on Goose's 2026 album BIG MODERN!, this shapeshifting, doomsday-clock-paced rocker had never been played live before the record came out. Its official video was directed by the band's longtime collaborator Will Thresher.

title: Good2B
fact: "Good2B" is the first single from jam band Goose's 2026 album Big Modern!, released on their own label, No Coincidence Records. The band described the song as capturing a kind of joyful surrender amid modern-life chaos, calling it "a personal oasis in the algorithm."

title: If You Could Read My Mind
The Wreck Of The Edmond Fitzgerald
Delirium
fact: Delirium is track 10 on The Mountain, Gorillaz's ninth studio album (February 27, 2026). It features Mark E. Smith of the post-punk band The Fall, built from outtakes of his 2010 Plastic Beach sessions.

title: New Gold (feat. Tame Impala and Bootie Brown)
Orange County
fact: Gorillaz kept the title "Orange County" even after the song's original planned collaboration with Mexican singer Peso Pluma fell through, despite Damon Albarn having traveled to Pluma's Orange County studio to work on it. The finished version instead features singer-songwriter Kara Jackson and sitar player Anoushka Shankar, produced with Argentine producer Bizarrap -- and the words "Orange County" never actually appear in the lyrics.

title: Stylo feat. Mos Def and Bobby Womack
The Happy Dictator
fact: The Happy Dictator, featuring the art-pop duo Sparks, was the lead single from Gorillaz's 2025 album The Mountain. The collaboration was teased when Sparks posted a photo with Damon Albarn at his Studio 13, and Russell Mael joined Albarn for a performance on Jimmy Kimmel Live.

title: We Got the Power feat. Jehnny Beth
Stylo (feat. Mos Def and Bobby Womack)
Somebody That I Used To Know
Guardian Angel's Arms
fact: Graham Hunt's "Guardian Angel's Arms," from 2026's American Pyramid, was recorded with an eight-piece band at Minnesota's Pachyderm Studios - the same studio where Nirvana recorded In Utero.

title: A.M. 180
fact: A.M. 180 is from Grandaddy's 1997 debut album, Under the Western Freeway, and was released as a single in 1998 with a cover of Pavement's Here on the B-side. It peaked at number 88 on the UK singles chart and is used as the theme music for the BBC Four series Charlie Brooker's Screenwipe.

title: Cabin in My Mind
fact: "Cabin in My Mind" is from Grandaddy's 2024 album Blu Wav, the band's sixth record and first new album in nearly seven years, whose title is a portmanteau of bluegrass and new wave. Frontman Jason Lytle has said a friend coined the phrase "cabin in my mind" while they were traveling together on tour, and he liked the idea of it enough to build the song around it; the track also features pedal steel guitar, a first for the band.

title: He's Simple, He's Dumb, He's the Pilot
Way We Won't
fact: Way We Won't was released as a single on September 9, 2016, ahead of Grandaddy's fifth album, Last Place (March 3, 2017), their first in about 14 years after 2003's Sumday.

title: The Adventures of Grandmaster Flash on the Wheels of Steel
Gallic Shrug
fact: "Gallic Shrug" is track four on Greg Freeman's 2025 album "Burnover," featuring pedal steel from Ben Rodgers. Freeman sings the title's gesture of indifference -- "all you get is a Gallic shrug" -- in a ragged, earnest falsetto that critics compared to Paul Westerberg at his most heartfelt.

title: California
fact: Grimes (Claire Boucher) moved from Vancouver to Montreal at 18 to study neuroscience and electroacoustics at McGill University, with a minor in Russian literature, before getting pulled into the city's underground music scene.

title: So Heavy I Fell Through the Earth
You'll miss me when I'm not around
Four Cypresses
fact: "Four Cypresses," from Grizzly Bear's 2017 album Painted Ruins, began with drummer Chris Bear's unusual rolling beat and chord change, around which singer Daniel Rossen then built a melody and lyric. The music video pairs the song with home-movie footage from Rossen's own childhood, presented with lyrics styled like old VHS captions, exploring themes of impermanence.

title: Gun-shy
fact: Grizzly Bear started as a solo bedroom project for Ed Droste, recording lo-fi demos on a four-track in his Brooklyn apartment in 2002. The band name was actually a nickname he'd had for an old boyfriend.

title: Losing All Sense
fact: Grizzly Bear's "Losing All Sense," from 2017's Painted Ruins, started as the oldest demo in the band's pile - Chris Taylor sped up its original guitar riff and added a bass line, then Daniel Rossen layered in melody, passing it back and forth for years before it took final shape. Its music video features actress Busy Philipps.

title: Mourning Sound
fact: 'Mourning Sound' is one of the most propulsive tracks Grizzly Bear ever made, built around a slinky bassline that recalls New Order. It started life as a guitar riff from Chris Taylor, with Daniel Rossen later adding the chorus. Its music video features a group of women performing a stylized dance ritual through a mansion, which the band described as a playful commentary on women's liberation. It comes from 2017's Painted Ruins.

title: Speak in Rounds
fact: "Speak in Rounds" comes from Grizzly Bear's 2012 album Shields. The band had spent months recording an entire album's worth of material in Marfa, Texas, but scrapped most of it; back at Ed Droste's grandmother's Cape Cod house, guitarist Daniel Rossen simply strummed by the fire while Droste sang, and songs like "Speak in Rounds" came together in that stripped-down setting. Droste's vocal take was recorded after he thought he had nothing left in the tank, giving it an unusually raw quality.

title: Three Rings
fact: "Three Rings" was released as a single in May 2017 ahead of Grizzly Bear's album Painted Ruins. The track builds through layered vocal harmonies and woodwinds over a dusty electronic drum loop before a burst of guitar closes it out.

title: While You Wait For The Others
Yet Again
fact: 'Yet Again' was the second single from Grizzly Bear's 2012 album Shields and was one of only two songs recorded during the band's initial sessions in Marfa, Texas. The single's cover art features Untitled #17, a 1981 gouache-and-crayon piece by American painter Richard Diebenkorn, which also appears in the Shields liner notes.

title: Alien Observer
fact: "Alien Observer" is the title track of Grouper's 2011 album A I A: Alien Observer, one half of a two-album set released the same day alongside its companion, A I A: Dream Loss. Both records were self-released by Liz Harris on her own label, Yellow Electric, and built from layered, ghostly vocals and arpeggiated guitar recorded over several years.

title: Heavy Water / I'd Rather Be Sleeping
album: Dragging a Dead Deer Up a Hill

title: CEO of Personal & Pleasure
fact: Guerilla Toss formed in Boston in 2011 and relocated to Brooklyn in 2015 after singer Kassie Carlson signed the band to James Murphy's DFA Records. Carlson has described the title track's attitude as firing her own inner critic and reinstating herself as the slightly unhinged CEO of her own emotional start-up - a tongue-in-cheek self-care pep talk rather than anything else.

title: Bad Love Is Easy to Do
My Valuable Hunting Knife
fact: At a lean two minutes, 'My Valuable Hunting Knife' is classic peak-era Guided by Voices — a fragment of melody that barely has time to introduce itself before it's over. Robert Pollard liked it enough to re-record a fuller version for the Tigerbomb EP later that year, and the band even shot a brand-new music video for it to mark Alien Lanes' 25th anniversary reissue in 2020.

title: Space Gun
fact: "Space Gun" is the title track and opener of Guided by Voices' 26th studio album, released in 2018. The song famously kicks off with a found-sound recording of an airport restroom paper towel dispenser before launching into Robert Pollard's trademark power-pop guitar charge.

title: Teenage FBI
fact: "Teenage FBI" was the first single from Guided by Voices' 1999 album Do the Collapse, recorded during the Dayton, Ohio band's brief run on a major label. The song later found new life placed in the TV shows Buffy the Vampire Slayer and Veronica Mars.

title: The Official Ironmen Rally Song
album: Under the Bushes Under the Stars

title: To Remake the Young Flyer
album: Under the Bushes Under the Stars
fact: "To Remake the Young Flyer" is a Tobin Sprout-written, Sprout-sung track from Guided by Voices' 1996 album Under the Bushes Under the Stars, the last record for over a decade to feature the classic mid-90s lineup of Sprout, Kevin Fennell, and Mitch Mitchell. The brief, under-two-minute song was engineered by John Shough and later resurfaced on the compilation The Best of Guided by Voices: Human Amusements at Hourly Rates.

title: Dud
fact: "Dud" opens Ill Times, a 2024 collaborative album by Jay Watson (of Tame Impala and Pond, recording as GUM) and Ambrose Kenny-Smith (of King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard and The Murlocs). The record was notably the first release on King Gizzard's own label imprint, p(doom) Records.

title: Let Your Hands Go
fact: GUV is the solo project of Toronto musician Ben Cook, who rebranded from his earlier name Young Guv. 'Let Your Hands Go,' the lead single from the 2026 album Warmer Than Gold, leans hard into early-'90s UK sounds - part Madchester rave, part shoegaze, part Britpop - and features guest vocals from Hatchie and Turnstile's Meg Mills.

title: Warmer Than Gold
fact: GUV's "Warmer Than Gold" is the title track of Ben Cook's 2026 album, made with a wide cast of collaborators including Hatchie and Turnstile's Meg Mills - Cook has said he set out to make a Brit-rock record that sounded like it was produced by the Beastie Boys.

title: Utopia
fact: Gwenno's 2025 album Utopia is mostly in English, a change from her earlier records: 2018's Le Kov was written entirely in Cornish, one of the few albums in the language, and helped spark new interest in it.

title: Fight For You
album: Judas and the Black Messiah Soundtrack

On The Road
fact: "On the Road" opens Habibi's 2024 album Dreamachine and was produced by Tyler Love and Jay Heiselmann, with contributions from James Richardson of MGMT. The Brooklyn band, co-founded by Detroit natives Rahill Jamalifard and Lenny Lynch, has been playing together since 2011.

Knockin' Heart
fact: Leithauser wrote and recorded 'Knockin' Heart' in a single evening, then shelved it for over a year before releasing it as the lead single from 2025's This Side of the Island. He built the track around a power-trio concept inspired by Nirvana, layering together three separate bass parts -- one of his own plus two recorded by The National's Aaron Dessner.

fact: "22" is track four on Hana Vu's album Romanticism (May 2024, Ghostly International), which was produced with drums by Jackson Phillips of Day Wave. Vu has said the song is about being 22, feeling like both a baby and the oldest she'd ever been. A stripped-down version later appeared on her Movies EP.

title: Alone
fact: "Alone" is the third track on Hana Vu's album Romanticism (May 2024, Ghostly International). It's one of the album's upbeat, lush moments, with soaring electric guitar riffs and a strummy guitar underneath.

title: Aquamarine
fact: Hand Habits is guitarist Meg Duffy, who started on drums in 5th grade before switching to guitar at 17. Beyond their own project, Duffy has toured and recorded with Kevin Morby and Perfume Genius, and played on records by Weyes Blood and Hurray for the Riff Raff.

title: Just to Hear You (feat. Perfume Genius)
Way it Goes
fact: "Way It Goes" is a track from Hand Habits' 2025 album Blue Reminder, the project of guitarist Meg Duffy, who wrote the song in a songwriting class. Duffy is also a sought-after touring and session guitarist who has played in the backing bands of Kevin Morby, Weyes Blood, and Sylvan Esso.

title: Legal Tender
fact: "Legal Tender" is the opening track on Handsome Furs' 2009 album Face Control, written by the duo of Dan Boeckner and Alexei Perry. It was recorded and mixed by Arlen Thompson at Mount Zoomer studio and mastered by Harris Newman at Hotel2Tango.

I Guess the Lord Must Be in New York City
Lights On
fact: "Lights On" opens Hatchie's 2023 album Giving the World Away, the follow-up to her breakout debut Keepsake. The Australian dream-pop artist built the song around a drum beat inspired by Siouxsie and the Banshees' "Kiss Them for Me," and has said writing it pushed her to write more directly and personally than before. The accompanying video was directed by her longtime guitarist and collaborator Joe Agius.

title: Lose It Again
fact: "Lose It Again" is the lead single from Hatchie's 2025 album Liquorice, the follow-up to her 2022 record Giving The World Away. Harriette Pilbeam, who records as Hatchie, co-wrote the song with fellow Australian musician Jenny McLennan, who performs under the name Orchin.

title: Nosedive
fact: Australian dream-pop artist Hatchie (Harriette Pilbeam) wrote "Nosedive" with Joe Agius and Jorge Elbrecht after a night out at a Denver goth club, and the trio tried to bottle that club's energy, including an unusual lyric-free chorus. It became a standout single ahead of her 2022 album Giving the World Away.

title: Obsessed
fact: Hatchie's "Obsessed," the third single from her 2019 debut album Keepsake, was inspired by Harriette Pilbeam's teenage habit of latching onto a new best friend for support. She's described it as ultimately a celebration of a formative friendship that pushed her to become a more adventurous person.

title: Quicksand
fact: Hatchie's “Quicksand” catches her in a familiar cycle - feeling ungrateful even when things in her life are, on paper, going well.

title: Sage
fact: For her 2025 album Liquorice, Hatchie chose to work with just one outside collaborator, and she wanted that person to be a producer who also fronts their own band. That search led her to Jay Som, who recorded "Sage" at her own home studio with Warpaint and Courtney Barnett drummer Stella Mozgawa behind the kit. Hatchie's real-life partner, Joe Agius, co-wrote the track alongside her.

title: Stay With Me
fact: "Stay With Me," from Hatchie's 2019 debut album "Keepsake," started as a songwriting exercise for Harriette Pilbeam to try something more upbeat and dance-ready than her usual dream pop -- she'd written it with another artist in mind before realizing it fit her own record. She's called herself "a sucker for crying-in-the-club tracks," and it became one of her favorites on the album.

title: Sugar & Spice
fact: Hatchie is Harriette Pilbeam from Brisbane, Australia - "Hatchie" was actually her family nickname growing up. Before going solo she played bass in the bands Go Violets and Babaganouj.

title: Sure
fact: "Sure" is the second single from Hatchie's debut EP Sugar & Spice (2018), the breakthrough release that introduced Australian dream-pop songwriter Harriette Pilbeam to a wider audience. In February 2018 the track was remixed by Robin Guthrie, guitarist of dream-pop pioneers Cocteau Twins, a fitting nod given the genre's influence on Hatchie's sound. The EP was released through Double Double Whammy, Ivy League, and Heavenly Recordings.

title: The Rhythm
fact: "The Rhythm" was released on April 21, 2022, as a single ahead of Hatchie's second album, "Giving the World Away," which arrived the following day through Secretly Canadian. The song reflects the Australian artist's shift toward a brighter, more polished synth-pop sound compared to her shoegaze-indebted debut EP.

title: Without A Blush
fact: 'Without A Blush' was the lead single from Hatchie's debut album Keepsake (2019) on Heavenly Recordings, pairing jagged, industrial-tinged guitars with chiming, bell-like synth tones. Its music video, directed by Joe Agius, was shot in a candlelit warehouse filled with rows of red roses.

album: Ego Death At A Bachelorette Party
fact: Hayley Williams first released "True Believer," from her 2025 album "Ego Death at a Bachelorette Party," as an exclusive, passcode-gated track distributed through her hair-dye company Good Dye Young, before it reached streaming via her label Post Atlantic. She gave the song its live debut with a performance on "The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon" in October 2025.

title: Extraordinary Wings
fact: "Extraordinary Wings" is a single from Heartworms -- the project of London artist Jojo Orme -- off her 2025 debut LP "Glutton for Punishment." The lyrics build a modern myth around flight and falling in the spirit of Icarus: the pull toward something extraordinary, shadowed by the fear of what it costs to reach that high.

title: (We Don't Need This) Fascist Groove Thang
P.U.N.K. Girl
fact: Heavenly formed in 1989 in Oxford, England, out of the ashes of the band Talulah Gosh, with Amelia Fletcher, Peter Momtchiloff, Rob Pursey, and Mathew Fletcher all carrying over from the earlier group. The band released "P.U.N.K. Girl" in 1993 on the indie label Sarah Records, and more than 30 years later the song found a whole new audience when it went viral on TikTok, helping spark a 2023-24 reunion tour.

title: Wish
fact: Heavenward is the shoegaze-leaning side project of Kamtin Mohager, better known for fronting The Chain Gang of 1974, and 'Wish' comes off the project's debut EP, Staircase Music. Mohager has said the sound leans on '90s touchstones like Catherine Wheel and Swervedriver, calling the whole project a kind of personal therapy session.

title: Cinnamon Temple
fact: "Cinnamon Temple" was released as a single in June 2024 ahead of Hiatus Kaiyote's fourth album, Love Heart Cheat Code. It has been described as equal parts noise rock, lo-fi, punk, soul, and prog.

title: Red Room
fact: "Red Room" came together in a single overnight studio session in Brazil, in the studio of famed composer Arthur Verocai, during sessions for Hiatus Kaiyote's 2021 album Mood Valiant. Drummer Perrin Moss said it came together faster than anything the band had written before, while singer Nai Palm traced the song's title and warmth to a red light in her vocal booth that reminded her of red-tinted windows from a childhood home.

title: Telescope
fact: "Telescope" is the second track on Hiatus Kaiyote's 2024 album Love Heart Cheat Code (Brainfeeder/Ninja Tune). The Australian band built it on Brazilian, samba-like rhythms and was inspired by Hubble telescope photos taken on each band member's birthday, and it nods to The Temptations' "My Girl" in its vocal melody.

title: Forget It
fact: "Forget It," from Hippo Campus's 2024 album "Flood," came together after the band scrapped roughly five years of earlier material and started fresh, pouring more unguarded feelings into the new songs. The track turns on nostalgic questions about a first love -- who spoke first, what you were wearing -- regardless of whether you'll remember the details someday.

fact: Released in 2023 on Father/Daughter Records ahead of the album The Whaler, this is the Florida band's catchiest moment on record. Multi-instrumentalist Tilley Komorny said it has "the most pop elements" of anything they'd written, while still refusing to settle into a normal pop song structure — very on-brand for a band that treats midwest emo like a chemistry set.

title: I Want You Back
fact: Hoodoo Gurus' “I Want You Back” sounds like a breakup song, but frontman Dave Faulkner wrote it about a former bandmate who quit and was dismissive on the way out - he flipped the anger into a mock “spurned lover” song aimed right at him.

title: Suzanne
Heartbreak Rules
fact: Heartbreak Rules is the title track of a mini-album released May 19, 2023: eight new songs, two reworked tracks from Natural Part and a cover of The Smashing Pumpkins' Luna. Dimitri Giannopoulos wrote and recorded it alone, stripping away the band's usual fuzz for a sparse sound.

"2468" is a 2024 single from Horsegirl, the Chicago trio of Penelope Lowenstein, Nora Cheng, and Gigi Reece, released alongside the announcement of their Cate Le Bon-produced second album "Phonetics On and On." It marked a deliberate shift from the raw, bare-bones approach of their 2022 debut "Versions of Modern Performance," which the band had recorded live-to-tape with engineer John Agnello at Chicago's Electrical Audio.

title: Julie
fact: "Julie," from Horsegirl's Cate Le Bon-produced 2025 album "Phonetics On and On," was originally written on acoustic guitar -- an instrument the band ultimately cut from the finished recording. The slower, more melancholic song reflects the loneliness of moving to a new city, paired with a video built around winter and unrequited love.

title: Friends of Friends
fact: The music video for Hospitality's "Friends of Friends" premiered on Stereogum in January 2012 and was directed by Scott Jacobson, a writer for Bob's Burgers and The Daily Show. It starred Arrested Development actress Alia Shawkat alongside comedians Kurt Braunohler and Gabe Delahaye, following the on-screen unraveling of a long-distance relationship.

title: I Like It Like It That
And I Was a Boy From School
Devotion
fact: Devotion is a new song Hot Chip released with their greatest-hits compilation Joy in Repetition. Alexis Taylor called it a celebration of the devotion to doing the project together, and compared bandmate Joe Goddard to Brian Wilson for his dedication to making great pop.

title: Night and Day
fact: Hot Chip's Alexis Taylor and Joe Goddard met as students at Elliott School in London - Taylor has said going to see Royal Trux play together was the concert that changed everything for him.

title: One Pure Thought
fact: "One Pure Thought" was the third single from Hot Chip's 2008 album Made in the Dark, credited to all five band members: Owen Clarke, Al Doyle, Joe Goddard, Felix Martin, and Alexis Taylor. Critics likened its bright, driving synth-pop sound to a mashup of Paul McCartney and New Order, and its music video set animated versions of the band inside a colorful, geometric "pointillist" world.

title: Over and Over
fact: "Over and Over" was Hot Chip's breakthrough single, from their 2006 album The Warning. Joe Goddard built the track while trying to recreate the bassline from ESG's "Dance," and Alexis Taylor's lyrics riff on the band's love of hypnotic, repetitive music like Terry Riley's "A Rainbow in Curved Air" — NME later named it the best single of 2006.

title: Break Right
fact: Break Right, from Hotline TNT's album Raspberry Moon, was the first song the band wrote as a full group. The instrumental parts came from guitarist Lucky Hunter, bassist Haylen Trammel and drummer Mike Ralston rather than frontman Will Anderson.

title: Julia's War
fact: "Julia's War" is the lead single from Hotline TNT's 2025 album Raspberry Moon, and it marks the first song the band recorded together as a full four-piece — frontman Will Anderson, guitarist Lucky Hunter, bassist Haylen Trammel, and drummer Mike Ralston — after earlier records had been largely a solo studio project. The band tracked the album with producer Amos Pitsch of Tenement. Anderson wanted the vocals to cut through clearly over the wall-of-guitar shoegaze sound, giving the song its earworm "na na na" chant.

title: Was I Wrong?
fact: Was I Wrong? opens Hotline TNT's album Raspberry Moon (2025). Bandleader Will Anderson had mapped out the song's structure in a demo, but bassist Haylen suggested adding extra flavor during the studio sessions.

title: Around Again
fact: Hovvdy's Charlie Martin and Will Taylor met by chance at a Colorado Rockies baseball game in Denver in 2014, where both happened to be touring with separate bands - they bonded over songwriting and started Hovvdy together in Austin.

title: Bad News
fact: "Bad News" marked the first time since their 2016 debut Taster that both Hovvdy members, Charlie Martin and Will Taylor, traded off verses on the same song. It appears on their self-titled 2024 album, released to mark a full decade of the duo making music together. Martin has described it as "a whirlwind song about reckless behavior and the unlikely characters that weave in and out of your life."

title: Blast
fact: "Blast" is a single from Hovvdy's sixth album, Big World, released on Arts & Crafts, and its video was directed by Michael Rees. On this record the Austin duo moves away from direct emotional statements toward more enigmatic songs about their place in the world.

title: Forever
fact: "Forever" comes from Hovvdy's 2024 self-titled double album, a 19-song set released on Arts & Crafts. The song's music video, directed by Michael Rees, stars comedians Veronika Slowikowska and Kyle Chase. It was one of the songs the band used to announce the record.

title: I Never Wanna Make You Sad
Jean
fact: "Jean" is a 2023 single by the Texas duo Hovvdy (Charlie Martin and Will Taylor), produced by Andrew Sarlo. The song pushes the band into new territory with Auto-Tuned vocals and a skittish rhythm, while lyrically it's about wanting to do right by the people you love even amid self-doubt.

title: Try Try Try
fact: Try Try Try is the lead single from Hovvdy's sixth album, Big World (August 2026). It was produced by longtime collaborator Ben Littlejohn and recorded in Nashville and Asheville, with Will Taylor and Charlie Martin arriving with only instrumentals rather than finished demos.

title: You Will Go Far
fact: You Will Go Far is track 9 on Big World, Hovvdy's sixth album (August 14, 2026). The band worked from instrumentals rather than finished demos with producer Ben Littlejohn, in sessions in Nashville and Asheville in fall 2025.

title: Rocking Pneumonia and the Boogie Woogie Flu
Doing It All For My Baby
Stars
fact: "Stars" was the second single from Hum's 1995 album You'd Prefer an Astronaut, peaking at No. 11 on the Modern Rock Tracks chart and helping the album sell over 250,000 copies. The song's video and track also got an unexpected pop-culture boost from an appearance on MTV's Beavis and Butt-Head.

title: Why I Like the Robins
fact: Hum's “Why I Like the Robins” comes from You'd Prefer an Astronaut, an album full of space imagery - this song imagines watching from a window for the robins to return, and seeing the world through a loved one's eyes.

album: Indigo Jack & The New World Border

title: JUST ME & FRIENDS
fact: "Just Me & Friends" was released as a 2023 single and later included on Huron John's third album, Indigo Jack & the New World Border (2024). Co-produced by Matt Neighbor, it blends neo-psychedelia with alt-pop and has been called "a love letter to honesty and pure connection."

title: Colossus of Roads
fact: "Colossus of Roads" is from Hurray for the Riff Raff's 2024 album The Past Is Still Alive. It's named for boxcar graffiti artist buZ blurr, and bandleader Alynda Segarra has said the song felt like creating a space where all outsiders can be safe together, built on guitar, pedal steel, and a deliberately out-of-tune piano.

title: Pyramid Scheme
fact: "Pyramid Scheme" was released February 20, 2025 as a standalone single, the band's first new music after their acclaimed 2024 album The Past Is Still Alive. The song channels contempt for the dark side of the internet and how it alienates and undermines artists and outsiders.

title: Chartered Trips
fact: "Chartered Trips" is track four on Husker Du's 1984 double album Zen Arcade, written and sung by Bob Mould with piano parts from both Mould and Grant Hart. It's frequently singled out as one of the album's more melodic, pop-oriented songs, one that pointed the way toward the band's next record, New Day Rising.

title: Don't Want to Know If You Are Lonely
I Apologize
fact: "I Apologize" appears on Hüsker Dü's sprawling 1984 concept album Zen Arcade, which the Minneapolis trio tracked and mixed in roughly two marathon days at a studio in Redondo Beach, California. Nearly the whole record, including this song, is first takes, a pace so punishing that singer Bob Mould's voice was reportedly shot by the end of the session. Despite the chaotic recording, "I Apologize" is often singled out as one of the album's most melodic, almost power-pop moments.

title: Never Talking to You Again
fact: This Grant Hart-written track appears on Husker Du's sprawling 1984 concept album Zen Arcade. In the middle of an otherwise loud hardcore record, it stands out as one of the band's first entirely acoustic recordings, built around interweaving vocals from Hart and Bob Mould over just a guitar. After Hart's death in 2017, Mould performed the song live as a tribute to his former bandmate.

title: Hit Me With Your Rhythm Stick
Criminal Kissing
fact: IAN SWEET's "Criminal Kissing" comes from Shiverstruck, an album produced by Ben H. Allen (Animal Collective, Soccer Mommy) at Maze Studios in Atlanta - the record arrived roughly a decade after Jilian Medford released her debut IAN SWEET album, Shapeshifter.

title: Concept Of Love
fact: Ibibio Sound Machine's "Concept of Love" leads their album Chopping Mountain - frontwoman Eno Williams switches between English and Ibibio across the song, an Afro-disco track she's said grew out of wanting to hold onto love, togetherness, and hope amid an unstable world.

title: Got to Be Who U Are
fact: "Got to Be Who U Are" is a 2024 single by London-based Afro-funk group Ibibio Sound Machine, fronted by Anglo-Nigerian singer Eno Williams, released on Merge Records ahead of their album Pull the Rope. The track opens over a traditional African mbira pattern before dropping into a house-influenced dance groove, built around the idea that what unites people matters more than what separates them.

title: Pull the Rope
fact: The title track of Ibibio Sound Machine's 2024 album Pull the Rope, produced by Ross Orton and Max Grunhard, uses a tug-of-war image to describe finding common ground across differences. For the big chorus vocals, the band brought in friends Richmond Kessie and Helen McDonald, plus keyboardist Max Kerman's mother, to beef up the backing harmonies.

title: Ember
album: For Love of Grace & the Hereafter
fact: Ember opens Iceage's sixth album, For Love of Grace & the Hereafter (May 29, 2026), their first album of new material in five years. The Danish band recorded it at Silence Studio in rural Sweden with a raw, live approach and minimal overdubs.

title: No Fear
album: For Love of Grace & the Hereafter

title: Shelter Song
fact: 'Shelter Song' comes from Iceage's 2021 album Seek Shelter, the first time the Danish band brought in an outside producer — Sonic Boom, aka Pete Kember of Spacemen 3 — recording at Lisbon's Namouche studio. The track's big, reverb-drenched hooks get an extra lift from the Lisboa Gospel Collective on backing vocals, a world away from the band's early, more abrasive sound.

title: Gift Horse
fact: "Gift Horse" was a single released in January 2024 ahead of IDLES' fifth album, Tangk, alongside "Dancer" and "Grace." The video was directed by David Helman, and the album was produced by Nigel Godrich, Kenny Beats, and IDLES member Mark Bowen.

title: Grace
fact: "Grace" was released in December 2023 as a single from IDLES' fifth album, Tangk (February 2024), which was produced by Nigel Godrich, Kenny Beats, and IDLES guitarist Mark Bowen. Frontman Joe Talbot has said it was the only song whose words and singing came out of their sessions with Godrich, and it builds slowly into a big crescendo, softer than most IDLES songs.

title: Mr. Motivator
fact: The title nods to the real "Mr Motivator," British fitness instructor Derrick Evans, who became a UK breakfast-TV fixture in the 1990s leading brightly dressed, high-energy workout segments on GMTV. IDLES borrowed his name for a song that piles up over-the-top pop-culture pump-up lines as a tongue-in-cheek call to self-improvement. It was released as the first single from their 2020 album Ultra Mono.

title: Rabbit Run
fact: Rabbit Run was released July 30, 2025 for the soundtrack of Darren Aronofsky's film Caught Stealing. It continues the heavy sound of IDLES' album TANGK, and the band said they were also recording new material with Kenny Beats and Nigel Godrich.

Real Wild Child (Wild One)
fact: Iggy Pop's "Real Wild Child (Wild One)" is a cover with a long history: it started as Australian rocker Johnny O'Keefe's 1958 song "Wild One" before Jet Harris of The Shadows retitled and reworked it as "Real Wild Child" in 1962. Iggy Pop's 1986 version, from his album Blah-Blah-Blah, became a UK Top 10 hit and later turned up in movies like Crocodile Dundee II and Adventures in Babysitting; in 2008 he even re-recorded it with the band Jet as a tribute to O'Keefe.

title: Seabird
fact: "Seabird" was written by Billy and Bobby Alessi and first released by the soft-rock duo Alessi Brothers in 1976. The little-known group Innovations put out its own dreamy, synth-tinged cover a year later on one of only two singles it ever released. The song has since become a cult yacht-rock favorite, covered by acts like Metronomy and featured on the soundtrack to Taika Waititi's Hunt for the Wilderpeople.

title: Stella Was a Diver and She Was Always Down
fact: Interpol frontman Paul Banks has never explained exactly who "Stella" is, keeping the lyrics deliberately open to interpretation -- a hallmark of the band's early songwriting style. Musically, the track's droning guitars and reverb-soaked atmosphere are often singled out as one of the clearest nods to Joy Division on Interpol's acclaimed 2002 debut, Turn on the Bright Lights.

title: Wings On Fire
fact: Interpol debuted "Wings On Fire" live in Albuquerque in April 2026, ahead of its release on This Mirror Weighs a Ton - their first album since 2022's The Other Side of Make-Believe.

title: About a Bruise
fact: "About a Bruise" comes from Iron & Wine's 2017 album Beast Epic, where Sam Beam pairs plucky piano, harp, and rhythm against heavier lyrical content. The song leans on vivid Southern imagery -- skies full of prayers, duck hunting, mall cops in Mobile -- building to a choir chanting "This is Alabama."

title: All In Good Time feat. Fiona Apple
In Your Ocean
fact: In Your Ocean was the lead single from Hen's Teeth (Sub Pop, February 2026), Iron & Wine's eighth album. Sam Beam has described it as a sibling record to Light Verse, his 2024 Grammy-nominated album.

title: Jezebel
fact: "Jezebel" is a highlight of Iron & Wine's 2005 album Woman King, written by Sam Beam and produced with Brian Deck. The song borrows the name of the Biblical queen Jezebel but flips the script, reimagining her sympathetically as a wronged woman rather than the villain of the original story.

title: Last of Your Rock 'n' Roll Heroes
fact: Last of Your Rock 'n' Roll Heroes is from Iron & Wine's 2018 Sub Pop EP Weed Garden, a set of six songs left over from the sessions for Sam Beam's album Beast Epic.

title: Me and Lazarus
fact: Iron & Wine's "Me and Lazarus," from 2013's Ghost on Ghost, was recorded in New York with a cast of jazz and Americana players - including Bob Dylan bassist Tony Garnier, jazz drummer Brian Blade, and members of Antony and the Johnsons - all brought together by producer Brian Deck.

title: Sundown (Back in The Briars)
fact: "Sundown (Back in the Briars)" appears on Iron & Wine's 2002 debut The Creek Drank the Cradle, a collection of lo-fi home recordings Sam Beam originally made just as demos to send to Calexico's Joey Burns and John Convertino in hopes they'd serve as his rhythm section. Instead, Beam wound up writing, performing, recording, and producing every track entirely by himself in a home studio.

title: Thomas County Law
fact: "Thomas County Law" appears on Iron & Wine's 2017 album Beast Epic, the project of singer-songwriter Sam Beam. Beam has said the song is about "both denying and accepting one's origins," wrestling with an ambivalent relationship to where he's from.

title: Waves Of Galveston
fact: 'Waves of Galveston' started life as an outtake from Iron & Wine's Ghost on Ghost sessions, written when The A.V. Club's 'State Songs' project tasked Sam Beam with writing a song about Texas. It remained one of his live staples for years before finally getting an official studio release on the 2018 Weed Garden EP.

title: Woman King
fact: Woman King was the title track of an Iron & Wine EP released February 22, 2005 on Sub Pop. Sam Beam recorded it in August 2004 with Brian Deck at Engine Studios, adding percussion, piano, violin and electric guitar to his usually hushed sound.

title: Your Fake Name Is Good Enough
(We Like To) Do it With the Lights On
fact: Islands' "(We Like To) Do It With the Lights On" comes from 2021's Islomania, the band's first album in five years - frontman Nick Thorburn has said the tongue-in-cheek title started as a throwaway joke, and that he built the song's melody on top of the groove first, a new approach for him on this record.

title: Back Into It
album: Should I Remain Here, At Sea

title: Rough Gem
fact: "Rough Gem" comes from Islands' 2006 debut album Return to the Sea. Islands was formed by Nicholas Thorburn and Jamie Thompson right after their previous band, The Unicorns, broke up in 2004, and the record — released on Rough Trade in Europe and Equator in North America — blended orchestral pop with playful horn-and-whistle hooks.

Derecho Demonico
fact: "Derecho Demonico" came out in April 2026 as a double single with "G.O.D. And The Broken Ribs" and later landed on Jack White's album Frozen Charlotte (July 2026, Third Man Records). They were his first new songs since 2024's No Name, played with his live band of Patrick Keeler, Dominic Davis, and Bobby Emmett.

title: Dollar Bill
fact: "Dollar Bill," from Jack White's 2026 album Frozen Charlotte, is built as a stripped-down, nursery-rhyme-like chant — reviewers have noted it uses only around 32 unique words across the whole song. Its repeated hook, "I did it for the love and the dollar, a dollar bill," gives the track its title.

title: G.O.D. And The Broken Ribs
fact: This song came out in April 2026 as a double single with "Derecho Demonico" and was later included on Jack White's album Frozen Charlotte (July 2026, Third Man Records). It features his live band: Patrick Keeler on drums, Dominic Davis on bass, and Bobby Emmett on keys.

title: Neighbors Blues
fact: Neighbors Blues is the closing track on Jack White's seventh solo album, Frozen Charlotte (2026, Third Man Records). It leans into the fuzzed-out garage-rock sound of his earlier records.

title: That's How I'm Feeling
fact: "That's How I'm Feeling" comes from Jack White's 2024 album No Name, which had one of the most unusual rollouts in recent memory: White first gave the record away free as unmarked white-label vinyl to customers at Third Man Records stores in Nashville, Detroit, and London, with no artist name or song titles printed anywhere on the sleeve. He wrote, recorded, and produced the entire record himself at his own Third Man Studio.

title: Would You Fight For My Love?
fact: Before music, Jack White (born John Gillis, the youngest of ten kids) briefly considered the priesthood and ran his own upholstery shop in Detroit. He married drummer Meg White in 1996 and took her last name when they formed The White Stripes.

title: Hi-De-Ho
fact: Jack White built "Hi-De-Ho" around a sample of Cab Calloway's 1943 tune "Hi-De-Ho Man" after hearing it on the radio and wanting its scatting to ride over a drumbeat; White had been a Calloway fan since childhood, when his father showed him old footage of the bandleader. White sent the track to Q-Tip, who reportedly sent back his own scatting vocal just five minutes later, and the song appears on White's 2022 album Fear of the Dawn.

fact: "Lips" was released in August 2023 as a single ahead of Jane Remover's second album, Census Designated (October 2023, DeadAir Records). Jane followed it with the 2025 album Revengeseekerz.

title: 12 Steps
fact: The title of Japanese Breakfast's "12 Steps" sounds like it's about recovery, but it's actually named after 12 Steps Down, a real bar in South Philadelphia where Michelle Zauner first met the man who became her husband. The 2017 song, from Soft Sounds from Another Planet, is her tongue-in-cheek apology for the timing.

title: Be Sweet
fact: Japanese Breakfast's Michelle Zauner is also a bestselling author - her memoir Crying in H Mart topped the New York Times bestseller list and is being adapted into a feature film.

title: Everybody Wants To Love You
fact: "Everybody Wants to Love You" appears on Japanese Breakfast's 2016 debut album Psychopomp. The recording features bassist Peter Bradley playing alongside bandleader Michelle Zauner's own guitar and keyboard parts — Bradley later married Zauner and went on to become the band's touring guitarist.

title: Kokomo, IN
fact: Japanese Breakfast's "Kokomo, IN" comes from 2017's Soft Sounds from Another Planet - Michelle Zauner's acclaimed second album under the Japanese Breakfast name, later re-recorded and included as a bonus cut on 2021's Jubilee.

title: Machinist
fact: "Machinist" was the first single from Michelle Zauner's Japanese Breakfast album Soft Sounds from Another Planet (2017). Set to a synth-pop groove, the song tells a tongue-in-cheek, B-movie-style sci-fi story about a woman who falls for a robot, closing out with an unexpected saxophone solo. The music video leans further into the retro space-opera concept.

title: Orlando in Love
fact: "Orlando in Love" was released January 7, 2025 as the lead single announcing Japanese Breakfast's album For Melancholy Brunettes (& Sad Women), written by Michelle Zauner and produced by Blake Mills. The title nods to Orlando Innamorato, the unfinished Renaissance-era epic poem by Matteo Maria Boiardo.

title: Paprika
fact: "Paprika" opens Japanese Breakfast's 2021 album Jubilee with a burst of horns and strings inspired by the "Parade" theme from Satoshi Kon's 2006 anime film of the same name. Michelle Zauner, who had spent the prior years taking music theory and piano lessons to sharpen her composing, worked with bandmate Craig Hendrix and a small ensemble of string and horn players to build the song's marching-band-style crescendo.

title: Posing in Bondage
fact: 'Posing in Bondage' sits on Japanese Breakfast's 2021 album Jubilee, the first record where Michelle Zauner co-wrote full orchestral string and horn arrangements herself rather than leaving those decisions to the studio. She credited the confidence to arrange more ambitiously to having dipped into strings and horns in smaller doses on her previous album, Soft Sounds from Another Planet.

title: Savage Good Boy
fact: The music video for Japanese Breakfast's 'Savage Good Boy' stars Michael Imperioli -- Christopher from The Sopranos -- opposite frontwoman Michelle Zauner. The song appears on 2021's Jubilee, the album that pushed Japanese Breakfast into the mainstream and landed a Grammy nomination for Best Alternative Music Album. Musically, the track is built on bouncing drums and a bright, bubbly bassline, a deliberately upbeat sound Zauner designed as a stark contrast to the song's lyrics.

title: Slide Tackle
fact: Despite its title, "Slide Tackle" from Japanese Breakfast's 2021 album Jubilee has nothing to do with soccer - Michelle Zauner has said she hasn't played since third grade. She explained that she liked the idea of literally wrestling or tackling her own brain into submission, forcing herself to feel joy, and that image became the song's central idea.

title: The Ballad of the Witches' Road (Pop Version)
fact: Michelle Zauner's version of "The Ballad of the Witches' Road" comes from Marvel's Disney+ series Agatha All Along, where the song appears in several different cast versions. Co-produced by Jack Antonoff, her take has a sweeping, orchestral, Fleetwood Mac-style sound.

title: I Can't Believe I Did This Without You
Savory
fact: "Savory" was Jawbox's first single off their 1994 major-label debut, For Your Own Special Sweetheart, and it picked up airplay on MTV's 120 Minutes even though it never charted. A few years later, members of the band Far teamed up with Deftones' Chino Moreno to record their own cover of it for Far's 1997 EP Soon.

title: Superbike
fact: 'Superbike' was the lead single from Jay Som's 2019 album Anak Ko, which Melina Duterte wrote, recorded, and produced entirely herself during a solo retreat in Joshua Tree. The lyrics imagine a motorcycle as an escape fantasy from heartbreak. Duterte has said she aimed for a sound combining the Cocteau Twins with Alanis Morissette.

title: The Bus Song
fact: Jay Som is the solo recording project of Melina Duterte, who wrote, recorded, and produced her 2017 debut album Everybody Works largely on her own. "The Bus Song," from that album, has been described as a glistening "mass-transit reverie" carrying echoes of sunshine pop.

title: Empire State Of Mind feat Alicia Keys
HEALMODE
fact: 'HEALMODE' appears on Jeff Rosenstock's 2023 album HELLMODE, and its title is a deliberate, hopeful wordplay counterpoint to the album name. Rosenstock wrote it after his band's first tour since 2019, reflecting on having moved away from California to escape wildfires and drought, and expressing gratitude for one person in his life. It's a notably quieter, acoustic-leaning track compared to his usual ska-punk energy.

title: Enough
fact: Enough is a single from Jeff Tweedy's 30-song triple album Twilight Override, released September 26, 2025. The album features his sons Spencer and Sammy Tweedy alongside Chicago collaborators including James Elkington, Sima Cunningham, Macie Stewart and Liam Kazar.

title: To be a rose
fact: "To Be a Rose" was the lead single from Jenny Hval's 2025 album Iris Silver Mist. Over a drum-machine beat, Hval half-speaks the line "A rose is a rose is a rose is a cigarette," nodding to Gertrude Stein's famous repeated-rose line. The accompanying video splices together tour footage Hval shot between 2015 and 2024, edited by Jenny Berger Myhre.

title: A Postcard to Nina
fact: A Postcard to Nina is from Jens Lekman's second album, Night Falls Over Kortedala (2007). In 2022 the album was pulled from streaming over sample clearances and reissued as The Linden Trees Are Still in Blossom.

title: How We Met The Long Version
On A Pier, On The Hudson
fact: "On a Pier, On the Hudson," featuring singer Matilda Sargren, appears on Jens Lekman's 2025 album Songs for Other People's Weddings. It's part of a full narrative concept album about a fictional wedding singer, released alongside a companion novel Lekman co-wrote with author David Levithan.

title: Come Again
fact: Come Again is the lead single from Jim James' 2026 album Wowed Out on ATO Records, his first solo album in eight years. It began as a piece he composed for a scene set in a teddy bear factory, and the album grew out of music he wrote for two film projects in the early 2010s.

title: Sold
fact: Jo Passed's "Sold" comes from Their Prime, the Vancouver band's 2018 debut full-length for Sub Pop. The project started as just singer Jo Hirabayashi and drummer Mac Lawrie, who moved to Montreal together and toured across the continent before growing into a full band.

fact: 'Colleen' is a then-unreleased Joanna Newsom song that surfaced on the Joanna Newsom and the Ys Street Band release, from the same era as her acclaimed 2006 album Ys. Like the mythic storytelling on Ys, 'Colleen' unfolds as a kind of fairy tale, following a young mermaid or sea-nymph who has forgotten who she really is. It's built in the same dense, harp-driven, novelistic style that made Ys a cult favorite.

title: Inflammatory Writ
fact: "Inflammatory Writ" was one of only three brand-new compositions on Joanna Newsom's 2004 debut, "The Milk-Eyed Mender" (the rest were older songs she re-recorded). It's a playful, country-tinged tune built around upright piano rather than her signature harp, widely noted as one of the album's funniest, most tongue-in-cheek moments.

title: Peach, Plum, Pear
fact: "Peach, Plum, Pear" comes from Joanna Newsom's 2004 debut album The Milk-Eyed Mender and is driven entirely by a harpsichord rather than her signature harp. The song has since been covered by Owen Pallett (performing as Final Fantasy) on his 2006 EP Young Canadian Mothers, as well as by the band Straylight Run.

title: Dancin' Late at Night
fact: 'Dancin' Late at Night' appears on Modern Lovers 88, from a period when Jonathan Richman steered his band away from its earlier Velvet Underground-indebted sound toward a gentler blend of pop and 1950s rock and roll. The track itself chugs along with an upbeat feel critics have compared to a mix of Buddy Holly, Chuck Berry, and the Ventures.

Just My Friend
fact: "Just My Friend" is the lead single from Jordan Patterson's 2026 EP "Songs From A Valley Girl," her debut release for Secretly Canadian. Patterson, a North Carolina-born, L.A.-raised singer-songwriter, built the upbeat piano track around the direct question that gives it its hook: "Do you wanna be just my friend?"

title: Crosses
fact: "Crosses" was the title track of José González's debut EP, released in June 2003, and was later folded into his first full-length album, Veneer, that October. The stripped-down acoustic track later gained wider exposure when it soundtracked the season-two finale of the TV series The O.C.

title: Heartbeats
fact: Jose Gonzalez's hushed, acoustic-guitar version of "Heartbeats" is a cover of a 2002 song by Swedish electronic duo The Knife. His recording became a hit after it soundtracked Sony's famous 2005 "Bravia" TV commercial, in which 250,000 real bouncy balls cascade down a San Francisco street, pushing the song to No. 9 on the UK charts.

title: Swing
fact: Jose Gonzalez's "Swing," from 2021's Local Valley - his first new album in six years - blends West African highlife guitar lines with Caribbean rhythms into a song about body positivity, built around the simple message that it's okay to move however you want, wherever you are.

title: Atmosphere
fact: Joy Division first worked up this song under the working title 'Chance' for a 1979 Manchester radio session before recording the version we know that October with producer Martin Hannett at Cargo Studios in Rochdale. As with much of the band's writing process, Peter Hook's layered bassline came together first, with Bernard Sumner's synths and Stephen Morris's drums building the song's hazy, atmospheric wall of sound around it.

title: Heart and Soul
fact: "Heart and Soul" was recorded in March 1980 at Britannia Row Studios in London for Joy Division's second album, Closer, with producer Martin Hannett. It leans more on synthesizers than the band's earlier work, using an Arp Omni to create its distinctive sound.

title: Love Will Tear Us Apart
fact: Joy Division first recorded this song at Pennine Studios in Oldham on January 8, 1980, but the band and producer Martin Hannett weren't happy with it, so they redid it in March at Strawberry Studios in Stockport. The June 1980 single has since been covered in at least 168 recorded versions.

title: Transmission
fact: 'Transmission' was Joy Division's debut single for Factory Records, released in October 1979, and was deliberately left off their album Unknown Pleasures because the band believed singles and albums should stay separate. The band also recorded it for a John Peel session at the BBC's Maida Vale studios, and its driving 'dance, dance, dance to the radio' refrain made it one of their most influential early tracks.

title: Evening Mood
album: Something In The Room She Moves
fact: "Evening Mood," from Julia Holter's 2024 album Something in the Room She Moves, was partly inspired by her daughter's favorite film, Miyazaki's Ponyo. Holter wove an actual recording of her own pregnancy ultrasound heartbeat, run through a phaser, into the track alongside Dev Hoff's fretless bass and Chris Speed's clarinet.

title: Don't Know How To Keep Loving You
Get Away From Me (I Think I'll Love You Soon)
fact: Julia Jacklin's "Get Away From Me (I Think I'll Love You Soon)" is a breezy slice of '80s-inflected jangle pop that introduced her 2026 album The Gem. The record takes its name from a small Melbourne bar Jacklin frequented after moving there from Sydney, and it was recorded at Rat Shack studio with Jacklin co-producing alongside Robert Muinos.

title: If I Had The Hand Of God
fact: "If I Had the Hand of God" is a single from Julia Jacklin's 2026 album The Gem on 4AD. Jacklin wrote the country-rock track as a meditation on life as a touring musician, partly inspired by a recent trip to Nashville.

title: The Hardest Thing
fact: "The Hardest Thing," the third single off Julia Jacklin's 2026 album "The Gem," comes with one of the year's most ambitious music videos — a single unbroken shot filmed entirely from a helicopter weaving through the Melbourne skyline, directed by Danny Cohen.

title: 11th Dimension
fact: Julian Casablancas' "11th Dimension," the lead single from his 2009 solo debut Phrazes for the Young, earned Pitchfork's "Best New Track" honor - Danielle Haim, later of Haim, played drums in the song's music video and in Casablancas' touring band.

title: Popsicle
fact: Popsicle was a single from Juliana Hatfield's 2025 album Lightning Might Strike. Its video was directed by Paige Applin, and Hatfield has said the frozen summer treat is a symbol for the dread in her head, wrapped in bright pop sweetness.

title: flutter
fact: "flutter" was the debut single from the band julie, written and recorded in Los Angeles after members Keyan Pourzand and Alexandria Elizabeth moved there for architecture school. They finished recording it just before COVID lockdown and released it in 2020 hoping it might reach 1,000 streams; instead it went on to rack up more than 30 million plays, launching the band's career.

title: Ringside
fact: Julien Baker's "Ringside," from 2021's Little Oblivions, comes from the first Julien Baker album built around a full-band sound - she produced it herself and played nearly every instrument, with boygenius bandmates Phoebe Bridgers and Lucy Dacus contributing backing vocals.

title: The Modern Leper
album: Tiny Changes A celebration of the Midnight Organ Fight

title: All of the Time
fact: All of the Time was released in August 2021 as a single from Jungle's third album, Loving in Stereo. The British group started in 2013 when London producers Josh Lloyd-Watson and Tom McFarland teamed up, and they release their music on their own label, Caiola Records.

title: Busy Earnin'
fact: Jungle is the London duo Josh Lloyd-Watson and Tom McFarland, who have been friends since age nine when they lived next door to each other in Shepherd's Bush. They kept their identities secret when the project started in 2013.

title: CANDLE FLAME (feat. Erick The Architect)
fact: "Candle Flame" was the lead single from Jungle's 2023 album Volcano, built around sped-up, soul-pitched vocal samples meant to capture the fire and passion of early love. The guest verse comes from Erick the Architect of the rap group Flatbush Zombies, whose energetic delivery added extra intensity to the track.

title: Happy Man
fact: "Happy Man" was released in May 2018 as a double single with "House in L.A." ahead of Jungle's second album, For Ever. The track later found a second life well beyond the album, turning up in an O2 phone commercial, Netflix's "Elite," and as the opening theme for Apple TV+'s "WeCrashed."

title: Heavy, California
fact: "Heavy, California" is actually from Jungle's second album, For Ever, released in September 2018 on XL Recordings, rather than the band's self-titled 2014 debut, which had been shortlisted for the Mercury Prize. The track was shared as a single in July 2018, one of the first tastes of the follow-up record.

title: I've Been In Love (feat. Channel Tres)
fact: Jungle's "I've Been In Love," featuring Channel Tres, comes from 2023's Volcano - bandmember Josh Lloyd-Watson has called it "the most honest record" Jungle has made, an extension of the group's long-running love for soul music.

title: Keep Moving
fact: "Keep Moving" was the lead single from Jungle's 2021 album "Loving in Stereo," premiering on BBC Radio 1's Annie Mac show before release. The band paired the disco-leaning track with a West Side Story-inspired music video, choreographed and directed alongside longtime collaborator Charlie Di Placido.

title: Talk About It
fact: 'Talk About It' comes from Jungle's 2021 album Loving in Stereo, which found the London duo expanding their sound with disco strings and hard-hitting percussion layered under their signature falsetto harmonies. The album broadened Jungle's collaborator list beyond the group's core writing team.

title: ENDLESS DEATHLESS
fact: "Endless Deathless" is the title track from Just Mustard's third album, which the Dundalk, Ireland band recorded together at Black Mountain studio near their hometown. The group - vocalist Katie Ball, David Noonan, Mete Kalyoncuoğlu, Rob Clarke and Shane Maguire - blends shoegaze noise with dance-leaning beats, a sound that later led to them supporting The Cure on a run of outdoor stadium shows.

title: WE WERE JUST HERE
fact: "WE WERE JUST HERE" is the title track from Irish band Just Mustard's third album, released in October 2025 and mixed by David Wrench, known for his work with FKA twigs, Frank Ocean, and Sampha. Its synth-driven, propulsive pulse has drawn comparisons to early New Order.

title: Neverender (starring Tame Impala)
fact: "Neverender" opens Justice's fourth album, Hyperdrama (April 2024), and features Kevin Parker of Tame Impala singing in falsetto. It won the Grammy for Best Dance/Electronic Recording, and Parker and the French duo also teamed up on the album's "One Night/All Night."

title: CAN'T STOP THE FEELING! (Original Song from DreamWorks Animation's "TROLLS")
No One
fact: "No One" was released in November 2023 as the lead single from Kacy Hill's fourth album, Bug (2024). Hill co-produced it with Bartees Strange and Aidan Spiro, blending folk-pop songwriting with airy harmonies.
