title: Army Dreamers
fact: "Army Dreamers" stood out on Kate Bush's 1980 album Never for Ever for being built around a hypnotic waltz rhythm, an unusual choice for a pop single. Released that September, it reached the UK Top 20. Its widely praised music video uses a visual trick in which the camera follows a young child who appears to age into a young adult within a single continuous shot.

title: Cloudbusting
fact: The famous "Cloudbusting" video, the second single from Bush's 1985 album Hounds of Love, was co-conceived by Bush and director Terry Gilliam and stars Donald Sutherland, already a major movie star from M*A*S*H and Ordinary People. Sutherland turned the role down multiple times and only agreed after Bush personally showed up at his door to ask him herself; since he couldn't get a work visa on short notice, he ended up filming it for free.

title: Deeper Understanding
fact: Kate Bush originally released "Deeper Understanding" on her 1989 album The Sensual World, built around a lonely character's relationship with a computer, with the chorus voice created using an early vocoder. When she re-recorded the song for 2011's Director's Cut, Bush had her then-12-year-old son, Bertie, provide the spoken "computer" voice instead.

title: Hello Earth
fact: Kate Bush recorded Hounds of Love (1985) in a 48-track studio she built in a barn behind her home near London. The choir on Hello Earth is the Richard Hickox Singers performing Tsintskaro, a Georgian folk song she first heard in Werner Herzog's film Nosferatu the Vampyre.

title: Running Up That Hill (A Deal With God)
Sat in Your Lap
fact: "Sat in Your Lap" was the first single from Kate Bush's 1982 album The Dreaming, released in June 1981, about 15 months before the album itself. It's built on a Fairlight CMI synthesizer, a Linn drum machine, and bamboo sticks that her brother Paddy Bush and the drummer swooshed from ten feet apart.

title: The Man With the Child in His Eyes
This Woman's Work
fact: Kate Bush wrote “This Woman's Work” for the 1988 film She's Having a Baby, matching her lyrics to a dramatic hospital scene the director had already sent her - it's sung from the perspective of a partner realizing how much he loves her.

title: Wuthering Heights
fact: Kate Bush wrote "Wuthering Heights" in a single night after catching just the final ten minutes of a 1967 BBC adaptation of the Emily Bronte novel, before she'd even read the book. She insisted on it as her debut single over her label's preferred choice, and when it hit No. 1 in the UK in 1978, she became the first female artist to top the British chart with a self-written song.

title: Cool Dry Place
fact: "Cool Dry Place" is the title track from Katy Kirby's 2021 debut album, released via Keeled Scales Records. The song builds from a whisper-sung, stripped-down opening into a sweeping folk-rock arrangement, with a deconstructed guitar solo that critics compared to Big Thief and Sandy (Alex G). Kirby has cited influences ranging from Leonard Cohen to contemporary indie-folk songwriters.

title: Table
fact: Katy Kirby has said "Table" is a lighthearted outlier on her 2024 album Blue Raspberry, serving almost as an epilogue to the record, and that she simply finds it fun to sing. Like several songs on the album, it carries an official co-write credit for her backing band, since Kirby felt their playing shaped the songs enough to earn them songwriting credit alongside her lyrics.

title: Kaeru no Tame ni Kane wa Naru (Staff Roll)
Higher
fact: "Higher" was the third preview single from Welsh producer Kelly Lee Owens' fourth album, Dreamstate, following "Sunshine" and "Love You Got." Owens described each single as another taste of the feeling within the album.

title: crawl
fact: Ken Park is the solo project of Liam Creamer, a San Diego native now based in New York who writes wistful, coming-of-age indie rock about the growing pains of chasing your dreams far from home. "Crawl" appears on his self-titled debut EP, released in February 2026 on TODO Records, built around an acoustic arrangement meant to evoke nostalgia mixed with optimism. Creamer has said it features some of the EP's most emotional vocal work.

title: shatter
fact: Ken Park's "Shatter" is the debut single from Liam Creamer's apartment-recording project - written when he was 17, blending '60s harmonies with '90s indie-rock haze from growing up on My Bloody Valentine, The Smashing Pumpkins, and The Beach Boys' Pet Sounds.

title: Black and Blue
fact: Kevin Hambrick is a Fort Wayne, Indiana musician who was a fixture of the city's indie rock scene through the 2000s and 2010s. "Black and Blue" closes Refill, Part 1 (2024), a collection of previously unreleased b-sides, demos, and other recordings from 2004 to 2014.

"100,000" appears on Kevin Morby's album Little Wide Open. Morby has said the song's guitar parts were inspired by Tom Verlaine's playing style, written together with frequent collaborator Meg Duffy, whom he describes as sharing a kind of "telepathic guitarmony shorthand."

title: A Night at the Little Los Angeles
Die Young
fact: Die Young is from Kevin Morby's 2026 album Little Wide Open (Dead Oceans). It grew out of a melody he wrote at a soundcheck in a small village in France in summer 2024 and finished in 2025.

title: I Have Been To The Mountain
fact: Kevin Morby's "I Have Been to the Mountain," from 2016's Singing Saw, is one of his most richly orchestrated songs - built around mariachi horns, an angelic choir, and psychedelic guitar, recorded with Sam Cohen in Woodstock, New York after Morby started writing on an old piano that came with a new house.

title: If You Leave And If You Marry
Miles, Miles, Miles
fact: This track comes from Kevin Morby's 2013 debut solo album, Harlem River, which he assembled after leaving his earlier bands Woods and The Babies, sending home demos to collaborators Justin Sullivan and Rob Barbato to help flesh out.

title: Parade
fact: "Parade" comes from Kevin Morby's 2014 album Still Life, and it works as a tribute to one of his musical heroes, Lou Reed, with a nod to Reed tucked into the lyrics. The album's title and cover art were actually borrowed from an art piece by Maynard Monrow called "Still Life with the Rejects from the Land of Misfit Toys," which gets referenced again in the song's closing lines. The track features a small chorus of guest singers alongside Morby and was produced by Rob Barbato.

title: PBJ
fact: Kevin Morby's "PBJ" reunited him with producer Aaron Dessner of The National, joined by Justin Vernon of Bon Iver on guitar and Andrew Barr on drums. The title comes from a phrase a friend told him - calling driving with the windows down while blasting the AC "Peanut Butter Jelly" - that he's never been able to verify anyone else has heard before.

title: Sucker In The Void (The Lone Mile)
The Jester, The Tramp & The Acrobat
fact: "The Jester, The Tramp & The Acrobat" opens Kevin Morby's 2014 sophomore album Still Life, released on Woodsist Records. The song leans on circus and performance imagery, framing itself as one of several traveling, larger-than-life characters who recur throughout the record.

title: The Dark Don't Hide It
album: Farewell Transmission / The Dark Don't Hide It

title: A Love International
fact: "A Love International" was the lead single from Khruangbin's fourth album, A La Sala (April 2024, Dead Oceans), whose title means "to the room" in Spanish. The trio recorded the album with no outside collaborators besides their engineer Steve Christensen, and the video was directed by Scott Dungate.

title: August 10
fact: "August 10," from Khruangbin's 2018 album Con Todo El Mundo, is a reworking of "August 12," the very first song the Houston trio ever wrote. To create it, the band listened to the original backwards, learned to play that reversed version, and recorded it roughly six years after the original, making it a deliberate piece of connective tissue between their first and second albums.

title: Camo me quieres
fact: The song, properly titled "Como Me Quieres," comes from Khruangbin's 2018 album Con Todo el Mundo. Bassist Laura Lee based it on a running exchange with her grandfather, who would ask her "Como me quieres?" ("How do you love me?") and only accept one answer -- "Con todo el mundo" ("With all the world") -- which also became the album's title.

title: Connaissais de Face
fact: Connaissais de Face first appeared on Khruangbin's album Mordechai. The Texas trio later reworked it as Connaissais de Face (Tiger?), a collaboration with Ginger Root, on their 2024 album A La Sala.

title: Evan Finds the Third Room
fact: "Evan Finds the Third Room" appears on Khruangbin's 2018 album Con Todo El Mundo. Its title nods to scholar Homi K. Bhabha's "third space" theory, describing a space where different cultures blend into something new. The band later released a dub version of the track titled "A La Sala," Spanish for "to the living room."

title: Mr. White
fact: 'Mr. White' is the instrumental opening track on Khruangbin's 2015 debut album, The Universe Smiles Upon You. With no lyrics beyond a looping, whispered 'white cat, white cat,' the Houston trio lets the song's smoky, jazz-lounge groove do all the talking. Fans have long pointed out the title's nod to Harvey Keitel's character in Reservoir Dogs, fitting for a band that builds instrumental worlds out of cinematic atmosphere.

title: So We Won't Forget
fact: 'So We Won't Forget' appears on Khruangbin's 2020 album Mordechai, which marked a shift for the Texas trio toward songs with prominent lead vocals after years of largely instrumental music. It was one of the first Khruangbin tracks to put singing so clearly in the spotlight.

title: Time (You and I)
fact: Khruangbin's album Mordechai is named after a friend of bassist Laura Lee Ochoa who once encouraged her to jump off a waterfall - the feeling of that leap stuck with her, including on “Time (You and I),” a song about wishing you had more time with the people you love.

title: White Gloves
fact: 'White Gloves' appears on Khruangbin's 2015 debut, The Universe Smiles Upon You, recorded in a remote barn in the Texas countryside. The Houston trio takes its name from the Thai word for 'airplane' (literally 'engine fly'), a tribute to the 1960s-70s Thai funk records that first drew guitarist Mark Speer and drummer DJ Johnson together before bassist Laura Lee joined. That global, crate-digging influence runs through the band's whole catalog.

title: White Gloves ii
album: The Universe Smiles Upon You ii

title: Death Fantasy (Ft. Miguel)
fact: "Death Fantasy" is the third track on Kilo Kish's 2022 album American Gurl, featuring a guest vocal from Miguel and a music video directed by Dave Laven. The New York Times described its mood as more of a trance-like spell than a straightforward hook. The collaboration went well enough that Kilo Kish and Miguel teamed up again in 2025 for the song "Negotiate."

title: Nobody Loves You More
fact: "Nobody Loves You More" is the title track of Kim Deal's debut solo album (November 2024), which she wrote and recorded over about a decade. It brings together current and former members of The Breeders, including her sister Kelley Deal, and its final sessions were at Steve Albini's Electrical Audio studio in Chicago.

title: NOT TODAY
fact: Not Today was the lead single from Play Me (Matador, March 2026), Kim Gordon's third solo album. Justin Raisen produced it, as he did her Grammy-nominated 2024 album The Collective, but this time the sound leans on krautrock-style repetition.

title: Play Me
fact: The title track of Kim Gordon's 2026 album Play Me opens the record with a 1990s-inspired hip-hop beat and a horn section. Like her prior solo album The Collective (2024), Play Me was produced by Justin Raisen.

title: 21st Century Schizoid Man (including Mirrors)
album: In the Court of the Crimson King

title: The Court of the Crimson King (including The Return of the Fire Witch and The Dance of the Puppets)
album: In the Court of the Crimson King

title: Alien Metal
fact: Alien Metal comes from PetroDragonic Apocalypse, King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard's 24th studio album - a thrash-metal record released on 13 different vinyl variants, and the first half of a planned "yin and yang" pair with their album The Silver Cord.

title: Crumbling Castle
fact: Crumbling Castle's home album, Polygondwanaland, was released by King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard under an open license with the master tapes posted online for free - inviting fans and small labels to press and remix it however they liked. Hundreds of different fan-made editions exist, including a K.K. Slider-style Animal Crossing tribute pressed on vinyl.

title: Cyboogie
fact: King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard's "Cyboogie" appears on 2021's Butterfly 3000, an album that began as loops of arpeggiated modular synthesizers before being reworked into dream-pop songs - it was also the first King Gizzard album released on the band's own label, KGLW, rather than through Flightless Records.

title: Fishing for Fishies
fact: King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard's title track "Fishing for Fishies" is a warped nursery rhyme against recreational fishing - when asked what inspired the 2019 album's title, Stu Mackenzie simply wrote, "hunting makes me sad." Its music video, directed by Jason Galea, has the band floating on a raft past an alligator playing electric piano.

title: Gondii
fact: Gondii is on King Gizzard's 2022 album Ice, Death, Planets, Lungs, Mushrooms and Lava. The band recorded most of it in about a week, improvising with only a tempo, a key signature and a title to start each day. The name refers to the parasite Toxoplasma gondii.

title: Ice V
album: Ice, Death, Planets, Lungs, Mushrooms and Lava

title: Iron Lung
album: Ice, Death, Planets. Lungs, Mushrooms and Lava

title: Mars For The Rich
fact: Mars for the Rich is from Infest the Rats' Nest (2019), King Gizzard's first full-on metal project, released between their microtonal and jam-heavy albums to show off how many styles the Australian band works in.

title: Paper Mache Dream Balloon
fact: King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard recorded almost all of their 2015 album Paper Mache Dream Balloon inside an empty shipping container on a family farm in country Victoria, Australia, trading their usual heavy psych-rock gear for nylon-string guitars, clarinet, double bass, cello, and hand drums. The title track is about turning troubles into something else entirely -- frontman Stu Mackenzie has described it as daydreaming your worries onto an imaginary balloon and letting them float away.

title: People Vultures
fact: "People-Vultures" is one of nine tracks on King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard's 2016 album Nonagon Infinity, which was built so every song flows seamlessly into the next and the final track loops right back into the first, letting the whole record play forever without a break. The song's music video shows the band members merging into a giant "Person-Vulture" character who tangles with other creatures pulled from the album's other tracks.

title: Shanghai
fact: "Shanghai," written by Stu Mackenzie and Ambrose Kenny-Smith, appears on King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard's 2021 album Butterfly 3000. The track is built around hypnotic synth loops and Kenny-Smith's falsetto verses before the band stretches it into an extended jam on the main riff, a staple of their live shows.

title: The River
fact: "The River" opens King Gizzard & The Lizard Wizard's 2015 album Quarters!, clocking in at exactly 10 minutes and 10 seconds to match the record's concept of four equal-length tracks. Built in a non-standard 5/4 time signature inspired by Dave Brubeck's "Take Five," the song moves through a jazzy, improvisational structure, and its parts were pieced together in unusual locations, including harmonica recorded in a touring van and vocals cut in a rented London rehearsal room.

title: Vegemite
fact: "Vegemite" is a tongue-in-cheek 2014 single by Australian band King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard, written and produced by frontman Stu Mackenzie as a two-and-a-half-minute ode to the salty Australian breakfast spread. It was released as a promo tie-in to the band's fourth studio album, Oddments, put out the same year on their own Flightless label.

title: Yours
fact: King Gizzard & the Lizard Wizard's "Yours," written by frontman Stu Mackenzie, opens 2021's Butterfly 3000 - a bright synth-pop turn for the famously genre-hopping band, built around the simple idea of finding comfort and security in another person.

title: Seaforth
fact: King Krule's saxophonist Ignacio Salvadores joined the band after Archy Marshall spotted him playing sax under a bridge in East London, and the Argentine multi-instrumentalist became a key collaborator on 'Seaforth.' The song was the atmospheric lead single from 2023's Space Heavy, produced by Dilip Harris with King Krule's longtime touring band of Salvadores, George Bass, James Wilson and Jack Towell.

title: Landline
fact: King Tuff's "Landline," from 2026's MOO, was recorded entirely on his Tascam 338 tape machine - the same one he used on his very first album, Was Dead, years earlier.

title: Sun Medallion
fact: King Tuff (Kyle Thomas) has said "Sun Medallion" grew out of a dream and centers on a small charm he once bought at a hospice thrift store that he felt carried real power. The psychedelic pop song is loosely set in his hometown of Brattleboro, Vermont.

title: Twisted On A Train
fact: "Twisted on a Train" is the lead single and opening track from King Tuff's 2026 album MOO, which Kyle Thomas recorded himself in Vermont on the same vintage Tascam 388 tape machine he used for his breakthrough album Was Dead. Every copy of MOO even comes packaged with a handmade mini-newspaper called The Daily Moo.

title: Philosophize In It! Chemicalize With It!
I Was Made for Lovin' You
Pure Michigan
fact: Pure Michigan is a single from Blowin' Up, the fourth album from Canadian band Kiwi Jr. (August 14, 2026). Singer Jeremy Gaudet said he'd been trying to write a song about the Detroit-Windsor border for a couple of years, and it got finished once the band booked studio dates in Detroit.

title: Baby Dee
fact: Konk were a New York new-wave/disco outfit formed by avant-garde jazz musician Dana Vlcek, active in the city's vibrant early-'80s downtown dance-punk scene alongside acts like ESG, Liquid Liquid, and Bush Tetras. "Baby Dee," co-written by Vlcek and the band, later resurfaced on the compilation The Definitive Collection.

title: Elephant
fact: Konk were a New York dance band active from 1980 to 1988, blending disco, funk, Afrobeat, and post-punk alongside downtown-scene peers like ESG and Liquid Liquid. 'Elephant' was a highlight of their club sets at legendary venues like Paradise Garage and Danceteria, and it later resurfaced on the 2004 retrospective compilation The Sound of Konk.

title: MC's Act Like They Don't Know
99 BPM
fact: Kurt Vile's “99 BPM” is a nostalgic nod to playing in bands with a friend named Rob back around 2012 - “99 BPM, well, what's that between friends?”

title: Another good year for the roses
Baby's Arms
fact: 'Baby's Arms' opens Kurt Vile's 2011 album Smoke Ring for My Halo, recorded with producer John Agnello. The gentle, fingerpicked acoustic arrangement led critics to compare Vile's delivery to a young Leonard Cohen or Nick Drake. It's a comfort-and-solace song, setting a softer tone before the record's rockier tracks kick in.

title: Chance to Bleed
fact: Chance to Bleed is a single from Kurt Vile's tenth studio album, Philadelphia's Been Good to Me (May 29, 2026, Verve Forecast). Vile started the album in late 2023 and recorded much of it in his basement studio, with guest vocals on the song from Natalie Hoffman, Ethan Buckler and Greg Cartwright.

title: Chazzy Don't Mind
fact: The title nods to "Chazzy," a nickname for the Seattle band Chastity Belt, whose singer Julia Shapiro provides guest vocals on the track. Vile has said Courtney Barnett introduced him to Chastity Belt's music while touring together, and he wanted the band on his 2022 album (watch my moves) after connecting with their lyrics. The song blends Vile's laid-back guitar style with Shapiro's deadpan delivery.

title: Feel My Pain
album: it's a big world out there

title: Mount Airy Hill (Way Gone)
fact: Kurt Vile named "Mount Airy Hill (Way Gone)" after the quiet, tree-lined Philadelphia neighborhood where he lives, which he's described as the place that makes him feel "completely calm." He recorded the song, from his 2022 album (Watch My Moves), in OKV Central, the home basement studio he finished building just before the pandemic began.

title: One Trick Ponies
fact: Kurt Vile's "One Trick Ponies," from 2018's Bottle It In, opens with an egg shaker, a countdown, and Vile blurting "ohhh, shit" once the beat kicks in - Barack Obama later named it one of his favorite songs of the year.

title: Rock o' Stone
fact: "Rock o' Stone" appears on Kurt Vile's 2026 album Philadelphia's Been Good to Me, which he recorded at his home studio, OKV Central, in the Mount Airy neighborhood of Philadelphia. Vile has described the record as his way of "bringing it all back home to Philly."

title: Speed of The Sound of Loneliness
Timing Is Everything (And I'm Falling Behind)
Zoom 97
fact: "Zoom 97" opens Kurt Vile's tenth studio album, Philadelphia's Been Good to Me (May 2026), and was recorded at his home studio in Philly's Mount Airy neighborhood. It takes its inspiration from Lincoln Drive, the winding road through the area, with Mikel Patrick Avery on drums and Jesse Trbovich on background vocals.

title: Can't Get You out of My Head
5 to 8 Hours a Day (WWwaG)
fact: L'Rain's "5 to 8 Hours a Day (WWwaG)," from 2023's I Killed Your Dog, is Taja Cheek's meditation on the discipline artistic work demands - the title nods to the hours-a-day grind of actually making music, folded into her usual blend of R&B, jazz, noise, and pop.

title: elmyra
fact: L'Rain is Brooklyn musician Taja Cheek, who got her start hosting DIY noise shows in her own basement, with acts like TV on the Radio's Kyp Malone stopping by. Her stage name is a tribute to her mother, Lorraine.

title: Pet Rock
fact: "Pet Rock" comes from L'Rain's 2023 album I Killed Your Dog, released through Mexican Summer. Brooklyn multi-instrumentalist Taja Cheek, who records as L'Rain, has described the hazy, guitar-driven track as "a morose ode to the white dad rock I never listened to." It's built on bright, twisting guitar lines under her serene, fuzzed-out vocals.

title: soulless cycle
fact: 'soulless cycle' served as the lead single for L'Rain's Fata Morgana, which she's described as the closing chapter of a four-album arc that started with her self-titled 2017 debut. The track was co-produced with Ben Chapoteau-Katz and leans into the record's blend of gospel, dancehall and tape-loop textures.

title: The Lines
fact: "The Lines" is a 2025 single from L.A. Witch's album DOGGOD, marking a shift toward colder post-punk and darkwave textures. Guitarist Sade Sanchez used chorus and flanger pedals along with vintage string machines like the Solina and Roland VP330 to get the track's wiry, European-leaning sound. Its music video features ASL interpreter and dancer Lark Detweiler signing out different meanings of the word "lines."

title: Strange World
fact: "Strange World" was the first single from La Luz's album News of the Universe (May 2024), their first for Sub Pop. It opens with a murky, distortion-drenched guitar riff over pitter-pattering toms.

title: City Of Angels
fact: "City of Angels" was released in October 2022 as the first single from Ladytron's 2023 album Time's Arrow, the band's first new music since 2019. Band member Daniel Hunt explained the song is "about forgetting... how fragile it is," blending imagery of different cities into one rather than describing any single real place.

title: Car Anymore
fact: Lala Lala's "Car Anymore" opens her 2026 album Heaven 2 with a saxophone cameo from fellow Chicago musician Sen Morimoto.

title: DIVER
album: I Want The Door To Open

title: Does This Go Faster?
fact: Lala Lala is the project of Chicago singer-songwriter Lillie West, and "Does This Go Faster?" arrived as her first song after signing to Sub Pop. It was co-produced by West and Melina Duterte of Jay Som, with Abby Black on drums and Sen Morimoto adding saxophone. West wrote the swirling, synth-driven track while traveling alone in Iceland, after putting her belongings in storage and stepping back from her old life to figure out what came next.

title: Even Mountains Erode
fact: Even Mountains Erode is track 2 on Lala Lala's 2026 album Heaven 2 (Sub Pop). Lillie West played almost everything on the record herself, working with co-producer Melina Duterte, who records as Jay Som.

title: Newcastle
fact: Lankum's 'Newcastle' is their take on a centuries-old English folk tune first published in The English Dancing Master back in 1651. The Irish band learned their version from musician Sean Fitzgerald, who was taught it by his mother as a child, and it appears on their 2023 album False Lankum.

title: Kiss Me on the Floor
fact: "Kiss Me on the Floor" was released as a single in 2023 and appears on Laraw's 2024 album Quarter Life Crisis via Bravo musique. It was written by Lara Rawadi (Laraw) and Matt Kahane and produced by Quinton Sung and Laraw.

title: Collect Call
fact: "Collect Call" was the lead single from Last Dinosaurs' 2022 album From Mexico With Love, a record guitarist Lachlan Caskey wrote entirely on his own while living in Mexico during the pandemic, separated from his Brisbane bandmates. The band chose "Collect Call" as the first single by group vote because it felt like the rockiest, most upbeat way to reintroduce themselves.

title: Cower
fact: 'Cower' is by Latchkey Kids, a band formed by three friends -- Hanny, Joey, and Cyle -- in New Brunswick, New Jersey, who bonded over a shared love of bands like The Menzingers and Pinegrove. The song appears on their 2026 album Year of Summers.

title: (We Don't Need This) Fascist Groove Thang
Daft Punk Is Playing At My House
fact: Daft Punk Is Playing at My House was recorded in 2003-04 at Long View Farm in Massachusetts and Plantain Recording House in New York, produced by DFA. It became LCD Soundsystem's biggest single, earning a Grammy nomination for Best Dance Recording and reaching number 29 on the UK chart.

title: Dance Yrself Clean
fact: LCD Soundsystem's "Dance Yrself Clean" opens 2010's This Is Happening with nearly nine minutes of slow build - it starts as a stripped-down, muttering groove before exploding into a full synth-pop eruption around the three-minute mark. Kid Cudi later sampled it for his song "All Talk."

title: I Can Change
fact: LCD Soundsystem's James Murphy co-founded the influential label DFA Records in 2001 - the initials jokingly stood for "Death From Above" - before launching LCD Soundsystem itself the following year.

title: new body rhumba
fact: 'New Body Rhumba' was LCD Soundsystem's first new song in five years, written specifically for the soundtrack of Noah Baumbach's 2022 film White Noise. Frontman James Murphy, who had previously scored Baumbach's films Greenberg and While We're Young, wrote and produced the track with drummer Pat Mahoney and keyboardist Nancy Whang.

title: New York I Love You But You're Bringing Me Down
fact: "New York I Love You But You're Bringing Me Down" closes LCD Soundsystem's 2007 album Sound of Silver, and it was also the final song the band played at its original farewell concert at Madison Square Garden in 2011. Sound of Silver itself is dedicated to Dr. George Kamen, a New York psychiatrist and longtime friend of frontman James Murphy, and the album earned the band a Grammy nomination for Best Electronic/Dance Album.

title: you wanted a hit (electric lady sessions)
x-ray eyes
fact: "x-ray eyes" was LCD Soundsystem's first new song since 2022's "New Body Rhumba," first heard on an NTS Radio show before its official release in late 2024. James Murphy wrote it with bandmates Al Doyle and Nancy Whang, and it was pressed on a limited-edition 12-inch with a "trash can dub" remix.

title: Phanta
fact: Phanta is from Le Tigre's 1999 self-titled debut album. The trio reunited in 2022 to play their first show in over a decade, and the song has found new fans through fan-made TikTok videos.

title: Guzzle Blood
fact: "Guzzle Blood" opens Les Savy Fav's 2024 album OUI, LSF, their first in 14 years, and was its second single. It's an urgent rocker with bursts of horns on the choruses and frontman Tim Harrington delivering his lines in clipped, half-rapped bursts.

title: Earthy
fact: "Earthy" opens Lia Ices' 2021 album Family Album, starting with just Ices on solo piano before blooming into a psych-Americana jam midway through. The record was produced by JR White of the band Girls, and the "Earthy" video was shot entirely on Super 8 film by Conor Hagen.

album: They Threw Us All in a Trench and Stuck a Monument on Top

album: They Were Wrong, So We Drowned

album: They Threw Us All in a Trench and Stuck a Monument on Top

title: It Will Get Worse
fact: "It Will Get Worse" is the lead single from Ripped and Torn, the 2025 debut album by Chicago trio Lifeguard — Asher Case, Isaac Lowenstein, and Kai Slater. It's a fast, d-beat-driven punk track recorded with producer Randy Randall of the band No Age, capturing the energy of the house-party scene the band came up playing in.

title: Old Town Road (feat. Billy Ray Cyrus)
I Want To Be You
fact: "I Want To Be You" is a single from Lime Garden's debut album One More Thing (February 2024, So Young Records), produced by Ali Chant. Singer Chloe Howard says it came from a memory of being 14 at her first gig and wondering whether she wanted to be like, or be with, someone on stage.

Empty Mansions
album: Time Will Wait for No One
fact: 'Empty Mansions' appears on Local Natives' 2023 album Time Will Wait for No One, the band's fifth record. It was recorded across a string of historic Los Angeles studios with producer John Congleton, during a stretch the band has described as a period of major life changes - some members becoming fathers, others moving through isolation and loss - which shaped the album's emotional highs and lows.

title: NYE
album: Time Will Wait for No One

title: Past Lives
fact: "Past Lives" was Local Natives' first new song in three years, arriving in 2016 as the lead single from their album Sunlit Youth following 2013's Hummingbird. Guitarist Taylor Rice said of the track, "The world is not static, it's made new over and over again."

title: When Am I Gonna Lose You
Not Dead Yet
fact: Not Dead Yet, released February 19, 2021, was Lord Huron's first new music since 2018's Vide Noir, and later appeared on their album Long Lost (May 21, 2021). The video shows the band performing with ghosts of musicians past on an old television set.

title: Hollywood Blvd.
fact: "Hollywood Blvd." was Loren Kramar's single announcing his signing to Secretly Canadian, an opulent '70s-style track with horns and bells about receiving a star on the Hollywood Walk of Fame. Kramar directed the video himself, casting comedian John Early as a Hollywood studio tour guide.

title: Feast of Tongues
fact: "Feast of Tongues" was the first new music from Los Campesinos! since 2017 and the lead single from their album All Hell (July 2024, Heart Swells), their first in seven years. It's track six on the album.

title: A Kiss to Build a Dream On
It's Been a Long, Long Time
When The Saints Go Marching In
Ain't Misbehavin'
album: Satch Plays Fats: A Tribute to the Immortal Fats Waller

title: Blue
fact: "Blue" was released in October 2023 as the first new music from the duo Loving (Jesse Henderson and David Parry) since their 2020 debut album If I Am Only My Thoughts. The band has said the song was discovered like an old photograph in a journal, with the blueness and dizziness of a new love.

title: Breakers
fact: The closest match in Low's catalog is 'Breaker,' the second track on their 2007 album Drums and Guns - the trio's first record to lean heavily on loops and samples. Built from synthetic percussion, handclaps, and Alan Sparhawk's jagged guitar skronk, it was recorded with Mimi Parker on drums and vocals and Matt Livingston on bass.

title: Dinosaur Act
album: Things We Lost In The Fire

title: Disappearing
fact: Low's "Disappearing" comes from 2021's Hey What, the Minnesota duo's only album recorded just as a two-piece - Alan Sparhawk and Mimi Parker's two vocals sit inside waves of distorted, roaring noise, produced by BJ Burton, who also helped shape Bon Iver's 22, A Million.

title: No Comprende
fact: "No Comprende" comes from Low's 2015 album Ones and Sixes, recorded with producer BJ Burton at Justin Vernon's (Bon Iver) April Base Studios, not far from the Duluth, Minnesota duo's home. The track pairs Alan Sparhawk's heavily distorted guitar with a slow build into a cavernous, atmospheric finale.

title: Sunflower
album: Things We Lost In The Fire
fact: "Sunflower" opens Low's 2001 album Things We Lost in the Fire, which the Minnesota trio recorded with famed engineer Steve Albini in Chicago before finishing touches were added back home in Minneapolis by Tom Herbers. The song is sung by married bandmates Alan Sparhawk and Mimi Parker, whose intertwined harmonies became one of the band's signature sounds.

title: Words
fact: Words opens Low's 1994 debut album, I Could Live in Hope. The band formed in Duluth, Minnesota around Alan Sparhawk and Mimi Parker, and critics filed their hushed, spare sound under the label slowcore.

title: Young Republicans
fact: Lower Dens' Jana Hunter formed the band in 2010 after realizing what she'd actually grown tired of wasn't touring - it was performing her old solo material live. Putting together a backing band for one last tour led straight into starting Lower Dens.

title: Faux Sweetness
fact: Lucid Express is a five-piece dream pop/shoegaze band from Hong Kong. "Faux Sweetness" comes from their second album, Instant Comfort, released via Kanine Records.

title: Promise Me
fact: Lucid Express is a dream-pop band from Hong Kong, and "Promise Me" is from their second album, Instant Comfort (2026). The music video, directed by Neo Yeung, was filmed over 24 hours during the 2025 Chinese New Year.

title: Car Wheels on a Gravel Road
album: Car Wheels on a Gravel Road

title: Jackson
album: Car Wheels on a Gravel Road

title: Right in Time
album: Car Wheels on a Gravel Road

title: When the Night Comes Falling from the Sky
First Time
fact: "First Time" appears on Lucy Dacus's third album, Home Video (2021), a song-by-song look back at her adolescence. Dacus has said she began writing it spontaneously while on a brisk walk, singing the melody to herself before it grew into a song about the rush of first love.

title: Fool's Gold
fact: Lucy Dacus wrote "Fool's Gold" right after hosting a New Year's Eve party, sitting alone in the quiet once every guest had gone home. Rather than being about a specific breakup, the song is more about the anxious overthinking that comes with a new year -- worrying you won't get where you hope to be, while still trying to trust that you will. It was released as a standalone single in 2019.

title: Going Going Gone
fact: "Going Going Gone," from Lucy Dacus's 2021 album "Home Video," features backing vocals from her boygenius bandmates Phoebe Bridgers and Julien Baker. The song looks back at an awkward teenage fling, fitting the album's larger theme of revisiting childhood and adolescence through old memories.

title: Hot & Heavy
fact: Lucy Dacus grew up in the Richmond, Virginia area, the daughter of a music teacher, and was writing her own songs by age eight. She later formed boygenius with fellow songwriters Phoebe Bridgers and Julien Baker, and the trio won two Grammys for their debut album.

title: I Don't Wanna Be Funny Anymore
Most Wanted Man
fact: "Most Wanted Man," from Lucy Dacus's 2025 album Forever Is a Feeling, is an upbeat love song dedicated to her boygenius bandmate Julien Baker, who also sings backing vocals on the track. The album was released March 28, 2025.

title: Nonbeliever
fact: 'Nonbeliever,' from Lucy Dacus's 2018 album Historian, is actually a splice of three separate songs she'd written at very different points starting in 2011. None of the individual versions felt complete on their own, so in 2016 Dacus realized what they had in common, cut them apart, and reassembled the best pieces into one finished song.

title: Planting Tomatoes
fact: Planting Tomatoes was Lucy Dacus's first new music of 2026, first released as a Record Store Day exclusive 7-inch in April before reaching streaming. She shot its lyric video herself in Tokyo.

title: Small
fact: Luisa Wilson is a Memphis-born, New York City-based singer-songwriter and multi-instrumentalist who graduated from NYU's Clive Davis Institute of Recorded Music, where she studied music production and songwriting. "Small," released in October 2024, was her debut single, blending her jazz-pop sound with R&B and Motown influences.

album: Inside Every Fig Is A Dead Wasp

album: Inside Every Fig Is A Dead Wasp

title: Shrug
album: Inside Every Fig is a Dead Wasp

title: Tom
fact: "Tom" appears on Lunar Vacation's album Everything Matters, Everything's Fire (September 2024, Keeled Scales), produced by Drew Vandenberg. Singer Gep Repasky originally named the song after Tom Schwartz of Vanderpump Rules, and the band, who grew up together as childhood friends, call Decatur, Georgia home.

title: Where is Everyone?
album: Inside Every Fig is a Dead Wasp

title: Here And Now
album: The Best of Luther Vandross... The Best of Love

title: Happy Now
fact: "Happy Now" comes from The Afterparty, which Lykke Li has called her sixth and possibly final studio album. She's described the song's sound as what you'd get "if ABBA and the Prodigy had a baby and it wouldn't stop crying", a pretty perfect summary of its mix of pop sweetness and jittery energy.

title: I Want to Help You Ann
fact: Boston garage-rock institution the Lyres recorded "I Want to Help You Ann" on December 21, 1981, releasing it in 1983 on the local Ace of Hearts label. The pulsing, tremolo-driven single helped revive vintage 1960s garage-rock sounds with a new punk-era energy, landed at number 24 on The Village Voice's Pazz & Jop critics' poll of that year's best singles, and was later covered on a 1998 single by the Chesterfield Kings.

title: For Beginners
fact: "For Beginners" is the hushed opening track on M. Ward's 2009 album Hold Time. That same record also features a guest appearance from country legend Lucinda Williams, who joins Ward on a cover of Don Gibson's "Oh Lonesome Me."

title: Amnesia
fact: "Amnesia" comes from M83's 2023 album Fantasy, which Anthony Gonzalez made as a deliberate return to the guitar-and-synth energy of the band's 2005 breakout Before the Dawn Heals Us. Rather than building to one big explosion, the song is constructed as a patient slow-burn, blending M83's trademark cinematic scale with more spacious arrangements.

title: Blister Sunrise
fact: "Blister Sunrise" is the opening track on M83's tenth studio album, I Wrote You a Letter, released September 25, 2026. Frontman Anthony Gonzalez put the song out as the album's lead single three weeks earlier and recorded the record with collaborators Joe Berry, Clement Libes, and Benoit de Villeneuve. The track opens abruptly, almost as if starting mid-song, layering synths, percussion, and strings under distant-sounding vocals.

title: Don't Save Us From The Flames
Kim & Jessie
fact: Kim & Jessie was the third single from M83's 2008 album Saturdays = Youth, written by Anthony and Yann Gonzalez with Morgan Kibby. Pitchfork ranked it number 5 on its best songs of 2008 and number 256 on its Top 500 Tracks of the 2000s.

title: Lune De Fiel
fact: 'Lune de Fiel' comes from M83 mastermind Anthony Gonzalez's 2019 album DSVII, which he recorded entirely on analog synthesizers as an homage to vintage video game soundtracks and '80s sci-fi film scores. The song's music video forms the second chapter of 'Extazus,' a three-part black-and-white short film directed by French filmmaker Bertrand Mandico. It's a good example of M83's ongoing side career of pairing its music with ambitious visual storytelling.

title: Midnight City
fact: M83's “Midnight City” was inspired by late nights watching Downtown Los Angeles come alive, and ends with a now-iconic saxophone solo played by James King of Fitz and the Tantrums.

title: Oceans Niagara
fact: Oceans Niagara is a single from M83's 2023 album Fantasy, the project of French musician Anthony Gonzalez. It also has an accompanying short film.

title: Reunion
fact: "Reunion" was the second single from M83's 2011 double album Hurry Up, We're Dreaming, written by Anthony Gonzalez with Yann Gonzalez and Morgan Kibby, and produced by Gonzalez with Justin Meldal-Johnsen. Built on a yearning, 1980s-indebted guitar line and a driving drumbeat, the song uses imagery like a "lightning rod" to describe the joy of reconnecting with someone who feels renewing.

title: Run Into Flowers
album: Dead Cities, Red Seas & Lost Ghosts

title: Wait
fact: "Wait" is a shoegaze-leaning track from M83's 2011 double album Hurry Up, We're Dreaming, notably less electronic than the rest of the record, opening on acoustic guitar before building into cinematic, Sigur Ros-sized swells. It was released as the album's fifth single in December 2012 with a video directed by the duo Fleur & Manu.

title: We Own The Sky
fact: "We Own the Sky" comes from M83's fifth album, "Saturdays = Youth" (2008), a record the French project built as a tribute to 1980s teen movies and new-wave radio. It was released as a single in December 2008 following the album.

title: 20191009 I Like Her
fact: "20191009 I Like Her" is one of 199 tracks on Mac DeMarco's 2023 surprise release One Wayne G, a nearly nine-hour compilation of demos recorded between 2018 and 2023. True to the album's concept, every song is titled with the date it was made, so this one was recorded on October 9, 2019. It's one of the more fleshed-out, lyric-driven demos on a tracklist that's mostly instrumental sketches.

title: 20200817 Proud True Toyota
fact: Proud True Toyota is part of One Wayne G, a huge 2023 collection of Mac DeMarco's home recordings, and he has played it live at Webster Hall in New York. That same year he released Five Easy Hot Dogs, an instrumental album recorded on a road trip from Los Angeles to New York, with each song named for the place it was recorded.

title: A Wolf Who Wears Sheeps Clothes
fact: "A Wolf Who Wears Sheeps Clothes" is track nine on Mac DeMarco's 2017 album This Old Dog. The song takes the old fable of a predator disguised as something harmless and plays it almost literally, with DeMarco singing a gentle warning about not letting "the world outside the windowpane" get to your head. The album overall marked a more introspective turn for DeMarco, with songs reflecting on family and growing older.

title: Baby's Wearing Blue Jeans
fact: Baby's Wearing Blue Jeans is from Mac DeMarco's 2012 debut album, Rock and Roll Night Club.

title: Brother
fact: "Brother" comes from Mac DeMarco's 2014 album Salad Days, which he wrote, performed, and recorded entirely by himself in about a month at his small Brooklyn apartment. He tracked the whole record on a Fostex A-8 reel-to-reel tape machine rather than in a professional studio.

title: Chamber of Reflection
fact: Chamber of Reflection is the one Salad Days song where synths replace Mac DeMarco's usual chorused guitar; the lead synth is a Roland JX-3P. The title comes from a Freemasonry meditation room, which DeMarco compared to his home studio.

title: Goodbye Weekend
fact: "Goodbye Weekend" comes from Mac DeMarco's 2014 album Salad Days, which he recorded almost entirely by himself in about a month inside his Brooklyn apartment, right after a year and a half of near-constant touring. The track is one of the few on the record where DeMarco name-checks his own nickname, "Macky," and it closes with one of the album's more extended guitar solos.

title: Gualala
fact: "Gualala" opens Mac DeMarco's 2023 all-instrumental album Five Easy Hot Dogs, a record where each track is named for a town he passed through on an actual road trip up the California and Canadian coast, with songs recorded and mixed at each stop. The album's only vocal moment anywhere is DeMarco's spoken count-in at the very start of this opening track.

title: Heart to Heart
fact: From Mac DeMarco's 2019 album Here Comes the Cowboy, this breezy, laid-back track became his very first entry on the Billboard Hot 100, debuting at No. 98 — a quietly big milestone for an artist who built his following almost entirely outside the mainstream charts.

title: Holy
fact: Holy is from Mac DeMarco's 2025 album Guitar, which he recorded November 16-28, 2024 at his home studio in Los Angeles. He made the whole record himself, apart from mastering by David Ives, and filmed the Holy music video himself too.

title: My Kind of Woman
fact: 'My Kind of Woman' is the lead single from Mac DeMarco's 2012 sophomore album, 2, and is widely regarded as the record's standout, melodic peak. Unlike much of the album's loose, lo-fi style, the song leans into a warm, timeless pop sound that critics have compared to a modern indie-rock standard.

title: No Other Heart
fact: "No Other Heart" appears on Another One, a surprise eight-song mini-album Mac DeMarco wrote and recorded entirely on his own at his home studio in Far Rockaway, Queens, in just a few weeks in early 2015 — squeezed in between tour dates for his previous album, Salad Days.

title: Ode To Viceroy
fact: Mac DeMarco recorded his 2012 album 2, home to "Ode to Viceroy," entirely in his Mile End, Montreal apartment - by his own account, wearing nothing but his underwear the whole time.

title: Passing Out Pieces
fact: "Passing Out Pieces" appears on Mac DeMarco's 2014 album Salad Days, whose title borrows a phrase from Shakespeare's Antony and Cleopatra referring to a carefree youth. Behind its warm, dreamy synth-pop, the song turns into a wry self-critique of the touring musician's life, opening with a line about how time away from home took its toll on him.

title: Rock and Roll Night Club
fact: "Rock and Roll Night Club" is the title track of Mac DeMarco's debut EP, released in March 2012 through Captured Tracks. On it, DeMarco adopted an exaggerated, deep-crooning glam-rock voice as a kind of character performance, a slowed-down vocal style unlike his later, more familiar sound. The EP's reception convinced Captured Tracks to fund his first full-length album, "2," later that year.

title: Shining
fact: "Shining" opens Mac DeMarco's 2025 album Guitar, which he wrote and recorded entirely in his Los Angeles home studio over the course of just twelve days. The track introduces the high falsetto voice DeMarco leans on throughout the record, backed by light acoustic guitar and bass.

title: The Way You'd Love Her
fact: Released in 2015 as the first single from his mini-LP Another One, "The Way You'd Love Her" was written and recorded entirely by Mac DeMarco on his own at his home studio in Far Rockaway, Queens.

title: This Old Dog
fact: Mac DeMarco recorded 2017's This Old Dog using mostly just voice, acoustic guitar, synths, and a drum machine - a deliberately slower, moodier record than his earlier albums, made after he relocated from Queens to Los Angeles and let the songs marinate longer than usual.

title: Can't Hold Us ft. Ray Dalton
Don't Do Me Good (feat. Kacey Musgraves)
Fatal Optimist
fact: 'Fatal Optimist' is the title track of Madi Diaz's follow-up to her acclaimed 2023 album Weird Faith. Diaz has described 'fatal optimism' as the hope you keep choosing even knowing a relationship might not work out - the willingness to be vulnerable despite the risk. It's framed as something of a flip side to the hopeful love songs on Weird Faith.

title: Feel Something
fact: "Feel Something" is the lead single from Madi Diaz's album Fatal Optimist, released on ANTI- and co-produced with Gabe Wax. Diaz has described the record as the closing chapter of a loose trilogy that began with 2021's History of a Feeling and continued on the Grammy-nominated Weird Faith.

title: Nervous
fact: Madi Diaz was homeschooled in rural Pennsylvania, where her woodworker father taught her piano starting at age five. After Berklee and years as a Nashville songwriter, she later joined Harry Styles' touring band on guitar and backing vocals.

title: Worst Case Scenario
fact: "Worst Case Scenario" was released in October 2024 as a new track on the deluxe edition of Madi Diaz's album Weird Faith. Diaz described the song as coming from a habit of coping with anxiety by mentally rehearsing the worst possible outcome in advance, as a way to feel prepared for whatever might happen. The track is a gritty indie-folk song built around her conversational, diary-like lyrics.

A Song From Under the Floorboards
fact: Magazine's 1980 single was inspired by Fyodor Dostoevsky's novella 'Notes from Underground,' with the title drawing on a more literal translation of the book. It was produced by famed Manchester producer Martin Hannett and released on Virgin Records ahead of the album The Correct Use of Soap. Simple Minds (who toured with Magazine in 1979) later covered the song, and Morrissey recorded his own version as a B-side in 2006.

title: #1 Best Of All Time
fact: "#1 Best of All Time" is a single from Mamalarky's 2025 album Hex Key, a fast, high-energy track that plays with the idea of competitiveness and betting on yourself even when the odds feel stacked against you. It followed the band's 2022 album Pocket Fantasy and helped introduce the more amped-up sound of Hex Key.

title: Anhedonia
fact: Mamalarky singer Livvy Bennett and drummer Dylan Hill actually met back in middle school band class, and they'd already been making music with multi-instrumentalist Michael Hunter since high school by the time the group came together in Austin. Bassist Noor Khan joined later after Bennett put out a call for a bassist on, of all places, Tinder. Even the band's name came from a word-association game: roommates jotted down random words while the group jammed, and "Mamalarky" just stuck.

title: Feels So Wrong
fact: "Feels So Wrong" was the second single Mamalarky released after signing to Epitaph Records, a laid-back, sunny track leaning into 1970s AM-radio and yacht-rock textures reminiscent of Steely Dan. Bandleader Livvy Bennett wrote it around the idea that the things meant to make us feel good often bring less meaning than confronting what's actually hard. It appears on the band's 2025 album Hex Key.

title: Banana Ghost
fact: "Banana Ghost" appears on Six Demon Bag, the 2006 sophomore album by Philadelphia experimental rock group Man Man, led by singer/keyboardist Ryan Kattner under the stage name Honus Honus. Six Demon Bag's carnival-esque blend of clattering percussion and theatrical vocals was what first pushed the band, formed in Philadelphia in 2003, into extensive national touring.

title: Simple Math
fact: Manchester Orchestra's "Simple Math" is the title track from their 2011 concept album, framed by frontman Andy Hull as "two dueling conversations - me and my wife, and me and my God." It was recorded across multiple studios in Nashville and Atlanta between August and December 2010.

fact: Cursive is from Mandy, Indiana's second album, Urgh (Sacred Bones, February 2026). The English-French noise band's 2023 debut, i've seen a way, was recorded in unusual spaces including caves, crypts and shopping malls.

Myrtle
fact: Mary in the Junkyard's “Myrtle” is named for a comforting turtle character - “Myrtle told me that I don't need to worry” - part of a concept album imagining the singer's past life as a fisherman.

title: New Muscles
fact: 'New Muscles' by mary in the junkyard was written on accordion, and the lyrics are about as low-stakes as it gets -- bandmate David joining a gym. The music video, though, is no joke: bandmates Clari Freeman-Taylor and Saya Barbaglia spent a full year training in Muay Thai so the fight scene in the video could be real. It's a single from the London trio's debut album, Role Model Hermit.

Teardrop
fact: Teardrop features vocals by Elizabeth Fraser of the Cocteau Twins, who also wrote the lyrics. The band had reportedly planned a Madonna vocal, but took a vote and went with Fraser. It later became the opening theme of the TV series House.

title: Unfinished Sympathy
fact: For "Unfinished Sympathy," from 1991's Blue Lines, producer Johnny Dollar brought in arranger Wil Malone to record a 40-piece orchestra at Abbey Road Studios. The orchestral session cost so much that Massive Attack had to sell one of their vehicles, a Mitsubishi Shogun, to help cover the bill.

title: Unwell
album: More Than You Think You Are

title: Bonnet Of Pins
fact: "Bonnet of Pins" is the lead single from Matt Berninger's second solo album, Get Sunk (2025), his first solo release since 2020's Serpentine Prison. Recorded with producer Sean O'Brien, the song builds from driving drums and guitars into a burst of horns and choral backing vocals under Berninger's baritone, with the album featuring guest contributions from musicians including Booker T. Jones and Meg Duffy of Hand Habits.

title: Walking On A String
fact: Matt Berninger and Phoebe Bridgers recorded this for the Netflix film Between Two Ferns: The Movie, and it became the first single from Berninger's 2020 solo debut Serpentine Prison, which was produced and arranged by Booker T. Jones. Berninger, the National's singer, has jokingly called it "a love song between a spider and a moth."

album: Right Back Where We Started From

title: Be My Angel
fact: "Be My Angel" appears on Mazzy Star's 1990 debut album, She Hangs Brightly. The band was formed in Santa Monica, California, around Hope Sandoval and David Roback, who had previously played in other Paisley Underground-scene bands including Rain Parade and Opal. The album blended dream pop, psychedelic rock, and folk influences and was first released on Rough Trade before being picked up by Capitol Records.

title: Flowers in December
fact: "Flowers in December" was the lead single from Mazzy Star's 1996 album Among My Swan, written by Hope Sandoval and David Roback and produced by Roback. It became the band's only UK Top 40 single, reaching No. 40, and its music video was directed by Kevin Kerslake.

title: Split Myself in Two
fact: "Split Myself in Two" is a fast, cowpunk-flavored track from Meat Puppets' influential 1984 album Meat Puppets II on SST Records. Clocking in at just over two minutes, it shows the Arizona trio still channeling the hardcore-punk energy of their earlier records even as they branched into country and psychedelia.

title: Time Baby III
fact: "Time Baby III" is a special version of Medicine's song recorded for the 1994 film The Crow's soundtrack, featuring guest vocals from Cocteau Twins singer Elizabeth Fraser (a different version, "Time Baby II," appears in the film itself). The Los Angeles shoegaze band, led by guitarist Brad Laner, got its distinctive tone by running guitars through a Yamaha 4-track recorder.

title: Carried Away
fact: Carried Away is from the Montreal band Men I Trust's album Equus Caballus. The trio formed in 2014 around Emmanuelle Proulx, Jessy Caron and Dragos Chiriac, and this song even nods to hair-metal influences.

title: I Come With Mud
fact: "I Come With Mud" opens Men I Trust's 2025 album Equus Asinus, from the Quebec City trio. The song begins with roughly ninety seconds of simple, repeated guitar chords before Emma Proulx's whispery vocals enter, setting a pastoral, Romantic-poetry-style tone — full of imagery about love and nature — that carries through the rest of the record.

title: Help I'm Alive
fact: "Help I'm Alive" is the breakout single from Metric's 2009 album Fantasies, written by Emily Haines and James Shaw and recorded in Austin, Texas. It made Metric the first fully self-released act to crack the Top 20 of the US Alternative radio chart, a landmark for the Toronto band's independent, DIY approach. Fantasies went on to win the 2010 Juno Award for Alternative Album of the Year.

title: Victim Of Luck
fact: "Victim of Luck" opens Metric's tenth studio album and reflects frontwoman Emily Haines's idea that you can be just as destabilized by sudden good luck as by bad luck. The band recorded it at Electric Lady Studios with producer Gavin Brown.

title: Light Your Way Home
fact: METZ's "Light Your Way Home," from their 2024 album Up on Gravity Hill, features guest vocals from Amber Webber of Black Mountain. Guitarist Alex Edkins has said it was one of his favorite tracks to write, citing bands like Jesu and Low as sonic inspirations, and that Webber's vocal turn took the song "to another stratosphere."

title: All We Ever Wanted Was Everything
Dancing in Babylon ft. Christine and the Queens
Flash Delirium
fact: 'Flash Delirium' was recorded for 2010's Congratulations with producer Pete Kember (aka Sonic Boom, formerly of Spacemen 3) and mixed by David Fridmann. MGMT had initially planned to release no singles at all from the album to keep it a unified listening experience, but ended up putting this track out as a free download before its single release.

title: I Found a Whistle
fact: MGMT's Andrew VanWyngarden and Ben Goldwasser met as freshmen at Wesleyan University and made their first recordings in Goldwasser's dorm room. The band was originally called The Management, later shortened to MGMT after learning another band already had that name.

title: Kids
fact: "Kids" started life years before "Oracular Spectacular" — Andrew VanWyngarden and Ben Goldwasser first played an early version back in 2003 as Wesleyan University students, cycling it through two self-released EPs before producer Dave Fridmann helped them re-record it (a semitone lower) for the 2007 album.

title: Time To Pretend
fact: MGMT first recorded Time to Pretend on a college laptop with cheap Radio Shack microphones. Producer Dave Fridmann re-recorded it for 2007's Oracular Spectacular at Tarbox Road Studios, speeding it up slightly and adding live drums while keeping much of the original recording.

All Alone (On My Own)
fact: Michael Rault started out self-releasing CD-Rs as a teenager in Edmonton, Alberta, playing in bands with names like the Nightshades before going solo with a sound built on 1960s and 70s psych-pop.

title: Switch Up
fact: "Switch Up" is Beastie Boys member Mike D's debut solo single, and the first new music from anyone in that group since 2011. The track actually started as a home-studio experiment with his sons, Davis and Skyler Diamond, who record together as the duo Very Nice Person, with additional production from Carter Lang. Mike D even premiered the song live, dropping it online while he was still on stage at a sold-out LA show.

title: B A D I D E A
fact: "B A D I D E A" was the lead single from Militarie Gun's second album, God Save the Gun (October 2025). Revolver reports that frontman Ian Shelton wrote it at the last minute, originally intending it for a hardcore record Doja Cat was planning.

title: Spilling Ink
fact: "Spilling Ink" is a single from Los Angeles alt-rock band MILLY's album Your Own Becoming, released via Dangerbird Records. Frontman Brendan Dyer said the band set out to write their fastest song yet, resulting in a track that rips through its riff and chorus in about two minutes.

I Felt Like

title: Political Song for Michael Jackson to Sing
Forget
fact: "Forget" appears as a bonus track on CD reissues of Mission of Burma's 1982 debut album, Vs. The band later reused the title for Forget, a 1988 compilation on Taang! Records gathering demos and outtakes the group recorded between 1979 and 1982, offering an early look at the band's pre-Vs. sound.

title: That's How I Escaped My Certain Fate
That's When I Reach for My Revolver
fact: Mission of Burma bassist Clint Conley wrote and sang "That's When I Reach for My Revolver" for the band's 1981 EP Signals, Calls and Marches. It found a huge second audience in 1996 when electronic artist Moby covered it as the first single from his album Animal Rights. Moby even recorded an alternate, radio-friendly vocal take so MTV would air the video, retitling that version "That's When I Realize It's Over."

title: Trem Two
fact: "Trem Two" appeared on Mission of Burma's 1982 debut album Vs., released on the Boston indie label Ace of Hearts Records, and was also issued as its own single. The album captured the chaotic energy of the band's live shows, leaning on tape-manipulation effects from member Martin Swope. Ahead of release, The Boston Phoenix praised the track, writing that it "sounds like the creation, destruction, and rebirth of the universe in four minutes."

title: Fireproof
fact: Mitski's "Fireproof" isn't actually a Mitski original — it's her cover of One Direction's song, recorded as a bonus track for the 2026 10th-anniversary deluxe reissue of Puberty 2. She swaps the boy-band original's soft acoustic strum for her own signature wall of fuzzed-out distortion.

title: First Love-Late Spring
fact: Mitski has said “First Love / Late Spring” came from falling in love at a moment when she really couldn't afford to. The song describes crying like a “tall child” - looking like an adult while feeling as overwhelmed as a kid.

title: Geyser
fact: "Geyser" is the opening track and lead single from Mitski's 2018 album Be the Cowboy. Mitski has called it "one of my vaguest songs," explaining she wrote it about the sacrifices -- of relationships, opportunities, even health -- that come with committing to a music career, with the song's slow musical build mirroring its title.

title: I'll Change for You
album: Nothing's About To Happen To Me
fact: Mitski's "I'll Change for You," the second single from 2026's Nothing's About to Happen to Me, came from wanting to write "a song about being pathetic" - channeling the irrational urge to beg an ex to take you back, in Mitski's own words.

title: If I Leave
album: Nothing's About to Happen to Me
fact: "If I Leave" is track four on Mitski's 2026 album Nothing's About to Happen to Me and came out as a single the same day as the album (February 27, 2026, Dead Oceans). Jared Hogan directed the video, which shows Mitski and her band performing in an abandoned house.

title: Lightning
album: Nothing's About to Happen to Me
fact: "Lightning" is the eleventh and final track on Mitski's eighth studio album, Nothing's About to Happen to Me, released in February 2026.

title: My Body's Made of Crushed Little Stars
fact: "My Body's Made of Crushed Little Stars" is track seven on Mitski's 2016 album Puberty 2, written and recorded with longtime producer Patrick Hyland at Acme Studios in New York. At under two minutes, the folk-punk track has remained a staple of her live setlists, including her Be the Cowboy tour.

title: My Love Mine All Mine
album: The Land Is Inhospitable and So Are We
fact: My Love Mine All Mine, with country-flavored piano and pedal steel, was the third single from Mitski's 2023 album The Land Is Inhospitable and So Are We. It became her commercial breakthrough: her first Billboard Hot 100 entry, peaking at number 26, and it reached number 8 in the UK.

title: Nobody
fact: Mitski spent her childhood moving between countries including Turkey, China, Malaysia, and the Democratic Republic of Congo because of her father's work with the U.S. State Department, before eventually studying music composition at SUNY Purchase.

title: Remember My Name
fact: "Remember My Name" is pure "Be the Cowboy" economy — Mitski and longtime producer Patrick Hyland pack the song's stadium-size drums and biting guitar hook into just two minutes and fifteen seconds, true to the album's philosophy of never overstaying a song's welcome.

title: Star
album: The Land Is Inhospitable and So Are We
fact: "Star" was co-written by Mitski and her longtime producer Patrick Hyland for her 2023 album The Land Is Inhospitable and So Are We, released as one of two singles on August 23, 2023. Its grand, twinkling arrangement was partly built from layers of organ parts painstakingly programmed into MIDI, with Mitski citing minimalist composer Terry Riley's repetitive style as an inspiration. She has said the song served as the album's guiding "North Star" while writing the rest of the record.

title: That's Our Lamp
fact: "That's Our Lamp" closes out Mitski's 2022 album Laurel Hell, written by Mitski and her longtime producer Patrick Hyland, who also produced the whole record. When asked to sum up the final track in three words, Mitski answered: "Carnival, happy, goodbye."

title: Two Slow Dancers
fact: "Two Slow Dancers" closes out Mitski's 2018 album Be the Cowboy, picturing two former sweethearts reuniting years later for one last dance in a high school gymnasium. It's one of the quieter, more stripped-down moments on a record otherwise built around a tightly wound, controlled persona Mitski created for the album. Critics singled it out as among the most affecting songs of her career.

title: Washing Machine Heart
fact: "Washing Machine Heart," from Mitski's 2018 album Be the Cowboy, is one of the shortest songs on the record at just over two minutes. Producer Patrick Hyland has said the track almost didn't make the album at all. Its black-and-white music video, directed by Zia Anger and funded by Tidal, was released that November.

title: Where's My Phone?
album: Nothing's About to Happen to Me

title: Why Didn't You Stop Me?
fact: From 2018's Be the Cowboy, this song is about the regret of walking away from a relationship and then wishing your partner had fought to keep you there. It also plays with the unreliability of memory, as the narrator searches for an old photo where her ex looks the way she remembers him.

title: Working for the Knife
fact: Working for the Knife was released October 5, 2021 on Dead Oceans as the lead single from Mitski's sixth album, Laurel Hell (February 4, 2022). It was her first major release since a hiatus that followed 2018's Be the Cowboy, and in the video she ceremonially discards a cowboy hat.

title: Dancing In The Club
album: Box for Buddy, Box for Star Deluxe
fact: "Dancing in the Club" is MJ Lenderman's cover of a song by This Is Lorelei (Nate Amos), recorded with Amos's help in late 2024 and released on the 2025 deluxe edition of Amos's album Box for Buddy, Box for Star. Where the original is an upbeat synth-pop tune, Lenderman reworks it into a slower, twangy, acoustic version that became a regular part of his live sets.

title: Joker Lips
fact: "Joker Lips" was released as the second single from MJ Lenderman's 2024 album Manning Fireworks, his first for ANTI- Records. Its music video, directed by Ben Turok, features Lenderman and his backing band, The Wind, performing on an overgrown North Carolina hillside.

title: Just Be Simple
fact: Just Be Simple is MJ Lenderman's cover of a Songs: Ohia song, recorded for the tribute album I Will Swim to You: A Tribute to Jason Molina. It was released as a preview in September 2025 and pressed on a limited 7-inch on January 23, 2026.

title: You Don't Know The Shape I'm In
fact: "You Don't Know the Shape I'm In" appears on MJ Lenderman's 2024 album Manning Fireworks, which topped several year-end best-of lists. Its title nods to The Band's classic "The Shape I'm In," and the finished track features clarinet from Shane McCord after going through several reworked versions in the studio. Lenderman walked through the song's evolution from demo to final recording in an episode of the podcast Song Exploder.

title: You Have Bought Yourself a Boat
Cinderella
fact: "Cinderella" was released in February 2025 as the lead single announcing Model/Actriz's sophomore album, Pirouette, following their breakout 2023 debut Dogsbody. The New York post-punk band, fronted by vocalist Cole Haden, dialed back some of their noisier tendencies on the track in favor of sleeker, club-ready grooves.

title: Doves
fact: "Doves" is a single from Model/Actriz's 2025 album Pirouette, which the band recorded across three studios -- Machines with Magnets in Pawtucket, Rhode Island, and The Cutting Room and Studio G in New York City -- with production by Seth Manchester. Much of the record was written while the band was on tour in 2023, and drummer Ruben Radlauer has said the techno and house music they were listening to on the road seeped into the album's sound.

title: Apple Cider, I Don't Mind
fact: Modern Baseball split songwriting duties down the middle between co-frontmen Jake Ewald and Bren Lukens, and "Apple Cider, I Don't Mind" is one of Lukens's tracks from the band's 2016 album Holy Ghost. Critics noted it as a stylistic departure, an anthemic, post-rock-tinged song blending The Cure's atmospheric melodies with the widescreen guitar sound of U2's Joshua Tree era.

Burch has said the song is about feeling the full spectrum of emotions and using that sensitivity as fuel for something positive. It marked her first new release after a run of quieter, more subdued records.

title: Fishbrain
fact: "Fishbrain" is the seventh track on Mount Kimbie's 2024 album The Sunset Violent, the duo's first record made as a full four-piece band. The album also features London artist King Krule as a guest vocalist on two other tracks.

title: Shipwreck
fact: "Shipwreck" started as one of the earliest instrumental demos Mount Kimbie wrote for their 2024 album The Sunset Violent, and it became a core thread running through the record. The album arrived seven years after the duo's previous full-length, 2017's Love What Survives, and "Shipwreck" was released as a single ahead of it.

title: Rang Tang Ring Toon
fact: "Rang Tang Ring Toon" is track four on Mountain Man's album Magic Ship (September 2018, Nonesuch Records). Its official video was directed by D.L. Anderson and filmed in Orange County, North Carolina, and the trio's close vocal harmonies carry the song.

title: Sweet Young Thing Ain't Sweet No More
Return To Sender
fact: "Return to Sender" is a single from Brooklyn alt-rock band MX LONELY, released in January 2026 ahead of their debut album All Monsters, out via Julia's War Recordings. The band is made up of vocalist Rae Haas, guitarist Jake Harms, and bassist Gabriel Garman, and the track features driving rhythms and distorted guitars typical of their sound.

title: Honey Power
fact: "Honey Power" is on My Bloody Valentine's Tremolo EP (February 1991, Creation Records), which topped the UK Indie Chart. Kevin Shields later joked that the EP really had seven tracks, but they called it four because "you're not allowed to" do that, so three short pieces went unnamed.

title: Only Shallow
fact: "Only Shallow" opens My Bloody Valentine's notoriously painstaking 1991 album Loveless, whose recording was so drawn-out that engineer Alan Moulder left partway through to work with other bands before returning months later. Guitarist Kevin Shields has said he had to be kept lightly damp with a water mister during tracking just to stop static from ruining the recordings.

title: Slow
fact: "Slow" first appeared on My Bloody Valentine's 1988 EP You Made Me Realise, released the same year as their debut album Isn't Anything. Critics point to the track as proof of the band's reinvention away from the jangly C86 indie-pop sound of their earliest records, pushing toward the noisier, more intense style that would go on to help define shoegaze.

title: I Will Sing You Songs
fact: My Morning Jacket recorded It Still Moves, home to the nearly eight-minute I Will Sing You Songs, at Above the Cadillac Studios in rural Shelbyville, Kentucky - with the album's horn parts tracked separately at Memphis's famous Royal Studios.

title: Just Because I Do
fact: This harmonica-driven track appears on My Morning Jacket's 2001 album At Dawn, recorded at a studio set up in a Kentucky barn where frontman Jim James famously tracked vocals inside an old grain silo. The natural echo from that unusual setup became a signature of the band's early sound.

title: Love Love Love
fact: My Morning Jacket's Jim James recorded vocals for their early album At Dawn inside an abandoned grain silo on his family's Kentucky soybean farm, drawn to its natural reverb.

title: Lowdown
fact: 'Lowdown' comes from My Morning Jacket's 2001 sophomore album At Dawn and later turned up on the band's live album Okonokos. It's become a genuine setlist workhorse for the band, performed in concert well over 250 times.

title: Squid Ink
fact: "Squid Ink," from My Morning Jacket's 2025 album Is, grew out of a basement jam with drummer Patrick Hallahan, with frontman Jim James building the song around the image of negative energy filling a room "like a squid shooting ink into the water." It comes from the band's first album made with an outside producer, Brendan O'Brien, rather than James producing solo.

title: The Day Is Coming
fact: My Morning Jacket's "The Day Is Coming" comes from 2011's Circuital, the band's sixth studio album - a deliberate return to warmer, more live-sounding production after the heavily synthesized, dub-and-reggae-tinged detour of 2005's Z.

The synth-pop trio performed the song as musical guests on The Late Show with Stephen Colbert, filmed in an empty room at the Brooklyn venue Baby's All Right while waitstaff wandered through the shot.

fact: "Inept Apollo" is a single from Nation of Language's 2025 album Dance Called Memory, their first release since signing to Sub Pop. The Brooklyn trio built the track around layered analog synths and singer Ian Devaney's echoing vocals, continuing their run of records steeped in early-'80s New Wave acts like Kraftwerk.

title: Now That You're Gone
fact: "Now That You're Gone" is from Nation of Language's 2025 album Dance Called Memory, the band's full-length debut for Sub Pop. The track was recorded, produced, and mixed in New York by Nick Millhiser, a producer known for his work with LCD Soundsystem and Holy Ghost!, and mastered by Heba Kadry in Brooklyn.

title: September Again
fact: "September Again" is a synth-pop track from Nation of Language's 2020 debut album, Introduction, Presence. Frontman Ian Devaney and synth player Aidan Noell, who are married, funded part of the recording by asking wedding guests to contribute to a studio fund instead of giving traditional gifts, turning their reception into an unlikely album budget.

title: Tougher Than The Rest
fact: Nation of Language's version of Bruce Springsteen's Tougher Than the Rest came out in 2026 as a limited 7-inch on Sub Pop, pressed in just 1,000 copies. Singer Ian Richard Devaney says they used a Yamaha CS-80, the same synth model featured on Springsteen's 1987 Tunnel of Love sessions.

title: Weak In Your Light
fact: "Weak in Your Light" opens Nation of Language's 2023 album Strange Disciple and was recorded in East Williamsburg, Brooklyn, with producer Nick Millhiser, also known for his work in Holy Ghost!. Frontman Ian Devaney wrote and sang lead on the track, pairing yearning vocals with the band's signature bouncy, minimalist synth-pop sound.

title: You've Passed
fact: "You've Passed" is the second track on Neutral Milk Hotel's 1996 debut On Avery Island, produced by Robert Schneider of the Apples in Stereo as part of the lo-fi Elephant 6 recording collective. An alternate version, taped at frontman Jeff Mangum's father's house, later surfaced on a box set years afterward. Despite rarely being played live, it's frequently cited by critics as one of the best songs in the band's catalog.

title: Age of Consent
fact: "Age of Consent" opens New Order's 1983 album Power, Corruption & Lies and was recorded at Britannia Row Studios in London. Driven by Peter Hook's melodic bass line, it's often cited as the bridge between the band's roots in Joy Division and their new synth-pop direction. The song was originally slated for the Wayne's World 2 soundtrack, but when the film's producers couldn't afford the licensing fee, a studio-musician cover was used in the movie instead.

title: Bizarre Love Triangle
fact: Released in November 1986 from the album Brotherhood, "Bizarre Love Triangle" surprisingly never cracked the UK or US Top 40, peaking at just No. 56 in Britain, though it hit No. 4 on the US Dance/Disco club chart. Written and produced by all four band members, it's since been ranked among Rolling Stone's 500 Greatest Songs of All Time.

title: Dreams Never End
fact: "Dreams Never End" opens New Order's 1981 debut album Movement, and it's sung by bassist Peter Hook rather than the band's usual lead vocalist, Bernard Sumner. Hook's melodic, foregrounded basslines on this track became a blueprint for the sound that would carry New Order onto dance floors for the rest of the decade. Even the title is a callback to the band's earlier incarnation, echoing a lyric from the song "Insight."

title: Love Vigilantes
fact: Love Vigilantes opens New Order's 1985 album Low-Life and was recorded in 1984 at Jam and Britannia Row studios in London. It leans on melodica and shows the influence of American country and folk music, a shift as the band moved from post-punk toward dance-rock.

title: Regret
fact: "Regret" was the lead single from New Order's 1993 album Republic. It reached number 4 in the UK and number 28 on the US Billboard Hot 100, the highest chart placing of the band's career in both countries.

title: Sub-Culture
fact: "Sub-culture" was the second single from New Order's 1985 album Low-Life, released on the Manchester label Factory Records. For the single, producer John Robie reworked the album track into a more club-oriented, electronic version, and a later batch of 1986 Razormaid remixes added extra vocals from Deborah Iyall of the band Romeo Void.

title: The Perfect Kiss
fact: The music video for New Order's "The Perfect Kiss" was directed by filmmaker Jonathan Demme and simply shows the band performing the entire nearly 11-minute song live in their practice room. The band played live rather than miming, recording straight to 24-track tape, and the shoot was filmed by cinematographer Henri Alekan, who decades earlier had shot Jean Cocteau's Beauty and the Beast.

title: The Village
fact: 'The Village' appears on New Order's 1983 album Power, Corruption & Lies. Its title was inspired by the British TV series The Prisoner, though the band says any resemblance between the lyrics and the show's imagery was coincidental. It was also the first New Order song built around more than one sequenced bassline, showing off the studio technology the band leaned on heavily that year.

title: Your Silent Face
fact: "Your Silent Face," from New Order's 1983 album Power, Corruption & Lies, was written by Bernard Sumner as a tribute to Kraftwerk, carrying a melody reminiscent of the German electronic pioneers' work. Its original working title was simply "KW1," short for "Kraftwerk One," before the band gave it a proper name for release.

title: Unity
fact: 'Unity' is a track from Operation Ivy's sole studio album, Energy (1989). The Berkeley ska-punk band broke up that same year after barely two years together, but two of its members, Tim Armstrong and Matt Freeman, went on to form Rancid. 'Unity' became one of the band's most enduring songs - it's been covered by other bands over the years, and original singer Jesse Michaels reunited with Armstrong and Freeman to perform it live at San Francisco's Warfield Theatre in 2006.
