fact: "Light on Our Feet" appears on Snail Mail's 2026 album Ricochet, released via Matador Records -- her first full-length in five years. The violin-and-strings-laden ballad draws an orchestral comparison to Smashing Pumpkins' Mellon Collie and the Infinite Sadness, part of an album the band has described as preoccupied with how time moves and what it leaves behind.

title: My Maker
fact: Lindsey Jordan first played "My Maker" in Seattle while touring with Dinosaur Jr. in 2025. She calls it the starting point for Snail Mail's third album, Ricochet, and shot its video in a hot air balloon, mostly in one take, co-directed with Elsie Richter.

title: Valentine
fact: Snail Mail's Lindsey Jordan started classical guitar lessons at age five and was writing her own songs by 12. She first performed as Snail Mail at just 15 years old and was quickly hailed as a guitar prodigy.

title: Brand New City
fact: Snocaps is a band led by siblings Katie Crutchfield (Waxahatchee) and Allison Crutchfield, joined by MJ Lenderman and producer Brad Cook. Brand New City is from their self-titled 2025 album on Anti- Records.

title: Coast
fact: "Coast" is the lead single from the surprise debut album by Snocaps, a new project from twin sisters Katie Crutchfield (Waxahatchee) and Allison Crutchfield (Swearin'), released on Halloween 2025. The record was made with producer and multi-instrumentalist Brad Cook, with additional contributions from MJ Lenderman. The sisters made their television debut performing "Coast" on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon that November.

title: Heathcliff
fact: Snocaps is a band formed by twin sisters Allison Crutchfield (of Swearin') and Katie Crutchfield (Waxahatchee), along with MJ Lenderman and Brad Cook. "Heathcliff," the second track on their 2025 self-titled debut, was written and sung by Allison; the album was produced and almost entirely engineered by Cook, with all four musicians switching between instruments.

title: death valley fridge magnet
fact: "death valley fridge magnet" marked SOAK's (Bridie Monds-Watson) first solo single in more than four years, arriving on Rough Trade after a run that included a 2024 collaboration with Fred again.. Monds-Watson has said the song is really about leaning on friendship to find her way back to herself.

title: Abigail
fact: "Abigail," a single from Soccer Mommy's 2024 album Evergreen, is a sincere serenade to Abigail, a non-playable villager character from the farming video game Stardew Valley. Sophie Allison originally wrote it as a casual songwriting exercise but liked the result enough to include it on the finished record.

title: M
fact: "M," the second single from Soccer Mommy's 2024 album Evergreen, marks a stripped-back turn in her production compared to the more experimental sound of her prior record. The song builds from acoustic guitar into a lush string arrangement that closes out in an expansive, flute-led outro.

title: Out Worn
fact: 'Out Worn' was one of the new songs Sophie Allison added to Collection, her 2017 breakout mini-album of reworked bedroom-pop recordings. She's said the song is about feeling a need for validation in a relationship, and NPR's Songs We Love singled it out as an early sign of her growth as a songwriter.

title: Rings Of Saturn
fact: Soccer Mommy's "Rings of Saturn" was Sophie Allison's first new song in two years, produced by Elliott Kozel - she's said she wrote it during a hard stretch when she'd take a telescope out into the yard to look at the moon and planets, finding that feeling small could take some of the weight off.

title: yellow is the color of her eyes
Not Sorry
fact: Not Sorry is from When a Flower Doesn't Grow, the debut full-length album (January 2026) from Softcult, the Ontario band made up of twins Mercedes and Phoenix Arn-Horn. The video came out the same day as the album.

title: Pill To Swallow
fact: "Pill to Swallow" was the first single teasing Softcult's self-produced 2026 debut album, When a Flower Doesn't Grow. The Ontario sibling duo handle nearly everything themselves: Phoenix Arn-Horn produces and engineers while Mercedes Arn-Horn writes the songs and directs the band's music videos.

title: Shortest Fuse
fact: 'Shortest Fuse' comes from the 2024 EP Heaven by Softcult, the Canadian duo of twin sisters Phoenix and Mercedes Arn-Horn. Before forming Softcult in 2020, the twins fronted the pop-punk band Courage My Love. Softcult blends grunge, shoegaze, dream pop, and riot-grrrl influences, and true to their DIY ethic, the sisters write, produce, and engineer all of their own music.

title: In Orbit
fact: In Orbit was Son Little's first new music in three years when it arrived in 2025, and it later appeared as track 9 on his 2026 album Cityfolk. Critics described it as a blend of R&B and folk-pop.

title: Blue Chicago Moon
fact: Songs: Ohia's "Blue Chicago Moon" comes from 2002's Didn't It Rain, an album Jason Molina named after a traditional gospel song popularized by Sister Rosetta Tharpe and Mahalia Jackson - it was recorded by Edan Cohen at Soundgun Studios in Philadelphia.

title: Just Be Simple
fact: "Just Be Simple" appears on "Magnolia Electric Co." (2003), the last album Jason Molina released under the Songs: Ohia name before adopting Magnolia Electric Co. as his band's name for every record that followed. The spare, tenor-guitar-driven track is typical of Molina's intimate indie-folk arrangements.

title: Lioness
fact: "Lioness" is from Songs: Ohia's album The Lioness. Jason Molina recorded it at Chem19 Studio in Glasgow, Scotland, with his friends Aidan Moffat and David Gow of Arab Strap and Alasdair Roberts.

title: Trans Am (this time anything finite at all)

fact: The music video for Sonic Youth's "100%," the lead single from 1992's Dirty, was directed by Tamra Davis and Spike Jonze and shot around Los Angeles, with Jonze filming much of it from a skateboard. It features then-skateboarder (later actor) Jason Lee, and bassist Kim Gordon plays a yellow Fender bass borrowed from actor Keanu Reeves. The song became Sonic Youth's highest-charting single to that point, reaching No. 4 on Billboard's Alternative Airplay chart.

title: Bull in the Heather
album: Experimental Jet Set, Trash and No Star
fact: "Bull in the Heather" is the lead single from Sonic Youth's 1994 album Experimental Jet Set, Trash and No Star. Kim Gordon said the song is about "using passiveness as a form of rebellion," and its title borrows the name of a racehorse that won the 1993 Florida Derby. The Tamra Davis-directed video features a visibly pregnant Gordon dancing alongside Bikini Kill's Kathleen Hanna.

title: The Sprawl
fact: Sonic Youth's "The Sprawl," from 1988's Daydream Nation, takes its title from the sprawling fictional megacity - stretching from Boston to Atlanta - in William Gibson's cyberpunk novels. The album was the band's first double LP and their last for an independent label before signing to Geffen.

title: What We Know
fact: This driving rocker from 2009's The Eternal is one of only two Sonic Youth songs with guitarist Lee Ranaldo on lead vocals, the other being 'Walkin Blue.' Its guitar riff was written as a nod to Sonic's Rendezvous Band, the short-lived Detroit rock group formed by former MC5 guitarist Fred 'Sonic' Smith.

title: The Day I Tried to Live
Losing Touch With My Mind
fact: "Losing Touch With My Mind" opens Spacemen 3's 1986 debut album Sound of Confusion. It's built from a cycling wave of guitar feedback that gradually gets wrestled back into driving, classic garage-rock rhythm, setting the tone for the band's recorded career.

title: Falling in Love With Myself Again
fact: "Falling in Love with Myself Again" appears on Sparks' 1974 breakthrough album Kimono My House, written by Ron Mael and produced by Muff Winwood — former bassist of the Spencer Davis Group turned in-house producer for Island Records.

title: Girl From Germany
fact: "Girl From Germany" appears on Sparks' 1974 breakthrough album Kimono My House, recorded in London after Ron and Russell Mael relocated from Los Angeles and assembled an entirely new British backing band. Produced by Muff Winwood, the album shot to No. 4 on the UK charts and earned the Mael brothers their first gold disc.

title: Never Turn Your Back on Mother Earth
Something for the Girl With Everything
The Number One Song in Heaven
fact: Sparks' "The Number One Song in Heaven" was written and produced with Giorgio Moroder after the Mael brothers heard his production on Donna Summer's "I Feel Love" and decided to ditch their guitars for synthesizers - it became a UK top-20 hit and, in 1997, was re-recorded with vocals from Bronski Beat's Jimmy Somerville.

title: This Town Ain't Big Enough for Both of Us
fact: Sparks' breakout 1974 single began as brothers Ron and Russell Mael's idea to have Russell recite movie-dialogue clichés between verses; they ended up keeping only the title line. Producer Muff Winwood added the song's distinctive Western-movie gunshot sound effects during the Kimono My House sessions in London. The single reached #2 on the UK singles chart and introduced British audiences to the duo's theatrical performance style via an appearance on Top of the Pops.

title: Portrait of My Heart
fact: "Portrait of My Heart" is the title track and opener of SPELLLING's 2025 album of the same name, her follow-up to 2021's The Turning Wheel. Singer Chrystia Cabral said she used the song's propulsive drum groove and anthemic "I don't belong here" chorus to work through performance anxiety, opting for a tighter, more rock-oriented sound than her earlier material.

title: Sometimes
fact: "Sometimes" closes out SPELLLING's 2025 album Portrait of My Heart, and it's actually a cover of the My Bloody Valentine shoegaze classic. Where the original buries its vocals in a wash of guitar noise, Bay Area artist Tia Cabral (who records as SPELLLING) brings the melody to the forefront over a dancier, synth-driven arrangement.

title: I'll Believe in Anything (2026 Solo Piano Version)
fact: This solo piano take began at Spencer Krug's January 2026 set at Unreal City Fest in Vancouver, then was recorded at Risque Disque Records in Ladysmith, BC for release on Sub Pop. The original I'll Believe in Anything is from Wolf Parade's debut album, Apologies to the Queen Mary.

title: Could It Be I'm Falling In Love
Working My Way Back To You
I Got A Line On You

fact: "1/500" is a track from Spirit of the Beehive's 2024 album You'll Have to Lose Something, released on the Saddle Creek label. It was written by band members Zack Schwartz and Rivka Ravede, with additional performance from Corey Wichlin.

title: I'VE BEEN EVIL
fact: "I've Been Evil" appears on Spirit of the Beehive's 2024 album "You'll Have to Lose Something" (Saddle Creek), the Philadelphia band's first full-length written after its two founding members and co-vocalists, Zach Schwartz and Rivka Ravede, ended their real-life relationship. The pair kept writing and recording together anyway, channeling the aftermath into the record's hushed, steady guitar textures.

title: THE SERVER IS IMMERSED
fact: Spirit of the Beehive formed in Philadelphia in 2014 and took their name from a 1973 Spanish film of the same title. The band has restlessly reinvented its sound with nearly every release, from shoegaze to glitchy, vaporwave-tinged electronics.

title: Always Together With You
fact: "Always Together With You" opens Spiritualized's 2022 album Everything Was Beautiful with frontman Jason Pierce's young daughter Poppy announcing the record's title, followed by the same Apollo 11 radio-transmission sound effects that introduced the band's 1997 classic Ladies and Gentlemen We Are Floating in Space. It's a supercharged rework of a demo the band had floated around since 2014.

title: Always Together With You (The Bridge Song)
Best Thing You Never Had (The D Song)
Broken Heart
album: Ladies and Gentlemen We Are Floating in Space

title: Crazy
fact: "Crazy" is a track from Spiritualized's 2022 album Everything Was Beautiful, released on Fat Possum Records, and features backing vocals from American country singer Nikki Lane. It was the second song revealed to the public ahead of the album's release.

title: Electricity
album: Ladies and Gentlemen We Are Floating in Space
fact: "Electricity" was released as a single in July 1997 from Spiritualized's album Ladies and Gentlemen We Are Floating in Space (June 1997), which NME named its Album of the Year. The album features guests including the Balanescu Quartet, the London Community Gospel Choir, and Dr. John.

title: Here It Comes
fact: The full title of this Spiritualized song is "Here It Comes (The Road) Let's Go," the lead single from 2018's And Nothing Hurt. Frontman Jason Pierce has described its lyrics as essentially "a list of instructions that, if followed, allows the listener to find my house," turning directions home into a sweeping, horn-and-harmony-soaked anthem. It's one of the more uplifting, cosmic-country moments in the band's catalog.

title: Hey Jane
fact: "Hey Jane" is the nearly 10-minute lead single from Spiritualized's 2012 album Sweet Heart Sweet Light - essentially two songs stitched into one, complete with a fake ending partway through before it lurches into a completely different second half. Frontman Jason Pierce recorded the album piecemeal across studios in Wales, Los Angeles, Reykjavik, and London over roughly two years, then spent another full year mixing it alone at home.

title: I Think I'm in Love
album: Ladies and Gentlemen We Are Floating in Space

title: I'm Your Man
fact: 'I'm Your Man' is the second track on Spiritualized's 2018 album And Nothing Hurt. Unusually for a band known for lush, orchestral production, bandleader Jason Pierce recorded almost the entire album himself on a laptop in an upstairs room of his London home, teaching himself digital recording from scratch because there wasn't a budget for a proper studio. Despite the bedroom setup, he painstakingly layered strings and horns part by part to make the record sound as full as his earlier studio albums.

title: Ladies & Gentlemen We Are Floating in Space (I Can't Help Falling in Love)
album: Ladies and Gentlemen We Are Floating in Space
fact: Spiritualized's title track "Ladies and Gentlemen We Are Floating in Space" borrows its melody from both Pachelbel's Canon in D and Elvis Presley's "Can't Help Falling in Love" - the album opens with band member Kate Radley's flat, deadpan voice on a phone recording saying the title phrase. NME ranked the 1997 album its #1 record of the year, ahead of Radiohead's OK Computer.

title: Ladies and Gentlemen We Are Floating in Space
album: Ladies and Gentlemen We Are Floating in Space

title: Let It Bleed (For Iggy)
fact: "Let It Bleed (For Iggy)" is a sprawling, blues-tinged track from Spiritualized's 2022 album Everything Was Beautiful, released on Fat Possum Records, and is explicitly dedicated to Iggy Pop as a tribute to his lasting influence on bandleader Jason Pierce. It's built around Pierce's broader exploration of how music tries to communicate feelings that words alone can't fully express.

title: On The Sunshine
fact: "On The Sunshine" opens Spiritualized's 2018 album And Nothing Hurt, a record notable because Jason Pierce (J. Spaceman) made almost all of it alone in an upstairs room of his London home rather than a studio. Short on a label budget, he built the album's lush, orchestral sound himself on a laptop, sampling and strumming along to classical records note by note before bringing in session players to physically perform the parts. He only left home to track instruments too bulky to fake, like timpani.

title: Soul on Fire
fact: "Soul on Fire" was the first single from Spiritualized's sixth album, Songs in A&E, released in May 2008 on Sanctuary Records. The album blends art rock, neo-psychedelia, garage rock, and gospel.

title: The A Song (Laid in Your Arms)
All the Pretty Girls Go to the City
Can I Sit Next To You
Do I Have To Talk You Into It
Don't Let It Get You Down
Don't You Evah
fact: "Don't You Evah" is a cover of "Don't You Ever" by The Natural History, a New York indie band fronted by Max Tepper, a friend of Spoon's Britt Daniel. Because The Natural History's own album was delayed for contractual reasons, Spoon's version on Ga Ga Ga Ga Ga (2007) actually came out before the original recording.

title: Got Nuffin
fact: Spoon's Britt Daniel described “Got Nuffin” as being about having “nothing to lose but darkness and shadows” - a song about the relief of shaking off negative thoughts.

title: I Summon You
fact: "I Summon You," from Spoon's 2005 album Gimme Fiction, was performed for the Black Cab Sessions series, whose motto is "one song, one take, one cab" — filming artists playing a single song while riding in the back of a moving London taxi. The band stripped the song down to just guitar and vocals for that version, versus the added bass and drums on the album cut.

title: My Babe
fact: "My Babe" appears on Spoon's 2022 album Lucifer on the Sofa, the first record the Austin band tracked in its own hometown studios in more than a decade. It was co-produced by Spoon and engineer Mark Rankin, with additional contributions from Dave Fridmann and Justin Raisen. The song shifts from a wistful acoustic ballad opening into a punchier, full-band second half.

title: Rent I Pay
fact: 'Rent I Pay' was the lead single from Spoon's 2014 album They Want My Soul, and frontman Britt Daniel has said the title phrase, 'that's the rent I pay,' was an expression his brother used to say. Daniel knew the song was special the moment the band first played back the basic recorded track in their rental van after a day in the studio, recalling that it gave him chills.

title: The Ghost of You Lingers
fact: Spoon's "The Ghost of You Lingers," from 2007's Ga Ga Ga Ga Ga, leans into a Spaghetti Western sound - critics have compared its dramatic sweep to a Morricone score wrapped in lo-fi garage-rock grit.

title: The Way We Get By
fact: Spoon's 'The Way We Get By,' off 2002's Kill the Moonlight, ended up everywhere in film and TV — it soundtracked scenes in Stranger Than Fiction and The O.C., and later turned up in Shameless. Britt Daniel built the song around that insistent piano riff and handclaps, turning a scrappy indie single into one of the band's most licensed tracks.

title: WhisperI'lllistentohearit
fact: Despite how it looks on a cuesheet, "WhisperI'lllistentohearit" is the real title of a track from Spoon's 2017 album Hot Thoughts, written by Britt Daniel and produced by Dave Fridmann. It was recorded across three different studios in New York, Texas, and California, and shows off Spoon's trick of making just a couple of instruments sound like a full band.

title: You Got Yr. Cherry Bomb
fact: "You Got Yr. Cherry Bomb" is the third track on Spoon's sixth studio album, Ga Ga Ga Ga Ga, released July 10, 2007 on Merge Records and Anti- (it's sometimes mixed up with the earlier Kill the Moonlight, but it's a different record). The album clocks in at just over 36 minutes across ten tracks.

title: Condensation
fact: "Condensation" is a single from Sports Team's 2025 album Boys These Days. The six-piece English band has said the song is literally about sweat — written after two years away from touring, it was meant to capture the physical feeling of being in a packed room with a crowd again. Musically, it leans into a bigger, Britpop-influenced sound reminiscent of bands like Blur.

title: I'm In Love (Subaru)
fact: Sports Team's “I'm In Love (Subaru)” is a love song about a shiny red Subaru - a stand-in for an idealized, “sorted” adult life that, the song admits, can't actually be bought.

title: Descartes
fact: "Descartes" is the lead single from Irish band SPRINTS' sophomore album All That Is Over, released via Sub Pop and City Slang. Frontperson Karla Chubb flips philosopher Rene Descartes' famous "I think, therefore I am" into her own version, "I speak so therefore I understand," and has said the song was partly sparked by a line about vanity from Rachel Cusk's novel Outline.

title: Heavy
fact: Heavy is from Letter to Self (January 2024), the debut album by SPRINTS, a garage-punk band formed in Dublin in 2019. Critics described the record as sounding like PJ Harvey fronting the Pixies.

title: Rage
fact: "Rage" appears on All That Is Over, the 2025 sophomore album from Dublin band SPRINTS. Formed in 2019, the group is made up of Karla Chubb, Sam McCann, Jack Callan and Zac Stephenson, and the record was produced by Daniel Fox as a follow-up to their 2024 debut, Letter to Self.

title: Up and Comer
fact: "Up and Comer" is a track from Irish band SPRINTS' 2024 debut album Letter to Self. Frontwoman Karla Chubb has said the song confronts the imposter syndrome and self-doubt she's felt since she first picked up an instrument, wondering if she'd always just be considered "good for a girl" rather than great, and she channels that frustration into one of the album's most ferocious tracks.

title: Juno
fact: Spud Cannon formed at Vassar College in 2016 and went through several other names - including The Black Jeans and Paper Dots - before settling on Spud Cannon. Their album Squeeze climbed to No. 3 on the College Radio Top 200.

title: Thrum a Dum
album: Next Time Read The Fine Print

title: Building 650
fact: "Building 650" is from Squid's 2025 album Cowards. Drummer and vocalist Ollie Judge wrote it after the English band's first trip to Japan, which happened just days after pandemic travel restrictions lifted in 2022 — he's said he wrote the lyrics about the particular feeling of being a stranger in an unfamiliar country, inspired partly by reading Ryu Murakami's novel In the Miso Soup and watching Lost in Translation on the flight over. Its music video was filmed on location in Japan.

title: Crispy Skin
fact: "Crispy Skin" opens with a synth intro that nods to The Who's "Baba O'Riley" before Squid's jagged guitars take over. It's a single from their 2025 album Cowards, produced by longtime collaborator Dan Carey and featuring an unusually wide cast of guests, including Danish songwriter Clarissa Connelly, composer Tony Njoku, and the Ruisi Quartet on strings. The record was actually finished before the band's previous album, O Monolith, had even come out.

title: Paddling
fact: Squid's "Paddling," from 2021's Bright Green Field, was a longtime live staple years before its release - the band started writing it back when they were still teenagers living in Brighton, and it explores the tension between simple pleasures and modern consumerism through the lens of The Wind in the Willows.

title: Undergrowth
fact: "Undergrowth" was one of three advance singles from Squid's second album, "O Monolith" (2023). Much of the record was written during a stay in rural Wiltshire at Real World Studios, the residential studio complex founded by Peter Gabriel.

title: Not Me
album: Say a Prayer to the Gods of Getting Going
fact: Ella Williams, who records as Squirrel Flower, has said 'Not Me' came to her after waking from a dream while staying in Silver City, New Mexico. She's cited the book Women Who Run With the Wolves as an inspiration, particularly its message about not settling for less than what you truly want.

artist: Ssgt. Sadler Barry (U.S. Army Special Forces)
title: Ballad Of The Green Berets
Big Time Nothing
fact: "Big Time Nothing" comes from St. Vincent's 2024 album All Born Screaming, which was a milestone for Annie Clark as the first St. Vincent record she produced entirely on her own, following 2021's Daddy's Home. Critics described the track's mix of spoken-word verses giving way to a squelchy funk chorus as sounding like a mashup of U2 and INXS.

title: Broken Man
fact: "Broken Man" was the first single from St. Vincent's 2024 album All Born Screaming, the first record she produced entirely by herself. The rhythm section is stacked with session heavyweights: Foo Fighters' Dave Grohl and drummer Mark Guiliana both appear on drums, Justin Meldal-Johnsen plays bass, and David Ralicke adds saxophone.

title: Digital Witness
fact: Before going solo as St. Vincent, Annie Clark played in the Polyphonic Spree and later in Sufjan Stevens' backing band. She took her stage name partly from the New York hospital where poet Dylan Thomas died, and partly from her great-grandmother's middle name.

title: El Mero Cero
fact: "El Mero Cero" is a Spanish-language version of St. Vincent's "Big Time Nothing," one of several songs she re-recorded for Todos Nacen Gritando, a full Spanish-language companion to her 2024 album All Born Screaming. She made the companion record as a way of thanking her Latin American fans, releasing it about six months after the original English version came out.

title: Flea
fact: 'Flea' was the second single from St. Vincent's 2024 album All Born Screaming, and it features Foo Fighters' Dave Grohl on drums alongside bassist Justin Meldal-Johnsen. Annie Clark has said she sent Grohl the song specifically because of its twisting, prog-style tempo changes, figuring the part would be right up his alley. It's one of the heavier, more rhythmically unusual tracks on the self-produced record.

title: Laughing With a Mouth of Blood
Marrow
fact: "Marrow" appears on St. Vincent's 2009 album Actor. Annie Clark has said the song grew out of her love of The Wizard of Oz, wanting to write about a character wishing "they had a spine made of iron," and aiming for a sound that was as visual and Technicolor as it was musical, built from distorted guitars, horns, and fluttering woodwinds.

title: Northern Lights
fact: For the frenzied guitar solo on "Northern Lights," from 2011's Strange Mercy, Annie Clark (St. Vincent) used an unusual delay pedal called the Sitori Sonics Tapeworm, which has two built-in synth oscillators. It's considered one of the more inventive pedal choices on the record, which Clark recorded with longtime producer John Congleton in her hometown of Dallas.

title: Prince Johnny
fact: St. Vincent's "Prince Johnny," from her self-titled 2014 album, is a tribute to a real friend of Annie Clark's - a portrait of the kind of New York City nightlife scene where people who fled their hometowns come to reinvent themselves.

title: Rattlesnake
fact: Rattlesnake opens St. Vincent's self-titled 2014 album, and its big fuzzed-out solo was played on Annie Clark's signature Ernie Ball Music Man guitar.

title: Save Me From What I Want
The Melting Of The Sun
fact: 'The Melting of the Sun' appears on St. Vincent's 2021 album Daddy's Home, a record built around a warm, vintage '70s New York sound. The track features backing vocals from Kenya Hathaway, daughter of soul legend Donny Hathaway, alongside singer Lynne Fiddmont, and the band performed it on Saturday Night Live shortly after its release.

title: The Strangers
fact: 'The Strangers' opens St. Vincent's 2009 album Actor, which she wrote imagining it as a score for a movie that doesn't exist, drawing inspiration from Disney soundtracks and the opening-credits music of Woody Allen films. Pitchfork liked it enough to rank it among the best tracks of the entire 2000s decade.

title: Roadkill
fact: 'Roadkill' marked Starcrawler's first release after signing to Big Machine Records in 2022, and it came with a fun crossover credit: it was produced by Tyler Bates, the film composer behind the scores for Guardians of the Galaxy and John Wick. The track also found the LA glam-rockers leaning harder into punk territory than their earlier, more theatrical material.

title: Stuck In The Middle With You
Na Na Hey Hey Kiss Him Goodbye
Danny
fact: "Danny" is the lead single from Stef Chura's 2026 album Dancing Alone on the Concrete, her first LP in seven years. The horn-dusted, country-tinged track features a pretty unexpected guest pairing: R.E.M.'s Peter Buck and Mike Mills.

title: Scream
fact: Stef Chura is a Detroit indie-rock musician known for a distinctive vocal style that swings between a howl and a yodel. She taught herself to home-record after moving to Detroit in 2012 while studying at the College for Creative Studies.

title: The Concrete
fact: "The Concrete" is the title track of Stef Chura's 2026 album Dancing Alone on the Concrete, her first LP in seven years. It was recorded at Chase Park Transduction studio in Athens, Georgia, produced by Robert Schneider of the Apples in Stereo, and features guest contributions from R.E.M.'s Peter Buck and Mike Mills alongside Sugar's David Barbe.

title: Freeze The Saints
fact: "Freeze the Saints" comes from Stephen Malkmus's 2005 solo album "Face the Truth," which he built largely on his own — playing and overdubbing most of the instruments himself, from banjo to sitar, around sessions with his band the Jicks. The ballad has stuck around as one of his most frequently played live staples ever since.

title: Baltimore
fact: "Baltimore" is from Stephen Malkmus and the Jicks' 2008 album Real Emotional Trash and runs well over six minutes. Malkmus, the former Pavement frontman, has talked about the Baltimore references in its lyrics.

title: Gardenia
fact: "Gardenia" comes from Stephen Malkmus and the Jicks' 2008 album Real Emotional Trash on Matador Records, built around Malkmus's typically leftfield, jangly guitar-pop songwriting. It was also issued on its own as a 7-inch single.

title: Real Emotional Trash
fact: Stephen Malkmus and the Jicks' title track "Real Emotional Trash" stretches past ten minutes, built around an extended midsection of interlocking guitar solos - the album was recorded at SnowGhost Music in Whitefish, Montana, and Foxtrot Studio in Chicago.

title: Aerial Troubles
fact: "Aerial Troubles" marked Stereolab's return after a 15-year break, serving as the first single from their 2025 album Instant Holograms on Metal Film. The track rides a motorik beat from drummer Andy Ramsay, with a phaser-soaked guitar line from Tim Gane underneath Laetitia Sadier's harmonized vocals.

title: Come and Play in the Milky Night
album: Cobra and Phases Group Play Voltage in the Milky Night

title: Fed Up With Your Job
fact: "Fed Up With Your Job" is one of two songs Stereolab released together as a single in September 2025, following Instant Holograms on Metal Film, their first studio album in fifteen years. It arrived as a limited seven-inch vinyl pressing of just 3,000 copies, timed to coincide with the start of a 41-date North and South American tour.

title: French Disko
fact: "French Disko" started life as "French Disco," the closing track on Stereolab's 1993 EP Jenny Ondioline, before the band re-recorded and re-spelled it for a standalone double 7-inch single. Unexpected UK radio airplay pushed it to a co-billed chart entry at No. 75, the band's first-ever UK chart appearance, and it later placed No. 5 in John Peel's 1993 Festive Fifty listener poll.

title: Metronomic Underground
fact: "Metronomic Underground" is the eight-minute opening track of Stereolab's 1996 album Emperor Tomato Ketchup. Although its sound is often credited to producer John McEntire of Tortoise, the band actually recorded it before they went to Chicago to work with him.

title: Percolator
fact: "Percolator," from Stereolab's 1996 album Emperor Tomato Ketchup, rides an unusual 5/4 rhythm topped with vibraphone, angular strings, and a cartoonish analog synth, reflecting the band's love of 1950s/60s space-age "bachelor pad" pop. The album itself takes its title from a 1971 experimental film by Japanese director Shuji Terayama.

title: The Flower Called Nowhere
fact: Stereolab's "The Flower Called Nowhere," from 1997's Dots and Loops, was recorded in Dusseldorf with co-production from Andi Toma of Mouse on Mars - part of the album's shift toward denser electronic production, blending bossa nova rhythms with the band's usual avant-pop.

title: The Noise of Carpet
fact: 'The Noise of Carpet' was the second single from Stereolab's 1996 album Emperor Tomato Ketchup, sitting at the album's midpoint as a callback to the band's earlier, rawer sound. It's built on a fuzzed-out guitar riff closer to the Velvet Underground than Stereolab's usual style, layered with wordless backing vocals from Laetitia Sadier, Mary Hansen, and Morgane Lhote.

title: Three-Dee Melodie
fact: 'Three-Dee Melodie' opens Stereolab's 1994 album Mars Audiac Quintet, a record widely seen as the moment the band fully fused their love of lounge and exotica with their krautrock-indebted grooves and analog synthesizers. The album marked a turning point toward a more accessible, melodic sound while keeping the band's experimental edge intact.

title: Transmuted Matter
fact: Transmuted Matter is from Instant Holograms on Metal Film, released May 23, 2025 on Duophonic UHF Disks and Warp Records. It was Stereolab's first new album in 15 years.

title: Vermona F Transistor
fact: Vermona F Transistor is from Instant Holograms on Metal Film (2025), Stereolab's first studio album in almost 15 years. The track features backing vocals from Molly Hansen Read, niece of former Stereolab guitarist Mary Hansen, and its title nods to Vermona, a maker of analog synthesizers.

title: You Are The Sunshine Of My Life
Alternative Ulster
fact: Stiff Little Fingers formed in Belfast in 1977 out of a covers band called Highway Star, taking their new name from a song by English punk band the Vibrators. Their breakthrough single shares its title with Alternative Ulster, a Belfast punk fanzine started in 1977 by teenage writer Gavin Martin to chronicle the city's emerging punk scene. The song, released in 1978, became the band's signature anthem and anchored their debut LP, Inflammable Material.

title: Suspect Device
fact: "Suspect Device" was Stiff Little Fingers' debut single, recorded on 4 February 1978 in a Downtown Radio studio in Newtownards normally used for recording jingles. Belfast journalist Gordon Ogilvie wrote the lyrics and handed them to singer Jake Burns after the band's fourth-ever gig. The band released it themselves on their own Rigid Digits label, and after a copy reached John Peel, who played it repeatedly on air, Rough Trade signed on to distribute it, helping it sell over 30,000 copies.

title: Heal
fact: "Heal" is the title track of Strand of Oaks' 2014 album, which marked a dramatic stylistic turn for songwriter Timothy Showalter — away from his earlier folk-rooted Americana sound and into a heavier, '70s/'80s/'90s-inspired hard-rock style. The record was produced by John Congleton with engineer/synth player Ben Vehorn and drummer Steve Clements, and it was widely named among the best albums of 2014.

title: Keys
fact: "Keys," from Strand of Oaks' 2019 album Eraserland, is a love song frontman Tim Showalter wrote for his wife Sue, built from real conversations the two had about growing older together. Showalter has said the second chorus captures the only take he and his producer could get through without getting emotional.

title: Radio Kids
fact: 'Radio Kids,' the first single from Strand of Oaks' 2017 album Hard Love, is Tim Showalter's tribute to growing up in the '80s and '90s with a blank cassette loaded in the tape deck, waiting to record a favorite song off the radio. It captures that solitary ritual of music fandom while hinting at the wider community of fans doing the same thing all over the world.

title: Shut In
fact: Strand of Oaks' "Shut In" comes from 2014's HEAL, an album singer-songwriter Timothy Showalter wrote in a three-week creative burst during a period of personal turmoil - he came out of it with some 30 songs, trimmed down to the ten that made the record, with mixing by John Congleton.

title: Too Much Time On My Hands
A Little Lost

title: A Running Start
fact: A Running Start is a single from Sufjan Stevens' 2023 album Javelin, which he described as being about the exhilarating rush of first loves and first kisses set against the beauty of nature. Stevens played every instrument on the track himself, with additional vocals from Nedelle Torrisi, Hannah Cohen, and Megan Lui.

title: Age of Adz
fact: The title track of Sufjan Stevens' maximalist 2010 album The Age of Adz draws heavily on the prophetic, sci-fi-tinged visionary art of Royal Robertson, a self-taught Louisiana sign painter whose apocalyptic drawings Sufjan stumbled across and became fascinated with. That found artwork ended up shaping the record's whole cosmic, electronics-meets-orchestra sound.

title: Chicago
fact: Sufjan Stevens' "Chicago" comes from his 2005 concept album Illinois and has appeared in the films Little Miss Sunshine and Veronica Mars. He's recorded five different versions of the song over the years.

title: Concerning the UFO Sighting Near Highland, Illinois
Decatur, or, Round of Applause for Your Stepmother!
Eugene
fact: Eugene is track 5 on Sufjan Stevens' 2015 album Carrie & Lowell, which was recorded in several places including Portland, Oregon, Norman, Oklahoma and Eau Claire, Wisconsin. Some parts were even recorded on an iPhone in a hotel room in Klamath Falls, Oregon.

title: Flint (For the Unemployed and Underpaid)
fact: "Flint (For the Unemployed and Underpaid)" opens Sufjan Stevens' 2003 album Michigan, the first entry in his planned "50 states" project. The track begins with a spare, minimal piano line that carries most of the song, and an electric guitar only enters as a surprise about three minutes in to close things out. Stevens wrote, performed, and recorded nearly the entire album himself while working a day job in New York.

title: For the Widows in Paradise, For the Fatherless in Ypsilanti
Futile Devices
fact: "Futile Devices" opens Sufjan Stevens' 2010 album The Age of Adz with hushed piano and acoustic guitar, standing out as the gentle outlier on an otherwise glitchy, electronic record. The song had a second life too: Shigeto remixed it in 2012, and producer Doveman reworked it again in 2017 for the soundtrack of the film Call Me by Your Name.

title: Lonely Man of Winter (Doveman Mix feat. Melissa Mary Ahern)
fact: This track has a delightfully odd backstory. In 2007, Sufjan ran a holiday "Xmas Song Xchange" contest and ended up trading away the rights to his original "Lonely Man of Winter" to the winner, theater artist Alec Duffy, in exchange for Duffy's own homemade Christmas song. Duffy held private listening parties with cookies and hot chocolate for over a decade before finally releasing it properly in 2018 as this Doveman-produced version with Melissa Mary Ahern, with proceeds benefiting his Brooklyn arts nonprofit JACK.

title: My Rajneesh
fact: "My Rajneesh" was released in July 2020 as the B-side to a limited double-sided 12-inch vinyl single alongside "America," pressed to just 1,500 copies worldwide. Both tracks came from the same writing sessions that fed into Stevens's next album, The Ascension.

title: Mystery of Love
fact: Director Luca Guadagnino originally asked Sufjan Stevens to narrate his 2017 film Call Me by Your Name, but Stevens offered to write an original song instead, drawing on the film's script and the source novel. The result, "Mystery of Love," earned Stevens an Academy Award nomination for Best Original Song at the 2018 ceremony.

title: No Shade in the Shadow of the Cross
fact: "No Shade in the Shadow of the Cross" served as the lead single from Sufjan Stevens' 2015 album Carrie & Lowell, released digitally in February and then on a limited 7-inch through Joyful Noise Recordings. A neat production detail: the low static running through the track isn't manipulated tape hiss, but the actual sound of an air conditioner fan blasting on high in Stevens' apartment while he recorded.

title: So You Are Tired
fact: "So You Are Tired" was the lead single from Sufjan Stevens' 2023 album Javelin. The recording features a sizable cast of guest backing vocalists, including Bryce Dessner of the National, adrienne maree brown, Hannah Cohen, Pauline Delassus, Megan Lui, and Nedelle Torrisi, giving the song's back half a choir-like swell.

title: Tell Me You Love Me
fact: "Tell Me You Love Me" appears on Sufjan Stevens' 2020 album The Ascension, and its glimmering piano intro reworks a phrase from "Climb That Mountain," a track off his instrumental album Aporia. The song's music video was directed by filmmaker Luca Guadagnino, best known for Call Me By Your Name.

title: The Ascension
fact: The Ascension is the title track of Sufjan Stevens' 2020 album, a 15-song, roughly 80-minute record on Asthmatic Kitty. It marked a big shift to electronic sounds after the quiet acoustic Carrie & Lowell.

title: The Dress Looks Nice on You
The Man of Metropolis Steals Our Hearts
The Only Thing
fact: "The Only Thing" is a hushed, finger-picked highlight from Sufjan Stevens' 2015 album Carrie & Lowell. For this record, Stevens did something he rarely does -- he handed over co-production duties to pianist and arranger Thomas Bartlett. The track also features guitar from Casey Foubert and Ben Lester, and was mixed by Stevens, Bartlett, and Patrick Dillett.

Tonya Harding
fact: Sufjan Stevens wrote and released "Tonya Harding" to coincide with the 2017 biopic I, Tonya - he'd actually sent the song to the filmmakers first, but they weren't able to find a way to use it.

title: Will Anybody Ever Love Me
fact: This 2023 single from Sufjan Stevens' album Javelin was self-produced, with additional vocals from writer and activist adrienne maree brown, along with Hannah Cohen and Megan Lui. Its kaleidoscopic music video was animated by Stephen Halker, a longtime visual collaborator of Stevens.

title: With My Whole Heart
fact: Sufjan Stevens released "With My Whole Heart" alongside "Love Yourself" as a Pride Month single in 2019, with proceeds from companion T-shirts going to organizations supporting LGBTQ youth.

Dream Woman
fact: "Dream Woman" was Suki Waterhouse's first solo single after her album Memoir of a Sparklemuffin, released through Sub Pop in 2025. She co-wrote the track with Natalie Findlay, with production from Jules Apollinaire. Waterhouse kept the project in the family, tapping her sister Imogen Waterhouse to direct the music video, with another sister, Madeleine, working as cinematographer.

title: Good Looking
fact: Suki Waterhouse first released "Good Looking" through Sub Pop in 2017 as the lead single from her debut EP, Milk Teeth. The song found a second life five years later when it went viral on TikTok in 2022, eventually reaching No. 14 on the US Hot Rock & Alternative Songs chart and earning platinum certification in the US.

title: I Will Love You
fact: "I Will Love You" is a single by Riverside, California sister duo Summer Twins (Chelsea and Justine Brown), who formed in 2008 blending 1950s/60s girl-group and surf-rock harmonies with a dreampop haze. The song appears on their 2012 self-titled debut LP for Burger Records, and the band wrote, shot, and edited its own low-budget music video around their hometown of Riverside in February 2012.

title: You Go on Ahead
fact: "You Go on Ahead" is a direct sequel to "Trumpet Trumpet, Toot Toot!" from Sunset Rubdown's earlier album Random Spirit Lover, the two songs forming songwriter Spencer Krug's two-part meditation on the contradictions of being a touring musician and performer.

title: Like a Fool
fact: "Like a Fool" opens Superchunk's 1994 album Foolish, their first full-length for Merge Records, recorded at a breakneck pace at Pachyderm Studio with producer Brian Paulson. The band deliberately put it first because its clean, written-on-acoustic-guitar sound was a surprising change of pace from the crunchy power chords fans expected from them.

title: Precision Auto
fact: "Precision Auto" opens Superchunk's 1993 album On the Mouth, produced by John Reis of Rocket From the Crypt alongside the band. The song's revved-up energy has made it a favorite for other bands to cover, most notably Jimmy Eat World, who recorded their own version for their 2010 album Invented.

Bonny
fact: Swapmeet's “Bonny” includes a shoutout to the TV show Malcolm in the Middle - the band has said it made the cut mainly because it fit the syllable count of the line.

title: I Know!
fact: According to the Australian band, "I Know!" practically wrote itself, emerging almost by accident out of an in-between-songs practice jam, unlike anything else on the record. It now opens their debut album, Mount Zero, blending jangle-pop and shoegaze with echoes of '90s alt-rock acts like Pavement and Sonic Youth.

title: Accent
fact: Sweeping Promises' "Accent," from 2026's You Say I Romanticize, is built around what the band calls a "cicadence" - a flapping, insectoid post-punk rhythm - wrestling with the uneasy feeling of trying to express yourself in a world that can make you feel like you're speaking a foreign language.

title: Pain Without a Touch
fact: Sweeping Promises recorded "Pain Without a Touch" in November 2021, tracking part of it inside a repurposed bathroom at the band's home for its natural reverb. The song became the Massachusetts post-punk duo's first release after signing to Sub Pop, co-released with Feel It Records. Its hard-picked bassline and sparse, splashy guitar work made it an instant college-radio favorite.

title: Coffee
fact: "Coffee" was the breakout 2014 single from Sylvan Esso's self-titled debut album, earning the North Carolina duo a national television performance on The Tonight Show Starring Jimmy Fallon that summer. Singer Amelia Meath has described the song as being about carving out a short personal break in an otherwise rushed day.

title: Concrete Glen
fact: Concrete Glen, from Sylvan Esso's 2026 album Ow, samples Sigur Ros' "Svefn-g-englar" - a band singer Amelia Meath has said soundtracked a lot of her childhood.

title: Die Young
fact: "Die Young" appears on Sylvan Esso's 2017 album What Now. Vocalist Amelia Meath wrote it as an experiment to see if she could pull off a straightforward love song, inspired by how falling in love had reshaped plans she'd made for her own life. Lines like "I had a plan, you ruined it completely" turn a wry joke into an upbeat synth-pop anthem.

title: Ferris Wheel
fact: Sylvan Esso's "Ferris Wheel," from 2020's Free Love, was the first song the band recorded in the studio they built themselves in the woods near their home in Durham, North Carolina.

title: Flood Season
fact: Before Sylvan Esso ever hit a studio, Amelia Meath caught a chorus of North Carolina crickets on an iPhone voice memo while writing this song — and that field recording ended up woven right into the finished track. 'Flood Season' lands on the duo's 2026 album Ow infinity, written after Hurricane Helene pushed them out of their longtime home in Durham before a cross-country move landed them in the middle of LA's 2025 wildfires. Sometimes the best samples really are just the sound of your own backyard.

title: Hot Slob
fact: Hot Slob is Sylvan Esso's first new single since 2022's No Rules Sandy, released in 2026 on their own label, Psychic Hotline. It features drummer TJ Maiani (Weyes Blood, Neneh Cherry) and Jenn Wasner of Wye Oak on extra guitar and vocals.

title: Kick Jump Twist
fact: Originally released as a 2016 B-side to 'Radio,' this bubbly synth-pop track later found a home on Sylvan Esso's 2017 album What Now. Singer Amelia Meath has said the song is about the performances we all put on for other people - practicing a look in the mirror, rehearsing how we present ourselves - set to a frenetic, retro-futuristic beat.

title: PARAD(w/m)E
fact: The title "PARAD(w/m)E" is a visual pun meant to be read as "parade with me." Sylvan Esso -- the duo of Amelia Meath and Nick Sanborn -- released it as a stand-alone single in January 2018, in between their albums What Now and Free Love. The accompanying music video, directed by Dan Huiting, is a bright, high-energy dance-party clip built around the song's title.

title: Play It Right
fact: Sylvan Esso's "Play It Right" is really the song that created the band - Amelia Meath, then singing in the folk trio Mountain Man, sent her a cappella vocal for the song to electronic producer Nick Sanborn and asked him to rework it his own way. The result was good enough that the two decided to keep making music together as Sylvan Esso.

title: Rooftop Dancing
fact: "Rooftop Dancing" was the second single from Sylvan Esso's 2020 album Free Love. Its music video, directed by Cheryl Dunn, follows a roller skater gliding joyfully around New York City and was conceived as a tribute to the resilience of New Yorkers during a difficult year.

title: Runaway
fact: Sylvan Esso's "Runaway," from 2020's Free Love, pairs Amelia Meath's bright, elated vocal with skittering, 8-bit-style synths from producer Nick Sanborn - the pair write and record together as a duo out of their own studio in Durham, North Carolina.

title: Sledge
fact: Sylvan Esso's "Sledge," from 2026's Ow∞ - their first album on their own label, Psychic Hotline - channels real disasters like Hurricane Helene and the LA wildfires into a tense, three-minute track. Amelia Meath's vocal take was captured almost entirely in first takes, giving it an unpolished immediacy.

title: Train
fact: "Train," from Sylvan Esso's 2020 album Free Love, grew out of singer Amelia Meath's goal of writing a song that was, in her words, "almost disgustingly" catchy. The duo later reworked the track for their WITH LOVE EP, released that December.

title: 20th Century Boy
fact: T. Rex recorded '20th Century Boy' in Tokyo in December 1972, in a rare session producer Tony Visconti didn't personally attend (though he remained officially credited). Backing vocals, handclaps, acoustic guitar, and saxophone were added later back in England. Despite being considered for the closing slot on the album Tanx, it was left off entirely and released as a standalone single in 1973, only showing up on Tanx as a bonus track on later reissues.

title: Children of the Revolution
fact: Marc Bolan wrote and T. Rex producer Tony Visconti helmed "Children of the Revolution," which became a UK number 2 hit in September 1972. An earlier version featuring Elton John on piano and Ringo Starr on drums was filmed for Starr's documentary "Born to Boogie," but the single itself was re-recorded in the studio without either guest musician.

title: Mambo Sun
fact: "Mambo Sun" opens T. Rex's 1971 glam-rock landmark Electric Warrior, produced by Tony Visconti. The album was pieced together across four different studios on two continents: Trident and Advision in London, Wally Heider's in Hollywood, and Mediasound in New York City.

artist: Taio Cruz feat Travie Mc Coy
title: Higher
Living in Another World
fact: "Living in Another World" was a hit single from Talk Talk's 1986 album The Colour of Spring, written by Mark Hollis and Tim Friese-Greene. The track features a guest organ performance from Traffic's Steve Winwood, and the album went on to reach number eight on the UK charts.

title: (Nothing but) Flowers
fact: David Byrne wrote this one as a cheeky flip of Joni Mitchell's 'Big Yellow Taxi' — instead of paving paradise to put up a parking lot, he imagines all the strip malls reverting back to nature, with the narrator missing his Dairy Queen and Pizza Hut. The 1988 track, from the album Naked, features Johnny Marr of the Smiths on lead guitar and Kirsty MacColl on backing vocals.

title: Blind
fact: 'Blind' opens Talking Heads' final studio album, Naked (1988), which the band built out of improvisational jam sessions in Paris with a large cast of guest musicians, including former Smiths guitarist Johnny Marr and singer Kirsty MacColl, before David Byrne added lyrics and vocals back in New York.

title: Born Under Punches (The Heat Goes On)
Crosseyed and Painless
fact: "Crosseyed and Painless" was tracked for 1980's Remain in Light at Compass Point Studios in Nassau, with vocals and overdubs finished later at Sigma Sound in New York. Guitarist Adrian Belew happened to be passing through on tour with David Bowie and ended up recording all his guitar parts for the entire album in a single session. The music video skips the band altogether in favor of the Electric Boogaloos breakdance crew, directed by Toni Basil.

title: Girlfriend Is Better
fact: "Girlfriend Is Better," from Talking Heads' 1983 album Speaking in Tongues, contains the line "as we get older and stop making sense" — which gave the band's classic 1984 concert film, Stop Making Sense, its title. The song was credited collectively to all four band members: David Byrne, Chris Frantz, Jerry Harrison, and Tina Weymouth.

title: Girls Want to Be With the Girls
album: More Songs About Buildings and Food

title: Heaven
fact: David Byrne has said the title of Talking Heads' 'Heaven' was actually borrowed from a real bar of the same name in the UK. In the song, heaven gets reimagined as a place where the same party and the same kiss repeat forever -- 'a place where nothing ever happens.' It appears on 1979's Fear of Music, the album where the band's arty, anxious sound really came into focus.

title: Lifetime Piling Up
album: Sand in the Vaseline: Popular Favorites
fact: "Lifetime Piling Up" was written by all four members of Talking Heads - David Byrne, Chris Frantz, Jerry Harrison and Tina Weymouth - as an outtake from the sessions for their 1988 album "Naked." It stayed unreleased until it surfaced on the 1992 compilation "Popular Favorites 1976-1992: Sand in the Vaseline," where it reached number 11 on the Billboard Alternative Airplay chart.

title: Love -> Building On Fire
fact: "Love -> Building on Fire" was Talking Heads' debut single, released in February 1977, seven months ahead of their first album. It was recorded at Sundragon Recording Studios in New York while the band was still a trio, before keyboardist Jerry Harrison joined, and was produced by Tony Bongiovi and Tom Erdelyi (better known as Tommy Ramone).

title: Love for Sale
fact: Despite sharing its title with the Cole Porter standard, Talking Heads' "Love for Sale" is an original David Byrne composition written for the 1986 film True Stories, which Byrne also directed. Byrne wrote the lyric in the style of a TV commercial pitch, borrowing real ad slogans like Greyhound's "Leave the driving to us" and Coke's "It's the real thing."

title: Memories Can't Wait
fact: David Byrne described Talking Heads' “Memories Can't Wait” as the band's version of a metal song - about memories that keep flooding back no matter how much you try to move on.

title: Psycho Killer
fact: The French-language bridge of "Psycho Killer" was written by bassist Tina Weymouth, who spoke French with her mother. David Byrne had originally wanted a Japanese-language verse, but when that didn't work out, drummer Chris Frantz suggested Weymouth translate it into French instead, which she finished in just over an hour. As a result, it's the only song on Talking Heads' 1977 debut album credited to all three of Byrne, Frantz, and Weymouth rather than Byrne alone.

title: Pulled Up
fact: Pulled Up is one of the closing tracks on Talking Heads' debut album, Talking Heads: 77 (September 16, 1977), and was released as a single in the UK in March 1978. The album's Super Deluxe Edition unearthed a previously unheard alternate Pop version of the song.

title: Slippery People
fact: "Slippery People," from Talking Heads' 1983 album Speaking in Tongues, blends gospel, funk and reggae, with lyrics nodding to the Book of Ezekiel's "four living creatures" and "wheel in the middle of a wheel." Gospel singer Mavis Staples was drawn to the song and has kept it in her live repertoire ever since.

title: Take Me To The River
album: More Songs About Buildings and Food

title: The Good Thing
album: More Songs About Buildings and Food

title: This Must Be the Place (Naive Melody)
fact: To keep this song simple, Talking Heads swapped instruments: bassist Tina Weymouth played guitar and guitarist Jerry Harrison played the repeating bass part on a Prophet-5 synthesizer. It closes 1983's Speaking in Tongues, and David Byrne said he wanted to write a love song that wasn't corny.

title: Apocalypse Dreams
fact: "Apocalypse Dreams" was the first song Kevin Parker ever co-wrote for Tame Impala, working with keyboardist Jay Watson on an album, Lonerism, that he otherwise recorded almost entirely alone. Parker says he wrote the lyrics before ever seeing the 2011 film Melancholia, then was startled by how closely its themes lined up once he finally watched it. The track kicked off Lonerism's promotional rollout as its first single in mid-2012.

title: Borderline
fact: Tame Impala's "Borderline" debuted live on Saturday Night Live in March 2019 before Kevin Parker had even finished writing the lyrics, ad-libbing much of it on the spot - listen closely after he sings "like a train" and you can hear an actual passing train in the mix.

title: Disciples
fact: "Disciples" is a sub-two-minute track from Tame Impala's 2015 album Currents, first previewed by Kevin Parker during a Reddit AMA. The song features guitar work from veteran musician Todd Rundgren, whose 1973 album A Wizard, a True Star had already shaped Parker's songwriting on the earlier record Lonerism.

title: Elephant
fact: "Elephant" was one of the oldest songs Kevin Parker had sitting around unused, and the band only decided to put it on 2012's Lonerism after rediscovering it during a soundcheck. The album went on to sweep Best Album, Best Rock Album, and Best Group at the 2013 ARIA Awards.

title: End Of Summer
fact: Kevin Parker quietly previewed 'End of Summer' during a surprise DJ set at Barcelona's Nitsa Club in June 2025, months before releasing it as his first new Tame Impala material since revisiting Lonerism for its tenth anniversary. As usual, Parker wrote, performed, produced, recorded, and mixed the track entirely himself, this time from his home studio in Fremantle, Western Australia.

title: Eventually
fact: "Eventually" was released as a single in June 2015 ahead of Tame Impala's third album, Currents, which came out in July 2015.

title: Expectation
fact: "Expectation" was recorded by Kevin Parker in mid-2009 at Wave House in Injidup, Western Australia, during the sessions for Tame Impala's debut album Innerspeaker. Released as the album's third single in December 2010, the six-minute track was mixed by Dave Fridmann and features cover art by Australian artist Leif Podhajsky.

title: Feels Like We Only Go Backwards
fact: Tame Impala is essentially one person, Kevin Parker of Perth, Australia, who started the project as a home-recording effort on Myspace in 2007. He layers his own multi-tracked voice to create the illusion of a full band.

title: I Don't Really Mind
fact: "I Don't Really Mind" closes out Tame Impala's 2010 debut album InnerSpeaker, giving the record what's been called an "intergalactic bubblegum" finish. Kevin Parker recorded and produced the album himself in a mansion overlooking the Indian Ocean, and it was later mixed by Dave Fridmann, known for his work with MGMT and The Flaming Lips.

title: It Is Not Meant to Be
fact: "It Is Not Meant to Be" opens Tame Impala's 2010 debut album Innerspeaker, a one-man studio project written, played, and recorded almost entirely by Australian musician Kevin Parker. Much of the album was tracked at a beach house called Wave House Injidup in Western Australia, and this opening track's dreamy vocal drew comparisons to John Lennon.

title: Music to Walk Home By
fact: Music to Walk Home By is on Tame Impala's 2012 album Lonerism. Kevin Parker wrote and produced the song himself, and it runs 5 minutes 12 seconds.

title: New Person, Same Old Mistakes
fact: This closing track from Tame Impala's 2015 album Currents was written, performed, and produced almost entirely by Kevin Parker. He originally pictured the song being sung by 1990s R&B trio TLC, since many of his songs start out as ideas he imagines giving to other artists. In 2016, Rihanna covered it as "Same Ol' Mistakes" on her album Anti.

title: Reality in Motion
fact: Tame Impala's "Reality in Motion" closes out 2015's Currents - one of the few moments on that mostly synth-driven album where Kevin Parker reaches back for his older, guitar-driven sound, with erratic rhythm changes mirroring the song's racing, overdriven feeling.

title: Runway, Houses, City, Clouds
fact: Tame Impala's Kevin Parker recorded nearly all of the band's 2010 debut album Innerspeaker by himself at a remote beach shack called Wave House in Injidup, Western Australia. The sprawling, largely instrumental "Runway, Houses, City, Clouds" runs over seven minutes and closes the album with additional guitar from bandmate Dominic Simper, before the record was mixed by producer Dave Fridmann in New York.

title: Solitude Is Bliss
fact: "Solitude Is Bliss" was the lead single from Tame Impala's 2010 debut album Innerspeaker, and Kevin Parker has called it "the most uplifting pop song" he could offer as a first introduction to the record. The single's artwork came from Australian artist Leif Podhajsky, who designed the visual look for the whole Innerspeaker era.

title: The Less I Know The Better
fact: Kevin Parker wrote and recorded nearly all of Currents alone in a home studio in Fremantle, Australia, and the song's instantly recognizable bassline isn't a bass at all — it's a guitar run through an octave-down pedal and guitar synth effects. Parker has said the core of the song, including that riff and the vocal melody, came together in about fifteen minutes. He briefly gave the track away to collaborator Mark Ronson before asking for it back, a decision that helped make it Tame Impala's signature song.

title: Why Won't You Make Up Your Mind?
Yes I'm Changing
fact: "Yes I'm Changing" is the third track on Tame Impala's 2015 album Currents, a record built entirely around the theme of personal transformation. As with nearly everything on Currents, Kevin Parker wrote, played, produced, and engineered the song by himself. Parker later said the songwriting came together so quickly it felt like someone else had written it.

title: Thin Air (feat. Enumclaw)
fact: "Thin Air" comes from Tanukichan's (Hannah Van Loon's) 2023 album GIZMO, which she wrote and recorded together with Chaz Bear of Toro y Moi. For this track the pair brought in Aramis Johnson of the Tacoma band Enumclaw as a featured vocalist.

title: The Concept
fact: "The Concept," written and sung by Norman Blake, was the second single from Teenage Fanclub's 1991 album Bandwagonesque on Creation Records. The sprawling six-minute track helped the Scottish band's album get named Spin magazine's Album of the Year for 1991, beating out Nirvana's Nevermind and R.E.M.'s Out of Time.

title: Impossible
album: how do you sleep at night?

title: Cool Job
fact: "Cool Job" was the lead single from Seattle post-punk band Telehealth's second album, Green World Image (2026), released after they signed to Sub Pop. The band is led by married couple Alexander Attitude and Kendra Cox, and Attitude directed the video himself.

title: Donor Country (A gOoD cAuSe)
fact: Donor Country (A gOoD cAuSe) is from Green World Image, Telehealth's debut album on Sub Pop (May 15, 2026). Its video imagines a talent show with witches, hedge trimmers, magicians and bubblegum blowers.

title: See No Evil
fact: 'See No Evil' kicks off Television's landmark 1977 album Marquee Moon, built around Tom Verlaine playing a single, undoubled guitar line on his 1958 Fender Jazzmaster, no overdubs needed. The song's reputation has only grown since: R.E.M. loved it enough to cover it as one of their annual holiday fan-club singles.

title: Vendetta
fact: Temples' 'Vendetta' marks a hard left turn for the English psych-rock band, swapping their usual retro guitar sound for a pulsing dance-floor groove. Frontman James Bagshaw described it as opening with 'an almost Justice-Daft Punk-sounding sample' before shifting into something closer to a modern David Guetta or Avicii track. It's the lead single from their album Bliss, the follow-up to 2023's Exotico.

fact: This is the lead single from Thao's upcoming 2026 album Show Me, her first in six years, co-produced by Tune-Yards' Merrill Garbus and Nate Brenner. It's a three-way team-up, stacking Thao's voice with Garbus and teenage punk outfit The Linda Lindas for one big, layered group vocal.

title: Gentlemen
fact: The title track and album were recorded at the legendary Ardent Studios in Memphis in 1993, with the band deliberately aiming for a "cinematic" sound — they even worked in the rumble of a car crossing the John A. Roebling Suspension Bridge on the record's opening. Frontman Greg Dulli has said Gentlemen is the only album he can remember writing while out on tour.

title: The House of the Rising Sun
Carnage
fact: The Antlers began in 2006 as the solo home-recording project of Brooklyn singer Peter Silberman before growing into a full band for 2009's breakthrough Hospice; today it's back down to just Silberman and drummer Michael Lerner. "Carnage" is the lead single from 2025's Blight, the band's first new album in four years, which Silberman wrote after taking walks through the fields near his home studio.

title: Director
fact: "Director" appears on The Antlers' 2014 album "Familiars," the follow-up to their breakout concept record "Hospice." On the track, frontman Peter Silberman sings in a falsetto that drew comparisons to Jeff Buckley, building toward a cymbal-heavy instrumental break.

title: Every Night My Teeth Are Falling Out
Hotel
fact: "Hotel" is the third track on The Antlers' 2014 album Familiars, a separate record from the band's earlier Hospice concept album. It was the second song released from Familiars, following lead single "Palace," and like the rest of the record it was mixed by Chris Coady; reviewers at the time noted the track's horn arrangement and groove marked a new, more upbeat direction for the band.

title: Palace
fact: "Palace," from the Antlers' 2014 album Familiars, draws on the extended architectural imagery that runs through the whole record — songwriter Peter Silberman uses palaces, fortresses, and mausoleums as metaphors for the elaborate mental structures people build around memory and identity. It's one of the few songs on the album addressed directly to its subject.

title: Something in the Air
fact: 'Something in the Air' is a 2025 single from The Antlers' album Blight, inspired by singer Peter Silberman's walks near his home recording studio. He's described the song as being about 'a looming threat that can take many forms,' part of an album that grapples broadly with climate anxiety and humanity's quiet, cumulative impact on the natural world.

title: Energy
fact: "Energy," from The Apples in Stereo's 2007 album New Magnetic Wonder, got a music video directed by actor Elijah Wood, marking his directorial debut. Wood was a longtime fan of the band and had signed them as the first act on his independent label, Simian Records, after meeting frontman Robert Schneider at SXSW in 2003.

title: Go
album: The Discovery of a World Inside the Moone
fact: Go opens The Apples in Stereo's 2000 album The Discovery of a World Inside the Moone, one of the earliest releases from Robert Schneider's Elephant 6 Recording Company collective. Schneider's songwriting on the record leans on the lush, layered pop production techniques associated with the Beach Boys and other 1960s studio pop. The album's title and concept riff on an old hoax about a fictional civilization discovered on the moon.

title: Tidal Wave
fact: "Tidal Wave" was the title track of the band's debut 7" EP, self-released in June 1993 under the name the Apples (before they became the Apples in Stereo) — notably, it was also the very first official release on the influential Elephant 6 Recording Co. label. Leader Robert Schneider co-wrote the song with Chris Parfitt and produced the whole EP on a four-track recorder.

title: Put a Flower in Your Pocket
Blue Shadows (feat. Karen O)
fact: 'Blue Shadows' reunited The Avalanches with Yeah Yeah Yeahs singer Karen O, following their 2020 collaboration 'Dial D for Devotion.' The track actually began years earlier as an idea from Avalanches member Andy Szekeres that was nearly forgotten until bandmate Tony Di Blasi rediscovered it in an old folder, and it marks the first time Karen O actually sings on an Avalanches track rather than reciting lyrics.

title: Frontier Psychiatrist
fact: "Frontier Psychiatrist," from The Avalanches' 2000 album Since I Left You, takes its title and several spoken-word samples from a 1960s comedy sketch called "Frontier Psychiatrist" by the duo Wayne and Shuster. The track is built from dozens of samples, reportedly more than any other song on the album, including a sampled horse whinny and a piece of music from the 1971 film Anna, all scratched together one phrase at a time by DJ Dexter Fabay.
