album: Box for Buddy, Box for Star (Deluxe)
fact: When Nate Amos, who records as This Is Lorelei, put together a deluxe reissue of Box for Buddy, Box for Star with guest reworkings, his very first thought was getting Snail Mail's Lindsey Jordan to sing "Two Legs." Jordan has called Amos one of the best songwriters of their generation and said recording vocals for it was a treat because it meant hearing his songwriting over and over. The redone version keeps the original's old-timey sampled texture but wraps it in Jordan's airy, doubled vocals.

title: Song to the Siren
fact: "Song to the Siren" was written in 1967 by Tim Buckley and his high-school friend and lyricist Larry Beckett, first appearing on Buckley's 1970 album "Starsailor." This Mortal Coil's 1983 cover, sung by Cocteau Twins' Elizabeth Fraser, was built around a guitar part Robin Guthrie improvised in a single take after hearing Buckley's original just once through headphones; the single spent 101 weeks on the UK independent chart.

title: Harrowdown Hill
fact: Thom Yorke's "Harrowdown Hill" was the first single from his 2006 solo debut The Eraser, reaching #23 on the UK singles chart - the song actually dates back to the sessions for Radiohead's Hail to the Thief, though Yorke felt it never quite worked as a Radiohead song.

title: Knife Edge
fact: "Knife Edge" comes from Thom Yorke's score for the 2024 Italian film Confidenza, only his second movie soundtrack after 2018's Suspiria. The stark, piano-led track accompanies a re-cut scene from the film, and its music video was built from footage arranged by the film's own editor.

Children of the Baked Potato (feat. Remi Wolf)
album: I Wish I Didn't Waste Your Time
fact: Thundercat released 'Children of the Baked Potato,' featuring Remi Wolf, as a single on September 15, 2025, ahead of his album Distracted. The title nods to The Baked Potato, the longtime hole-in-the-wall jazz club in LA's San Fernando Valley that has showcased fusion players for decades and shaped both musicians' backgrounds, with Thundercat calling Wolf 'a child of the Baked Potato like me.'

title: Painting of a Tree
fact: Tiberius started as a solo project for songwriter Brendan Wright before growing into a four-piece out of Boston who call their sound "farm emo." The title "Painting of a Tree" comes from an offhand line Wright once heard from an eccentric older man: "an artist cannot paint a tree, unless they examine all aspects of it." The song appears on their 2025 album Troubadour.

title: Sag
fact: Boston band Tiberius, originally the solo project of songwriter Brendan Wright, released "Sag" in early 2025 before it was picked up and re-released by the label Audio Antihero ahead of their debut album, "Troubadour." The song is about what locals call the "Allston to Bushwick pipeline," the well-worn path of Boston musicians moving to New York to chase their careers.

title: 16 Shells From a Thirty-Ought-Six
fact: "16 Shells From a Thirty-Ought-Six" is the second track on Tom Waits' 1983 album Swordfishtrombones, his first self-produced record and a major stylistic turn toward clattering, junkyard-orchestra arrangements. Waits said he wanted the track to have a chain-gang, work-song feel, built from metallic clangs and crashes meant to evoke the sound of a moving train.

title: All the World Is Green
fact: 'All the World Is Green' comes from Tom Waits' 2002 album Blood Money, a collaboration with playwright Robert Wilson and co-writer Kathleen Brennan built around Georg Buchner's play Woyzeck. Within that story the song functions as a tender love song, essentially a soldier's paean to his wife. It later turned up on the soundtracks to the films The Secret Life of Words and The Diving Bell and the Butterfly.

title: Anywhere I Lay My Head
fact: This song comes from Tom Waits' 1985 album Rain Dogs. Scarlett Johansson later used it as the title of her 2008 debut album of Waits covers, produced by David Sitek of TV on the Radio, with David Bowie singing backing vocals on two tracks.

title: Come On Up to the House
Goin' Out West
fact: "Goin' Out West" appears on Tom Waits' 1992 album "Bone Machine," which won the Grammy for Best Alternative Music Album. Waits co-wrote the song with his wife, Kathleen Brennan, and recorded it in a stark cellar room at Prairie Sun Recording with just a cement floor and a water heater for ambience, featuring Larry Taylor on electric upright bass and Joe Gore on guitar.

title: Ruby's Arms
fact: "Ruby's Arms" appears on Tom Waits' 1980 album Heartattack and Vine, recorded at Filmways/Heider Studio in Hollywood. French filmmaker Jean-Luc Godard later used the song in his 1983 film First Name: Carmen.

title: Shore Leave
fact: "Shore Leave," the second track on Tom Waits' 1983 landmark "Swordfishtrombones," follows a sailor wandering through a rainy Hong Kong night. Waits built the song's unusual percussive atmosphere from unconventional sources — a bass marimba, metal aungklung, and rice shaken over a bass drum — to conjure traffic, wind, and waves.

title: Tom Traubert's Blues (Four Sheets to the Wind in Copenhagen)
Way Down in the Hole
fact: Tom Waits wrote "Way Down in the Hole" for the 1987 Steppenwolf Theatre stage production Frank's Wild Years before it appeared on his album of the same name. It became famous years later as the theme song for HBO's The Wire, which used a different recorded version each season, including renditions by the Blind Boys of Alabama, the Neville Brothers, Steve Earle, and Waits's own original.

Chlorine
fact: Chlorine is from Bury the Key (Ghostly International, August 2025), the first full-length from Montreal band TOPS since 2020's I Feel Alive. The band self-produced it and leaned into a darker, "sinister disco" edge while keeping their dreamy sophisti-pop sound.

title: Baby Drive It Down
fact: "Baby Drive It Down" is a highlight from Toro y Moi's 2019 album Outer Peace, built around a marimba-like synth loop pulsing over a steady kick drum. Chaz Bear runs his vocals through heavy auto-tune and doubles the track, giving it a deliberately robotic feel. It's a good showcase of how Bear blends chillwave atmosphere with dance-pop structure.

title: Blessa
fact: Toro y Moi is Chaz Bear, considered one of the pioneers of the chillwave sound alongside artists like Washed Out. He studied graphic design in college and has released seven studio albums that range across wildly different styles.

title: Daria (feat. Kenny Beats)
fact: 'Daria' marked the first official studio collaboration between Toro y Moi and producer Kenny Beats, following Toro y Moi's guest appearance on Kenny's online freestyle show The Cave back in 2022. The song actually started as a Japan-only bonus track tied to Toro y Moi's album Hole Erth before getting a full standalone release. It dropped in the middle of a North American tour Toro y Moi was running alongside Panda Bear.

title: Freelance
fact: Freelance was the lead single from Toro y Moi's 2019 album Outer Peace. Chaz Bear wrote it about his return to the San Francisco Bay Area after living in Portland, Oregon.

title: Girl Like You
fact: "Girl Like You" is the lead single from Toro y Moi's fifth album, Boo Boo (2017), written, produced, and performed entirely by Chaz Bundick. The song's hazy opening sound was simply a factory preset on his synthesizer that he liked so much he left it in the final mix. It marked a playful, groove-driven turn after the more downtempo What For.

title: Hollywood (feat. Benjamin Gibbard)
fact: On "Hollywood," Toro y Moi's Chaz Bear teamed up with Death Cab for Cutie frontman Ben Gibbard, pairing a Blink-182-style guitar riff with a trap beat for an unusual genre mashup. The song appears on Bear's 2024 album Hole Erth, and Bear has said he'd long been a fan of Gibbard's music and it felt right to bring him onto the record.

title: Mirage
fact: "Mirage" opens Toro y Moi's fifth album Boo Boo (2017, Carpark Records). Chaz Bear has said he wrote the record as a form of personal therapy during a period of feeling self-conscious about fame after years of touring, drawing on influences like Travis Scott, Daft Punk, Frank Ocean, and Oneohtrix Point Never.

title: New Beat
fact: "New Beat" was the lead single from Toro y Moi's 2011 album Underneath the Pine, a deliberate about-face from his sample-heavy debut Causers of This. Chaz Bear built the whole record on live instruments instead, drawing inspiration from horror-movie soundtracks and space-disco composers like Piero Umiliani.

title: Ordinary Pleasure
fact: "Ordinary Pleasure" was released in December 2018 as the second single from Toro y Moi's sixth album, Outer Peace. As is typical for the project, mastermind Chaz Bundick wrote, produced, engineered, mixed, and performed every instrument on the track himself, blending synth-pop and disco with tribal drum patterns.

title: Postman
fact: 'Postman,' from Toro y Moi's 2022 album Mahal, samples the 1980 disco track 'A Lover's Holiday' by Change. The psych-funk song rides a bouncy bassline and a breezy vocal from Chaz Bundick.

title: Say That
fact: Say That was released January 1, 2013 as a single from Toro y Moi's album Anything in Return, and its video came out the next day, directed by HARRYS.

title: Sidelines
fact: "Sidelines" is the second track on Toro y Moi's surprise 2023 EP Sandhills, a tribute to Chaz Bear's hometown of Columbia, South Carolina. The song opens with the narrator recalling being a third-string player on a Friday night football team, using that memory as a jumping-off point for a broader look back at growing up. The EP runs just 13 minutes across five songs.

title: So Many Details
fact: Toro y Moi's "So Many Details," the lead single from 2013's Anything in Return, was written, produced, and performed entirely by Chaz Bundick himself - Pitchfork called it a leap forward in his songwriting after his move from South Carolina to Berkeley, California.

title: The Loop
fact: "The Loop" is the third single from Toro Y Moi's (Chaz Bear) seventh album Mahal, released via Dead Oceans — the album title is Tagalog for "love." The track's slow-strolling bassline and velvety groove draw comparisons to acid-jazz legend Roy Ayers.

title: Tuesday
fact: "Tuesday" is the opening track and lead single from Toro y Moi's 2024 album Hole Erth, whose title nods to the countercultural 1960s-70s publication Whole Earth Catalog. The song blends Chaz Bear's longtime love of pop-punk with rap-rock, and its video was directed by India Sleem; the full album also features guest spots from Ben Gibbard, Don Toliver, Porches, and Kevin Abstract.

artist: Toro y Moi feat. Unknown Mortal Orchestra
title: The Medium
fact: 'The Medium' pairs Toro y Moi's Chaz Bundick with Unknown Mortal Orchestra's Ruban Nielson, continuing a long friendship between the two artists -- Nielson previously contributed guitar to Toro y Moi's 2015 album What For?, and Bundick has covered UMO's 'Multi-Love' live. The song appears on Toro y Moi's 2022 album Mahal.

title: In A Dream
fact: "In A Dream" is the opening track and lead single from Trace Mountains' 2024 album "Into the Burning Blue," produced by Craig Hendrix (known for his work with Japanese Breakfast). Songwriter Dave Benton has said the track began as a prompt from a songwriting workshop he teaches, and that he was picturing Bruce Springsteen's "Tunnel of Love" and David Lynch's "Blue Velvet" while writing it.

title: Love Leave The Body
fact: 'Love Leave the Body' closes out Houston band Trembler's 2026 EP Total Sorry as an overdriven, shoegaze-tinged rocker built around a towering chorus. The band recorded and mixed the EP themselves at their own Shiny Tone Recordings, with mastering by Corey Coffman, who also produced their 2022 full-length Folding.

title: The Gonzales Shoulder
fact: Trembler is a four-piece band from Houston, Texas, made up of Luke Gonzales, CJ Anderson, Ceej Burton, and Martin Long. "The Gonzales Shoulder" appears on their 2026 EP Total Sorry, and reviewers noted the track's metallic tone and melodic guitar work drew comparisons to Death Cab for Cutie.

title: Drop
fact: Drop was the second single from Thee Black Boltz, the 2025 debut solo album from TV on the Radio's Tunde Adebimpe. It was produced by his bandmate Jahphet Landis and builds out from a looped beatboxing pattern.

title: God Knows
fact: God Knows is from Thee Black Boltz, the debut solo album by TV on the Radio frontman Tunde Adebimpe (Sub Pop, 2025). Adebimpe produced it with Wilder Zoby.

title: Magnetic
fact: 'Magnetic' comes from Thee Black Boltz, TV on the Radio frontman Tunde Adebimpe's debut solo album, released on Sub Pop in April 2025. At just two and a half minutes, its minimalist electro-punk pulse recalls his old band's early-2000s Brooklyn DIY days, with lyrics musing on 'the human race in the age of tenderness and rage.'

title: Heartbreak
fact: Heartbreak opens Tune-Yards' 2025 album Better Dreaming, their first since 2021's sketchy. Merrill Garbus and Nate Brenner build it from huge stacked vocal harmonies over a slow-jam beat full of clicks, pops and samples.

title: How Big Is The Rainbow
fact: How Big Is the Rainbow, a single from Tune-Yards' 2025 album Better Dreaming, is a clattering disco-house track. Its music video, directed by Dominic Mercurio, stars comedian and actress Star Amerasu.

title: Limelight
fact: 'Limelight' is the lead single from Tune-Yards' 2025 album Better Dreaming. Merrill Garbus and Nate Brenner wrote it after a night of dancing to George Clinton with their young child, who ended up singing on the finished track; the song almost got left off the record before fan and family response convinced them to keep it.

title: Myself in the Way (feat. Brendan Yates)
Nightjar
fact: Nightjar was released May 7, 2026 as a single with I See You and Realize, ahead of Turnover's album Down on Earth. After more than a decade on Run for Cover Records, the Virginia band released the album independently, with longtime front-of-house engineer Zac Montez producing to capture their live sound.

title: MYSTERY
fact: Turnstile grew out of Baltimore's hardcore scene in 2010, founded by singer Brendan Yates, who had previously drummed for the band Trapped Under Ice. Their 2025 album Never Enough won two Grammy Awards.

title: NEVER ENOUGH
fact: "Never Enough" is the title track and lead single from Turnstile's fourth album, which came out in June 2025 on Roadrunner Records. The song gave the Baltimore hardcore band their first number one on Billboard's Alternative Airplay chart, and the album went on to win Best Rock Album at the Grammys.

title: SEEIN' STARS
fact: "SEEIN' STARS," from Turnstile's 2025 album Never Enough, is a softer, disco-tinged departure for the hardcore band, featuring guest vocals from Blood Orange's Dev Hynes and Paramore's Hayley Williams. Critics noted its guitar riff echoes The Police's "When the World Is Running Down, You Make the Best of What's Still Around."

title: UNDERWATER BOI
fact: This Glow On track was recorded with producer Mike Elizondo, whose studio pedigree includes close work with Dr. Dre, according to Turnstile bassist Franz Lyons. For the music video, the band's own drummer, Daniel Fang, directed and built the entire animated world inside the classic MMORPG 'Second Life.'

title: Crying
fact: Crying is from TV on the Radio's 2008 album Dear Science, which the band followed in 2011 with Nine Types of Light on Interscope Records.

title: DLZ
fact: TV on the Radio's “DLZ” stands for “Dawn of the Loser,” a phrase from the song's final lines. It wasn't released as a single, but got a big boost in popularity after appearing in a season 2 episode of Breaking Bad.

title: Happy Idiot
fact: "Happy Idiot" was the first single from TV on the Radio's Seeds, the band's first album after the 2011 loss of longtime bassist Gerard Smith. It was recorded at guitarist Dave Sitek's home studio in Los Angeles, with Sitek producing.

title: Province
fact: TV on the Radio's "Province," from 2006's Return to Cookie Mountain, features David Bowie on backing vocals - the album was written by the full band and produced by guitarist Dave Sitek before landing on 4AD.

title: Satellite
fact: 'Satellite' isn't just a deep cut — it's the very first TV on the Radio song ever officially released, opening the band's 2003 debut EP Young Liars. Built from Tunde Adebimpe's looped, near-barbershop vocal harmonies over David Sitek's fuzzed-out production, with a flute line courtesy of Antibalas's Martin Perna, it set the template for the band's genre-blending sound years before Dear Science made them indie-rock royalty.

title: Will Do
fact: TV on the Radio began in 2001 when neighbors Tunde Adebimpe and Dave Sitek discovered they were both into music and visual art. They made an 18-song demo on 4-track recorders and silk-screened the CD covers by hand to hand out around Brooklyn.

title: Reality Cheque
fact: "Reality Cheque" is the second track on TV Star's debut album Music For Heads, released via Father/Daughter Records. The Seattle/Tacoma band grew out of the Pacific Northwest DIY scene during the pandemic, and its lineup includes bassist Mark Palm, who also fronts the band Supercrush.

title: When We First Met
fact: Twisted Teens' "When We First Met" comes from The Holy Cross Tigers on Sub Pop - the New Orleans garage-punk duo of Caspian Hollywell and Ramon "RJ" Santos blend the street-level grit of The Gun Club with early-punk urgency and dusty country-blues storytelling.

title: Black Paint
fact: "Black Paint" is the gritty first single from Ty Segall's 2026 album Chrome, his 18th studio record. It was recorded at Sonic Ranch in Texas with his full band - Ben Boye, Evan Burrows, Mikal Cronin, and Emmett Kelly - with Cooper Crain of Bitchin Bajas and Stereolab producing.

title: Glass
fact: Ty Segall is famously prolific - he's released a new solo album nearly every year since 2008, on top of numerous side projects, EPs, and collaborations.

title: Hospital
fact: Ty Segall's "Hospital" opens his 2026 album Chrome - released the same day as a companion EP, Love Fuzzz, both recorded with his full band of Ben Boye, Evan Burrows, Mikal Cronin, and Emmett Kelly.

title: White Liars
fact: Typhoon is led by Kyle Morton and known for its unusually large lineup - the Portland band has featured anywhere from 7 to 17 members on stage.

title: Like James Said
fact: Like James Said is from U.S. Girls' 2025 album Scratch It (4AD). Meg Remy wrote it with longtime collaborator Rich Morel, borrowing James Brown's advice to "dance until you feel better."

Barnacles
fact: Ugly Casanova was a side project formed by Modest Mouse frontman Isaac Brock in 1997. Brock originally credited the songs to a fictional character, "Edgar E. Graham," a persona he invented so he wouldn't have to do interviews about it.

title: Parasites
fact: "Parasites" appears on "Sharpen Your Teeth," the 2002 album by Ugly Casanova, a side project of Modest Mouse frontman Isaac Brock. The song started life as an unreleased Modest Mouse demo from the band's 1993 "Parasite Sessions." Brock originally tried to keep the Ugly Casanova project separate from his main band by crediting songwriting to a fictional collaborator named Edgar Graham.

title: Find Mii II (Find Mii II Ending)
Everyone Acts Crazy Nowadays
fact: "Everyone Acts Crazy Nowadays" is from Unknown Mortal Orchestra's 2018 album Sex & Food, which the New Zealand band recorded piecemeal in six different cities around the world: Mexico City, Seoul, Hanoi, Reykjavik, Portland, and Auckland. The song was written by brothers Ruban and Kody Nielson, with Ruban also producing the record.

title: FFunny FFrends
fact: Ruban Nielson uploaded "FFunny FFrends" anonymously to Bandcamp in May 2010, and within a day music blogs like Pitchfork were writing about it. He kept the project's identity secret at first because he wasn't sure what it should be, and the song later appeared on Unknown Mortal Orchestra's 2011 debut album.

title: Heaven 7
fact: "Heaven 7" is one of eight tracks on Unknown Mortal Orchestra's instrumental album IC-02 Bogota, released in 2025 as the second entry in a series documenting the band improvising music in different cities around the world. The band traveled to Bogota, Colombia and recorded at Estudio Naranja partly to help break in their new keyboardist, Christian Li, jamming out hypnotic, largely wordless material. The series began with 2018's IC-01 Hanoi.

title: How Can You Luv Me
fact: "How Can You Luv Me" appears on Unknown Mortal Orchestra's self-titled debut album, released June 21, 2011. The track was produced by frontman Ruban Nielson and incorporates a sample of "151 Rome Proof" by Lee Taylor & Soul Twisters Ltd. The debut album went on to win the 2012 Taite Music Prize in the band's native New Zealand.

title: Hunnybee
fact: Unknown Mortal Orchestra's "Hunnybee," from 2018's Sex & Food, began during a monsoon in Vietnam - frontman Ruben Nielson wrote it as a kind of time-capsule message of advice for his young daughter, Iris, to look back on someday.

title: Layla
fact: Don't let the title fool you, this "Layla" has nothing to do with the Eric Clapton classic. It's the lead single from Unknown Mortal Orchestra's 2023 double album V, with bandleader Ruban Nielson drawing on Hawaiian hapa-haole music while recording much of the record in Hawaii.

title: Like Acid Rain
fact: "Like Acid Rain," a short interlude from Unknown Mortal Orchestra's 2015 album Multi-Love, was written by brothers Ruban and Kody Nielson. Ruban produced, mixed, and engineered the entire record himself, while Kody flew out to Portland for five weeks to play drums and keyboards on most of the sessions.

title: Necessary Evil
fact: "Necessary Evil" is track 8 on Unknown Mortal Orchestra's 2015 album Multi-Love, and its warm brass chorus was played by frontman Ruban Nielson's father, jazz musician Chris Nielson. The two have continued performing the song together since, including as part of a family trio (with Ruban's brother Kody on drums) at UMO's 2023 NPR Tiny Desk Concert.

title: One at a Time
fact: "One at a Time" appears on Unknown Mortal Orchestra's 2013 album II, a short, funky track built around a distorted wah guitar riff and thumping bassline that pays clear homage to Sly and the Family Stone. II went on to win Best Alternative Album at the 2013 New Zealand Music Awards.

title: So Good At Being In Trouble
Swim and Sleep (Like A Shark)
fact: Swim and Sleep (Like a Shark) was released as a single in September 2012 ahead of Unknown Mortal Orchestra's album II (February 2013). An acoustic version of the song later appeared on the companion Blue Record EP.

title: That Life
fact: Unknown Mortal Orchestra is led by Ruban Nielson, whose father was a Maori horn player. Nielson first released UMO music anonymously on Bandcamp in 2010, and the project's self-titled debut album went on to win New Zealand's Taite Music Prize.

title: Ur Life One Night
fact: Unknown Mortal Orchestra's "Ur Life One Night," from 2015's Multi-Love, has a music video shot in India, inspired by traditional Asian art and Indian magical-realism - Ruban Nielson has said he specifically wanted to work with a director there, surprised he'd never made a video in the country with the world's biggest film industry.

title: Freaky
fact: Upchuck came together in 2018 out of Atlanta's skateboarding and DIY punk scene. "Freaky" is the lead single from their album Bite the Hand That Feeds, produced by Ty Segall and recorded at his home studio in Topanga Canyon, California, and its music video pays homage to actor Paul Reubens, best known for playing Pee-wee Herman.

title: DJ Got Us Falling In Love
Midwest
fact: "Midwest" appears on Australian band Vacations' 2023 album No Place Like Home. Singer Campbell Burns has said it was the first breakup song he'd ever written directly, inspired by the strain of leaving someone behind while out on tour, and he co-produced the track with John Velasquez.

title: Next Exit
fact: "Next Exit" was written by Vacations frontman Campbell Burns while the Australian band was on its first sold-out U.S. tour in early 2022, with the idea taking shape at a recording studio in Austin, Texas. It was co-produced by Burns and John Velasquez (known for his work with Zella Day and Gatlin) and marked the band's first new single since their 2020 album Forever in Bloom. The accompanying music video was shot on 16mm film to get a classic-cinema look.

title: Call Me a Fool
fact: Valerie June grew up singing in church in Humboldt, Tennessee, and taught herself guitar and banjo. She moved to Memphis at 18 and has since blended blues, folk, soul, and country into her own genre-defying sound - earning praise from Bob Dylan along the way.

title: Bambina
fact: "Bambina," from Vampire Weekend's 2024 album Only God Was Above Us, riffs on François Couperin's 1717 harpsichord piece "Les Barricades Mystérieuses" — an unusual reference for a rock band, but one that fits the Baroque influences that have run through Vampire Weekend's music since their earliest records.

title: Big Blue
fact: On 'Big Blue,' from 2019's Father of the Bride, Ezra Koenig addresses the Earth itself with the affectionate nickname that gives the song its title, treating the planet almost like an old friend. Despite the playful title, the song has the quiet, hymn-like earnestness of a devotional, with Koenig repeating the same humble verse over and over like a mantra. Koenig has cited Kacey Musgraves' Golden Hour as an influence on the album's warm, countryish psychedelia heard here.

title: Campus
fact: "Campus" is built entirely around Columbia University, where Vampire Weekend's members met and formed the band. The lyrics reference real spots on campus -- Low Plaza and South Lawn get a shoutout, and the balcony in the bridge is Hamilton Hall. Former member Rostam wrote the music around a scenario from Ezra Koenig's short story "Cruel Professor," capturing the awkwardness of running into an old crush on campus every day.

title: Capricorn
fact: "Capricorn" was the lead single from Vampire Weekend's 2024 album Only God Was Above Us, arriving five years after Father of the Bride. Frontman Ezra Koenig has said the wistful, string-laden track isn't about one specific person born under the sign, but uses Capricorn — the sign for people born at the very end of the year — as a lens for reflecting on time passing.

title: Diane Young
fact: "Diane Young," from Vampire Weekend's 2013 album Modern Vampires of the City, gets its title from wordplay on the phrase "dying young." The track was produced by Rostam Batmanglij, Ezra Koenig, and Ariel Rechtshaid, and its striking music video shows two vintage Saab cars in slow motion, achieved by filming just five seconds of real footage at 1,000 frames per second with a high-speed Phantom camera.

title: Don't Lie
fact: "Don't Lie" appears on Vampire Weekend's 2013 album Modern Vampires of the City. Frontman Ezra Koenig has described it as a kind of sequel to the band's earlier songs "M79" and "White Sky," built around a simpler, more direct arrangement than listeners might expect from the band.

title: Everlasting Arms
fact: "Everlasting Arms" appears on Vampire Weekend's 2013 album Modern Vampires of the City, written by Ezra Koenig and produced by Ariel Rechtshaid and Rostam Batmanglij. It's one of several tracks on the record built around the band's classically trained, baroque-pop arrangements.

title: Hannah Hunt
fact: Ezra Koenig began writing "Hannah Hunt" years before its release, starting the lyric while he was still a student at Columbia University. Vampire Weekend couldn't find the right musical arrangement for it in time for their first two albums, finally completing it for 2013's "Modern Vampires of the City" with producer Ariel Rechtshaid and bandmate Rostam Batmanglij.

title: Harmony Hall
fact: Vampire Weekend's "Harmony Hall" was the lead single from 2019's Father of the Bride, arriving after a six-year gap between albums - its lyrics even interpolate a line from their earlier song "Finger Back."

title: Hold You Now
fact: Hold You Now opens Vampire Weekend's 2019 album Father of the Bride as a duet with Danielle Haim, an idea that grew out of a conversation Ezra Koenig and Haim had years earlier in 2010. The track carries a co-writing credit for film composer Hans Zimmer, because it samples a Melanesian choral recording, "God Yu Tekem Laef Blong Mi," that Zimmer had used in his score for the 1998 film The Thin Red Line.

title: Mansard Roof
fact: "Mansard Roof" was Vampire Weekend's debut single, released in October 2007 and later placed as the opening track of their self-titled 2008 album. Written by Ezra Koenig and Rostam Batmanglij, the song takes its name from the distinctive sloped mansard-style roofs common in the coastal Northeast, setting the scene for the band's architecture-referencing lyrical style.

title: Mary Boone
fact: "Mary Boone," from Vampire Weekend's Only God Was Above Us, builds its rhythm from a sample of Soul II Soul's 1989 hit "Back to Life (However Do You Want Me)" — the same drum loop Primitive Radio Gods used for their 1996 single "Standing Outside a Broken Phone Booth with Money in My Hand." The track layers in a full choir, strings, and warbling synths, and takes its title from a prominent figure in New York's 1980s art world.

title: Obvious Bicycle
fact: Vampire Weekend's “Obvious Bicycle” never actually says the words “obvious” or “bicycle” anywhere in the lyrics - it was just the title Rostam Batmanglij gave the demo the day he wrote it, and it stuck.

title: One (Blake's Got a New Face)
fact: Despite the odd parenthetical, there really is a Blake behind this Vampire Weekend deep cut: Ezra Koenig met a friend of his girlfriend's named Blake, and the name just stuck in his head. He had the melody worked out long before he had any lyrics, and he's said the song's loose energy actually traces back to a Metallica reference. It closes out side one of the band's self-titled 2008 debut.

title: Oxford Comma
fact: Vampire Weekend's "Oxford Comma" name-checks Lil Jon in a song about grammar and not caring too much about the rules - Lil Jon was apparently flattered enough by the shoutout to send the band a case of his own Crunk Juice energy drink, and a real friendship followed.

title: Pravda
fact: "Pravda," from Vampire Weekend's 2024 album Only God Was Above Us, takes its title from the Russian word for truth. Frontman Ezra Koenig has said the song was inspired partly by his own family history: his great-uncle Henry Shapiro was a longtime Moscow correspondent, and Koenig grew up hearing his grandmother's proud stories about her brother. The track even weaves in a balalaika as it muses on memory, time, and distance from home.

title: Run
fact: Vampire Weekend's Ezra Koenig has said Run, from 2010's Contra, was written with Bruce Springsteen's Born to Run in mind.

title: Sympathy
fact: "Sympathy," from Vampire Weekend's 2019 album Father of the Bride, finds the band diving fully into dance music for the first time, with driving guitars and castanets giving it a sound critics compared to the dance-punk duo Basement Jaxx. When the band performed it on The Late Show with Stephen Colbert, they reworked the all-hook dance track into a lush, propulsive, semi-acoustic arrangement.

title: The Kids Don't Stand a Chance
Young Lion
fact: Young Lion closes Vampire Weekend's 2013 album Modern Vampires of the City. It's the only Vampire Weekend song where Rostam Batmanglij is the sole lead vocalist and writer.

title: Domino
album: His Band and the Street Choir

title: The Path Less Travelled
album: The Road To Hell Is Paved With Good Intentions

title: Flirted With You All My Life
The Ugliest Girl On The Beach
album: My Heart Is A Room With No Cameras In It
fact: Victoryland is a partnership between singer-songwriter Julian McCamman and producer Dan Howard, and "The Ugliest Girl on the Beach" marked a big milestone for the project -- it arrived alongside the announcement that the band had signed to the indie label Dead Oceans. The track is set to appear as a bonus song on the deluxe edition of their debut album, My Heart Is a Room with No Cameras in It.

title: I Held Her in My Arms
Can't Get Over You
fact: Vivian Girls set out to write a full-on, hooky '60s pop song with this one, and that's exactly what landed on their 2009 album Everything Goes Wrong. Fittingly lo-fi and fast, the whole record was tracked in just six days, with a lot of songs captured in single takes.

title: Beta Fish
fact: 'Beta Fish' is a single off Vundabar's 2025 album Surgery and Pleasure, the Boston trio's sixth record and first for the label Loma Vista. The hypnotic lyrics track the restless movement of a betta fish swimming in circles and biting at its own reflection, set to a repetitive, driving groove. Critics singled out the song's chanting final 90 seconds as some of the best songwriting on the whole record.

title: Your Apartment
fact: "Your Apartment" marked Wallows' first new music after their 2022 album Tell Me That It's Over, released as the lead single from 2024's Model. The song was co-written with Nate Mercereau, who has also worked with Andre 3000 and Shawn Mendes, and produced by John Congleton, known for his work with St. Vincent and Sharon Van Etten. It's a fast-paced, hook-driven track built around racing percussion and earworm guitar riffs.

title: Shake Your Head (Let's Go to Bed)
Feel It All Around
fact: "Feel It All Around" was a defining song of the chillwave sound and became the theme song of the IFC sketch comedy show Portlandia, which premiered in January 2011. It first appeared in 2009 and samples the 1983 song "I Want You" by Italian singer Gary Low.

title: Life Signs
fact: "Life Signs" is the lead single from Water From Your Eyes' 2025 album It's a Beautiful Place, released via Matador Records. Written by the duo's Rachel Brown and Nate Amos and produced with engineer Howie Weinberg, the track opens with a nu-metal-style backbeat before pivoting into the band's signature dream-pop chorus; Amos has said it was the first WFYE song he wrote picturing the band playing venues bigger than a basement.

title: Be Good
fact: Waxahatchee's "Be Good," from 2017's Out in the Storm, marked a shift away from Katie Crutchfield's earlier lo-fi sound - she recorded it with co-producer John Agnello at Philadelphia's Miner Street Recordings. Her stage name comes from Waxahatchee Creek, near where she grew up in Alabama.

title: Bored
fact: Waxahatchee's Katie Crutchfield has said "Bored," from 2024's Tigers Blood, grew out of a soured platonic friendship and was written from a place of anger rather than her usual sadness or heartache. She's noted that writing from anger felt like a riskier departure for her, since her comfort zone as a songwriter usually sits somewhere between sadness and heartache.

title: Fire
fact: Katie Crutchfield wrote much of "Fire," the first single from Waxahatchee's 2020 album Saint Cloud, while actually driving. The melody and lyrics came to her while crossing the Memphis & Arkansas Bridge on a road trip, which she says almost never happens since she usually writes at an instrument or with pen and paper.

title: Hear You
fact: 'Hear You' appears on Waxahatchee's 2017 album Out in the Storm, released on Merge Records. The record features Katie Crutchfield's sister Allison on keyboards and percussion, alongside touring Sleater-Kinney guitarist Katie Harkin.

title: Hell
fact: For "Hell," off 2020's Saint Cloud, Katie Crutchfield said she leaned into the melodramatic intensity of Dolly Parton's songwriting — especially "Jolene" — aiming to write something "a little bit psycho," since, as she put it, everybody feels that way sometimes.

title: Much Ado About Nothing
fact: "Much Ado About Nothing" is a Waxahatchee single Katie Crutchfield released in October 2024, in the same twangy folk-rock vein as her album Tigers Blood. It features MJ Lenderman on electric guitar along with Brad and Phil Cook, and later got a dedicated 7-inch release for Record Store Day 2025, backed with two more new recordings, "Mud" and "Next To Me."

title: Never Been Wrong
fact: Never Been Wrong was the second single from Waxahatchee's fourth album, Out in the Storm (2017). Katie Crutchfield sings it over big, blown-out guitars.

title: Oxbow
fact: "Oxbow" is the opening track on Waxahatchee's 2020 album Saint Cloud, which marked a turn toward a warmer, more rootsy Americana sound for songwriter Katie Crutchfield compared to her earlier, more lo-fi records.

title: Right Back To It (feat. MJ Lenderman)
fact: "Right Back to It" is the lead single from Waxahatchee's 2024 album "Tigers Blood," recorded at Sonic Ranch in Tornillo, Texas with producer Brad Cook. Katie Crutchfield wrote it backstage at Virginia's Wolf Trap while opening for Sheryl Crow and Jason Isbell, and the duet with MJ Lenderman marked his first appearance on the Billboard charts.

title: Sparks Fly
fact: 'Sparks Fly' appears on Waxahatchee's 2017 album Out in the Storm, recorded by Katie Crutchfield with her twin sister Allison playing keyboards and singing harmonies. The lyrics describe staying up all night at a Berlin bar and watching the sunrise, building from a quiet acoustic strum into a huge, chorus-swirled finish.

title: Where's Your Love Now
album: Box for Buddy, Box for Star
fact: 'Where's Your Love Now' is actually a cover -- Katie Crutchfield, who records as Waxahatchee, fell for the song by songwriter Nate Amos of This Is Lorelei and called it 'one of the best songs I've ever heard.' Her studio version even features Amos himself singing backing vocals. Crutchfield had been performing the song live for a while before officially releasing her take.

title: Miffed It
fact: Way Dynamic is the songwriting project of Melbourne's Dylan Young, and "Miffed It" appeared in 2025 on his third album, Massive Shoe. The album brings in backing musicians on pedal steel, upright bass, and clarinet, and this song's hushed tone has been compared to Nick Drake.

title: Officially
fact: Officially was released August 5, 2026 as a new song on the Jagjaguwar reissue of Massive Shoe, the album from Melbourne musician Dylan Young, who records as Way Dynamic.

Theme From The Dukes Of Hazzard (Good Ol' Boys)

title: Highwayman
Bath County
fact: Wednesday's "Bath County," from their 2023 album Rat Saw God, gets its title from an actual trip songwriter Karly Hartzman took with her partner, which included a stop at Dollywood and time spent sitting on a porch in Bath County, Virginia, where she wrote the song. The Asheville band's lineup on the record includes guitarist MJ Lenderman, bassist Margo Shultz, drummer Alan Miller, and pedal steel player Xandy Chelmis.

title: Chosen to Deserve
fact: Chosen to Deserve was the January 2023 single that announced Wednesday's fifth album, Rat Saw God (Dead Oceans, April 2023). Songwriter Karly Hartzman has said hearing the Drive-By Truckers song Let There Be Rock helped inspire it.

title: Elderberry Wine
fact: "Elderberry Wine" was Wednesday's first new song after their acclaimed 2023 album "Rat Saw God," co-led as always by singer-guitarists Karly Hartzman and MJ Lenderman and rooted in the band's Asheville, North Carolina home base. Its video, directed by Spencer Kelly, was filmed at a longtime Greensboro bar using real regulars as extras, including Hartzman's own father.

title: Fate Is...
album: I Was Trying to Describe You to Someone
fact: "Fate Is..." opens Wednesday's 2020 sophomore album I Was Trying to Describe You to Someone, the Asheville band's first real step into the alt-country sound that would define their later work. Songwriter Karly Hartzman draws on Southern literary imagery to describe stubbornly facing up to the consequences of one's own choices.

title: Handsome Man
fact: "Handsome Man" comes from Wednesday's 2021 album Twin Plagues, written by frontwoman Karly Hartzman and produced by Adam McDaniel and Alex Farrar. The Asheville band, which features guitarist (and now solo star) MJ Lenderman, built the track around layers of fuzzy, feedback-heavy multi-guitar interplay, including steel guitar, alternating with quieter passages.

title: How Can You Live If You Can't Love How Can You If You Do
fact: Wednesday's Karly Hartzman has described 'How Can You Live If You Can't Love How Can You If You Do' as 'a Big Star-esque love song concocted around a James Baldwin quote' from his novel Another Country. It's a notable stylistic left turn for the Asheville band, trading their usual buzzsaw guitars and feedback for twangy pedal steel and gentle acoustic tones. The track appears on 2021's Twin Plagues.

title: Pick Up That Knife
fact: "Pick Up That Knife," from Wednesday's 2025 album Bleeds, grew out of an unglamorous real-life memory: pedal steel player Xandy Chelmis getting sick in the mosh pit during Death Grips' set at Primavera Sound in 2023. Frontwoman Karly Hartzman has pointed to that chaotic moment as part of the spark for the song.

title: Quarry
fact: "Quarry" appears on Wednesday's 2023 album Rat Saw God, which the Asheville, North Carolina band recorded in just a week at the local Drop of Sun studio. Several reviewers noted that the song's opening verse echoes the chord changes and mood of The Kinks' "Waterloo Sunset" before the chorus breaks into a wall of distorted, shoegaze-indebted guitar.

title: Twin Plagues
fact: 'Twin Plagues' is the title track that opens Wednesday's breakout 2021 album of the same name, written by Karly Hartzman. Hartzman borrowed the phrase from author Richard Brautigan and uses it as a stand-in for the way certain personal events seem to recur throughout a life, like a cycle that can't quite be escaped. It set the tone for a record full of vivid, novelistic storytelling about growing up in North Carolina.

title: Wound Up Here (By Holdin On)
fact: Karly Hartzman borrowed the chorus line from a poem in her friend Evan Gray's book Thickets Swamped in Fence-Coated Briars and wrote the rest of the song around it. It's from Wednesday's sixth album, Bleeds (September 19, 2025, Dead Oceans), produced by Alex Farrar, and the first to feature bassist Ethan Baechtold.

title: Birthday Boy
fact: Birthday Boy was written by Aaron Freeman (Gene Ween) and appears on Ween's 1990 album GodWeenSatan: The Oneness. Gene Ween had actually been playing the song solo and acoustic during radio session appearances months before the studio version came out, and it remained a recurring pick in his acoustic sets for years afterward.

title: Gabrielle
fact: "Gabrielle" was originally recorded by Ween in 1994 during the sessions for their album Chocolate and Cheese but was left off that record. It finally saw official release more than a decade later on the 2005 outtakes compilation Shinola, Vol. 1.

title: Japanese Cowboy
fact: "Japanese Cowboy," from Ween's 1996 album 12 Golden Country Greats, has a melody close enough to Vangelis' "Chariots of Fire" that the band has performed the two songs back-to-back as a medley in concert. The album later got a 30th-anniversary deluxe reissue featuring 26 previously unreleased demos and outtakes.

title: Learnin' to Love
fact: Ween's “Learnin' to Love” came together after Gene Ween stumbled on a website full of horse-racing betting slang and turned it into a song.

title: Push th' Little Daisies
fact: "Push th' Little Daisies" is from Ween's third album, Pure Guava (November 1992), and was released as a single in 1993. It got a big boost after MTV's Beavis and Butt-head commented on the video, and it reached number 21 on Billboard's Modern Rock Tracks chart.

title: She Wanted to Leave (reprise)
fact: 'She Wanted to Leave (Reprise)' closes out Ween's 1997 concept album The Mollusk, a nautical-themed record, reprising the earlier song's yarn about a sailor whose love is carried off by pirates. Musically, the reprise plays as the band's homage/parody of British prog-rock group the Moody Blues.

title: The Argus
fact: The Argus is from Quebec, Ween's eighth studio album, released August 5, 2003. The roughly five-minute song builds to a guitar solo from Dean Ween (Mickey Melchiondo) and takes its imagery from the many-eyed giant Argus of Greek mythology.

title: Tried and True
fact: 'Tried and True' appears on Ween's 2003 album Quebec, the eighth LP from the New Hope, Pennsylvania duo of Gene Ween and Dean Ween. Amid the band's usual genre-hopping and irreverent humor, the track stands out as one of their more straightforwardly sincere, melodic songs. It's remained a fan favorite and a staple that showcases a more earnest side of the band's songwriting.

Baby Don't
fact: "Baby Don't" appears on Hoopla, the 2026 sophomore album from Weird Nightmare, the melodic side project of Alex Edkins, better known as the frontman of noise-punk band METZ. Weird Nightmare trades METZ's abrasive volume for hooky, jangling pop-rock songwriting.

title: Headful of Rain
fact: Weird Nightmare is the solo project of Alex Edkins, longtime frontman of the noise-rock trio METZ. Headful of Rain opens his 2026 album Hoopla, which he made with Spoon's Jim Eno at Machines with Magnets studio.

title: Might See You There
fact: "Might See You There," from the 2026 album Hoopla, is a jangly, nostalgic song about hometown boredom, hanging out in basements, and learning an entire punk catalog with friends. Weird Nightmare is the melodic solo project of Alex Edkins, better known as the frontman of the band METZ.

title: Can't See
album: So Much Country 'Till We Get There

title: Coyote
fact: Westside Cowboy is a four-piece band - Jimmy Bradbury, Reuben Haycocks, Aoife Anson O'Connell, and Paddy Murphy - who formed in Manchester in 2023. "Coyote" comes from their debut album, It Goes On, released in August 2026.

title: Don't Throw Rocks
album: So Much Country 'Till We Get There
fact: "Don't Throw Rocks" is the lead single from Westside Cowboy's second EP, So Much Country 'Till We Get There, released in January 2026 by the Manchester four-piece, winners of the 2025 Glastonbury Emerging Talent Competition. The song grew out of a lo-fi drum-machine demo made in a bandmate's bedroom and reflects on the passing of time.

title: Kick Stones (The Boys)
fact: "Kick Stones (The Boys)" is the lead single and opening track from Westside Cowboy's debut album It Goes On, released via Island Records. The Manchester four-piece has said a live recording of The Velvet Underground's "What Goes On" was a reference point while writing the song, and its music video was filmed at an FC United of Manchester match, featuring the club's players, volunteers, and supporters.

title: Paper Chains
fact: Westside Cowboy's "Paper Chains" is the second track on 2026's It Goes On, the Manchester four-piece's debut album.

title: Pin Up Boys
fact: Pin Up Boys is a single from It Goes On, the debut album from Manchester four-piece Westside Cowboy (August 21, Island Records). The band wrote it using an acoustic guitar, a drum machine sample pad and screwdrivers as drumsticks, then recorded it at Greenmount Studios in Leeds with producer Loren Humphrey.

title: The Wahs
album: So Much Country 'Till We Get There
fact: Manchester band Westside Cowboy — Jimmy Bradbury, Reuben Haycocks, Aoife Anson O'Connell, and Paddy Murphy — has said "The Wahs" started out almost as a joke before they realized the riff was too good to leave behind. The foot-on-the-accelerator track channels a 1990s American indie-rock sound.

title: catch these fists
fact: Catch These Fists was the first single from Wet Leg's second album, moisturizer (July 2025), which Rhian Teasdale and Hester Chambers made with producer Dan Carey. They focused on making songs that would be fun to play live, and the album debuted at number one in the UK.

title: A Lot's Gonna Change
fact: "A Lot's Gonna Change" opens Weyes Blood's 2019 album "Titanic Rising," which Natalie Mering recorded with producer Jonathan Rado of Foxygen. The track pairs lush baroque strings and piano with a maximalist arrangement that still leaves room for Mering's vocals, setting the cinematic tone for the rest of the record.

title: Andromeda
fact: Andromeda was the lead single from Weyes Blood's Titanic Rising (2019), co-produced by Natalie Mering and Jonathan Rado. Its space-themed video was partly filmed in 2018 but not finished until 2024, with Mering playing both an astronaut and an alien riding a meteor.

title: Children of the Empire
album: And in the Darkness, Hearts Aglow
fact: "Children of the Empire" is from Weyes Blood's 2022 album And in the Darkness, Hearts Aglow, the second chapter in a trilogy that began with 2019's Titanic Rising. Natasha Mering said she realized she had "a few songs left over" from that earlier album, which grew into this one; she co-produced the track with Jonathan Rado.

title: Everyday
fact: "Everyday," the second single from Weyes Blood's 2019 album Titanic Rising, channels a 1970s psychedelic-pop sound with an upbeat piano melody. Singer Natalie Mering has said the song is about the chaos and exhaustion of modern dating, likening it to everyone "sailing off onto ships to nowhere."

title: God Turn Me into a Flower
album: And in the Darkness, Hearts Aglow

title: Grapevine
album: And in the Darkness, Hearts Aglow
fact: "Grapevine" takes its title from the notorious stretch of Interstate 5 that climbs through Southern California's Tejon Pass, which Natalie Mering, who records as Weyes Blood, uses as a metaphor for old emotional entanglements that twist around us. She co-wrote and produced the track with Jonathan Rado for her 2022 album And in the Darkness, Hearts Aglow. The song opens on acoustic guitar before eerie bells ring out over the chorus.

title: It's Not Just Me, It's Everybody
album: And in the Darkness, Hearts Aglow
fact: "It's Not Just Me, It's Everybody" is the lead single from Weyes Blood's 2022 album And in the Darkness, Hearts Aglow, co-written with Ben Babbitt and Jonathan Rado and featuring harpist Mary Lattimore. Weyes Blood has called it a "Buddhist anthem" about the shared, universal nature of personal pain.

title: Movies
fact: Weyes Blood's “Movies” is an ode to cinema as a modern myth-maker - she wants her own life to have the meaning a movie does, even while admitting “the meaning of life doesn't seem to shine like that screen.”

title: Twin Flame
album: And in the Darkness, Hearts Aglow
fact: "Twin Flame," from Weyes Blood's 2022 album And in the Darkness, Hearts Aglow, playfully pokes fun at the New Age idea of a "twin flame" soulmate. Natalie Mering has described the twin-flame concept as the destructive kind of soulmate, where the highs and lows are so extreme the relationship can't last, set here to downtempo, '80s-tinged electronic production.

title: Wild Time
fact: "Wild Time," from Weyes Blood's 2019 album Titanic Rising, builds from Natalie Mering's piano and acoustic guitar into a lush orchestral arrangement featuring strings, trumpet, and a full-throated French horn solo. The dense, cinematic orchestration — with contributions from players like Daphne Chen and Eric Gorfain — reflects the album's broader 1970s-FM-radio-inspired production style.

title: Nothing On Me
fact: Nothing On Me opens White Lies' seventh album, Night Light (Play It Again Sam, November 2025). The trio recorded the whole record in singer Harry McVeigh's spare room.

title: Rigamarole
album: The Older I Get The Funnier I Was

title: Damage
fact: "Damage" is a single from Whitney's 2025 album Small Talk, recorded by the duo of Max Kakacek (formerly of Smith Westerns) and Julien Ehrlich (formerly of Unknown Mortal Orchestra) without an outside producer, with friends dropping into the studio to add parts. Ehrlich has said the band spent a while trying to avoid writing another breakup song before accepting the song needed to be one, as long as it felt distinctly Whitney.

title: No Matter Where We Go
fact: "No Matter Where We Go" comes from Whitney's 2016 debut Light Upon the Lake, written by Chicago duo Max Kakacek and Julien Ehrlich (previously of Smith Westerns and Unknown Mortal Orchestra, respectively). The song rides a chugging, Creedence Clearwater Revival-style groove topped with vocal harmonies reminiscent of Crosby, Stills & Nash.

title: See You Later, I'm Gone
fact: Whitney formed in Chicago in 2015 out of the ashes of two other bands: guitarist Max Kakacek had just come off Smith Westerns, while drummer-turned-frontman Julien Ehrlich had been keeping time for Unknown Mortal Orchestra. "See You Later, I'm Gone" is a more recent single from the duo, continuing the warm, horn-dusted sound they've built since their 2016 debut Light Upon the Lake.

If You Change
fact: If You Change is the lead single from Widowspeak's seventh album, Roses (2026, Captured Tracks), their first studio album since 2022's The Jacket. Molly Hamilton and Robert Earl Thomas recorded it at the Old Carpet Factory studio on the Greek island of Hydra.

title: Ashes of American Flags
fact: This Yankee Hotel Foxtrot track was recorded at Wilco's own Chicago studio, The Loft, during sessions that ran from late 2000 into the summer of 2001. Keyboardist and engineer Jay Bennett spent painstaking effort crafting the song's ten-second crossfade into the following track, 'Heavy Metal Drummer,' aiming for a seamless transition between the two very different songs.

title: Box Full of Letters
fact: "Box Full of Letters" was Wilco's debut single, released from their first album A.M. in 1995. It's often read as addressing the breakup of Jeff Tweedy's previous band, Uncle Tupelo, with its multilayered guitars giving the track a gritty, lived-in texture.

title: Casino Queen
fact: "Casino Queen" is a highlight from Wilco's 1995 debut album, A.M., named after a real riverboat casino. Jeff Tweedy has said he wrote the song at his father's suggestion that the boat would make good song material, and former Uncle Tupelo touring guitarist Brian Henneman guests on the track's raucous slide guitar.

title: Citizens
fact: 'Citizens' appears on Wilco's 2019 album Ode to Joy, recorded at the band's Chicago studio The Loft. For the record, classically trained drummer Glenn Kotche skipped playing a full kit and instead built his parts by recording individual percussion elements separately before stitching them together in the mix, giving the album's rhythms their distinct, orchestral feel.

title: Cousin
fact: The title track of Wilco's 2023 album "Cousin" marked the first time in over a decade that the band brought in an outside producer, Welsh musician Cate Le Bon. Tweedy and Le Bon first met when her band played Wilco's own Solid Sound Festival in 2019, leading to an invitation to produce the record at the band's Chicago studio, The Loft.

title: Everyone Hides
fact: "Everyone Hides" appears on Wilco's 2019 album Ode to Joy and was recorded at the band's own studio, The Loft, in Chicago. Its music video has the band literally playing a game of hide-and-seek around The Loft and the surrounding neighborhood, including a hiding spot inside the building pictured on the cover of their classic album Yankee Hotel Foxtrot.

title: Hearts Hard to Find
fact: This one's tucked into Wilco's sprawling 2022 double album Cruel Country, cut live at the band's own Chicago studio, The Loft. The sessions marked the first time all six members tracked together in one room since 2011's The Whole Love — Jeff Tweedy described that kind of live recording as "gathering around some wild collective instrument" that takes six sets of hands to play.

title: Hot Sun
fact: Wilco's 'Hot Sun' comes from the Hot Sun Cool Shroud EP, a 2024 release built from material recorded during the sessions for their album Cousin. The track leans into rolling, twangy guitars that echo the band's alt-country roots from the 1990s. Lyrically, it follows Jeff Tweedy's recurring theme of searching for meaning, framed against the image of an oppressive, inescapable sun.

title: I Am Trying to Break Your Heart
I'm a Wheel
fact: I'm a Wheel comes from Wilco's fifth studio album, A Ghost Is Born (June 22, 2004), and was released as a single on July 26, 2004.

title: I'm the Man Who Loves You
If I Ever Was A Child
Impossible Germany
fact: "Impossible Germany," from Wilco's 2007 album Sky Blue Sky, is built around an extended Nels Cline guitar solo that covers more than half the song. Cline has said he originally planned a scripted instrumental coda inspired by Television's "The Dream's Dream," but Jeff Tweedy talked him into just soloing instead. Live, the arrangement often stretches toward ten minutes, with Tweedy and Pat Sansone each playing separate interlocking guitar parts that build to meet Cline's solo.

title: Locator
fact: Wilco's "Locator" was released as the lead single from 2016's Schmilco - the band put it out on the exact one-year anniversary of their surprise previous album, also called Star Wars. Where Star Wars leaned into fuzzy glam guitars, Schmilco was a much more acoustic, stripped-down record.

title: Love Is Everywhere (Beware)
fact: Love Is Everywhere (Beware) was released as a single on July 16, 2019, ahead of Wilco's eleventh studio album, Ode to Joy, which came out October 4, 2019.

title: More...
fact: "More..." is the second track on Wilco's surprise 2015 album Star Wars, which the band released as a free download with no advance notice and a title that has nothing to do with the film franchise. The song's acoustic-driven verses give way to gnarled, swirling guitar effects, a tonal shift that stood out on the brief, 11-track record.

title: Quiet Amplifier
fact: "Quiet Amplifier" is widely seen as the centerpiece of Wilco's 2019 album Ode to Joy, pairing unusually heavy, march-like percussion with a warm cloud of guitars and cymbal shimmer. Jeff Tweedy's lyrics turn the song toward a hopeful close, singing "Shy little stars will shine."

title: Random Name Generator
fact: "Random Name Generator" appears on Wilco's 2015 album Star Wars, which the band surprised fans by releasing as a free download with no advance notice. Critics noted the song's fuzzed-out riff and stomping drums channel the glam-rock swagger of T. Rex.

title: Spiders (Kidsmoke)
fact: "Spiders (Kidsmoke)" started out as a straightforward folk-rock tune Wilco played on the Yankee Hotel Foxtrot tour, but during the sessions for 2004's A Ghost Is Born the band transformed it into an 11-minute motorik workout built on Glenn Kotche's metronomic drumming and interlocking keyboards from Mikael Jorgenson and producer Jim O'Rourke. It became one of the band's first extended guitar epics, drawing comparisons to Krautrock acts like Can and Neu!.

title: Taste the Ceiling
fact: "Taste the Ceiling" is track six on Wilco's Star Wars, the band's surprise free album released in July 2015. The song was co-written by Jeff Tweedy and longtime touring collaborator Scott McCaughey, and critics singled it out as one of the record's gentlest, most classic-pop moments.

title: The Joke Explained
fact: The Joke Explained is on Wilco's 2015 album Star Wars, which the band surprised fans with by releasing without advance announcement. The song is a fuzzy garage-rock number built around the line "I cry at a joke explained."

title: We Were Lucky
fact: "We Were Lucky" comes from Wilco's 2019 album Ode to Joy, which frontman Jeff Tweedy built out from simple song sketches he first recorded with drummer Glenn Kotche before the rest of the band filled them in. That process gives the record, and this track, a stripped-down, minimalist feel, with Kotche's steady, understated drumming driving much of the album rather than his usual intricate percussion work. It's a quieter, more intimate turn for a band known for sprawling arrangements.

title: You Satellite
fact: "You Satellite" comes from Wilco's 2015 album "Star Wars," which the band released as a complete surprise free download with no advance announcement. The song was co-written by Jeff Tweedy, drummer Glenn Kotche, and guitarist Nels Cline, and was recorded at the band's own Chicago studio, the Loft.

title: A Dancing Shell
fact: 'A Dancing Shell' comes from Wild Nothing's 2013 EP Empty Estate, recorded at Gary's Electric studio in Brooklyn in January of that year. The track opens with washy, wave-like percussion and a chirping synth arpeggio before building into a genuinely funky dance groove, with a burst of brass kicking in after the two-minute mark. It was a notable left turn for a band that made its name on dreamy, jangly guitar pop.

title: A Woman's Wisdom
fact: "A Woman's Wisdom" is track three on Wild Nothing's third album, Life of Pause (2016, Captured Tracks). It finds songwriter Jack Tatum pivoting from the band's shimmery '80s dream-pop toward a warmer blend of '70s AM-radio soul, funk, and R&B, with disco-tinged synth lines underpinning his breathy vocal. Critics compared the track's style to a mix of Jim O'Rourke and Tobias Jesso Jr.

title: Headlights On (feat. Hatchie)
fact: Headlights On is the first single from Hold (October 27, 2023, Captured Tracks), Wild Nothing's first album in five years. Jack Tatum's first self-produced record since his debut has Hatchie on backing vocals.

title: Life of Pause
fact: "Life of Pause" is the title track of Wild Nothing's 2016 album, released on Captured Tracks and Bella Union and produced by Thom Monahan. The song's shimmering synths and driving drums have drawn comparisons to early-1980s David Bowie, and critics singled it out as one of the record's most purely pop moments.

title: Nocturne
fact: Nocturne is the title track of Wild Nothing's 2012 second album on Captured Tracks. Jack Tatum recorded it in a real studio in Brooklyn with producer Nicolas Vernhes, after making the debut, Gemini, entirely on a laptop.

title: Ocean Repeating (Big Eye Girl)
fact: This one lands between Wild Nothing's two most acclaimed records, written and produced solo by Jack Tatum for the 2013 Empty Estate release, which bridged the gap between 2012's Nocturne and 2016's Life of Pause. It's a nice showcase of Tatum working entirely on his own rather than in the fuller studio setup he used on Nocturne.

title: Only Heather
fact: Wild Nothing's "Only Heather" comes from 2012's Nocturne - Jack Tatum's second album under the Wild Nothing name, which he began recording alone in Blacksburg, Virginia back in 2009.

title: Shadow
fact: "Shadow" was the first song released from Wild Nothing's second album, Nocturne (August 2012, Captured Tracks). It features a string section, something bandleader Jack Tatum says he never could have done on his earlier home recordings without a proper studio.

title: Shallow Water
fact: Jack Tatum wrote "Shallow Water," from Wild Nothing's 2018 album Indigo, as a love song for his wife, calling it a track about "finally arriving in the place you were meant to be." Musically it leans into 1980s new wave, pairing a post-punk bassline with Cocteau Twins-style synth textures.

title: Summer Holiday
fact: 'Summer Holiday' was Wild Nothing's very first single, released on Captured Tracks at the end of 2009 before founder Jack Tatum had even settled on a full band. It later appeared on Wild Nothing's 2010 debut album Gemini, with lyrics drawn from Tatum's teenage memories.

title: To Know You
fact: "To Know You" comes from Wild Nothing's third album, Life of Pause (2016), produced by Thom Monahan. It first appeared in late 2015 as one side of a double A-side single paired with "TV Queen," each track getting its own music video.

title: TV Queen
fact: Wild Nothing's "TV Queen," from 2016's Life of Pause, was recorded across sessions in Los Angeles and Stockholm with producer Thom Monahan - Peter Bjorn and John's John Eriksson guested on drums and marimba.

title: Air Drumming Fix You
fact: Air Drumming Fix You, released in March 2024, was Wild Pink's first new music since 2022's ILYSM and came with the band signing to Fire Talk Records. The title nods to Coldplay's Fix You, and the song ends with saxophones.

title: Box Store
fact: "Box Store" is the harmonica-laced opening track from Wild Pink's 2026 album Still Coming Down, and it's built around an unusually specific pair of subjects: a window-unit air conditioner and character actor William Fichtner. Frontman John Ross said the loping, wistful song reminded him of Warren Zevon, so he leaned into that direction while writing it.

title: Cloud or Mountain
fact: "Cloud or Mountain" appears on Wild Pink's 2024 album Dulling the Horns. The track shifts between a country-tinged feel and heavier, sludgier passages, and features pedal steel guitar from Mike "Slo-Mo" Brenner.

title: Dead For A Sec
fact: Wild Pink's "Dead for a Sec," from 2026's Still Coming Down, features MJ Lenderman harmonizing on the chorus and tearing into a Crazy Horse-style guitar solo over the outro - the album was recorded in just one week at Drop of Sun studios in Asheville with producer Alex Farrar.

title: Dulling The Horns
fact: Wild Pink began writing 'Dulling the Horns' during soundchecks while touring behind their 2022 album ILYSM. For the resulting 2024 album of the same name, frontman John Ross chose to record live in the room with engineer Justin Pizzoferrato, aiming for a rawer sound and citing Weezer's Blue Album as a guitar-tone reference point.

title: Pacific City
fact: Wild Pink's "Pacific City," from 2021's A Billion Little Lights, is named for the small town on the Oregon coast - frontman John Ross wrote it while watching the movie Heat, and it features the band's first-ever saxophone solo, played by Stephen Chen of San Fermin.

title: Round Of Applause At The End Of The World
fact: The lead single from Wild Pink's 2026 album Still Coming Down, led by singer-songwriter John Ross, brought in a stacked guest list: Wednesday's Xandy Chelmis on pedal steel, plus Hand Habits' Meg Duffy and members of MJ Lenderman's backing band The Wind. Ross himself plays the song's wheezing harmonica and accordion parts.

title: The Grass Widow In The Glass Window
Hang Up
fact: Hang Up is from the debut EP Bad Bad Luck (August 2021) by Wilder., a Long Beach, California duo of guitarist and vocalist Stephen Ramos and drummer Nick Sturz.

title: Return of the Rat
fact: "Return of the Rat" comes from Portland punk band the Wipers, led by guitarist Greg Sage, whose stripped-down, fuzzed-out sound became a direct blueprint for the grunge scene that followed a decade later. Kurt Cobain repeatedly named Wipers albums among the most influential records on Nirvana's own sound, and Nirvana recorded a faithful studio cover of "Return of the Rat" that was later released as a B-side.

title: When It's Over
fact: Clocking in past six minutes, "When It's Over" is one of the extended guitar "freakouts" that made 1981's "Youth of America" such a leap from the Wipers' earlier punk sound. Greg Sage's experimentation on that record is widely cited as a touchstone for the Pacific Northwest bands who came after, including Nirvana.

title: Youth of America
fact: The title track of Wipers' 1981 album Youth of America stretches to roughly ten minutes, a deliberate response from frontman Greg Sage against the era's trend of short, fast punk songs. The sprawling, motorik track went on to influence Sonic Youth and the broader noise-rock scene, and it's been covered by both the Melvins and Mission of Burma. Kurt Cobain later named the Youth of America album among his fifty favorite albums of all time.

title: 1 2 X U
fact: This track is on Wire's debut album Pink Flag (1977), produced by Mike Thorne and recorded in about a month at Advision Studios in London. The album squeezes 21 songs into roughly 35 minutes, and is now regarded as a landmark of post-punk.

title: Mannequin
fact: "Mannequin" is on Wire's debut album Pink Flag (1977), produced by Mike Thorne at Advision Studios in London. The album packs 21 songs into about 35 minutes, since Wire stopped each song as soon as it had said what it needed to.

title: Too Late
fact: "Too Late" appears on Wire's second album, Chairs Missing, released in September 1978. Produced by Mike Thorne, the record pushed the English post-punk band toward more atmospheric, synth-tinged textures than their stripped-down 1977 debut, Pink Flag, and the track was written by guitarist Bruce Gilbert.

title: Covergirl
fact: "Covergirl" appears on Triple Seven (2024), the debut album from Indianapolis band Wishy. Co-founders Kevin Krauter (formerly of the band Hoops) and Nina Pitchkites met in high school and started Wishy together in 2021 after Pitchkites moved back to Indiana from Philadelphia. The song's hazy, drum-driven sound has drawn comparisons to shoegaze acts like My Bloody Valentine.

title: Fly
fact: Wishy is an Indianapolis indie-rock band built around Kevin Krauter, formerly of the band Hoops, and Nina Pitchkites, who actually met years earlier as students at Carmel High School. They didn't form Wishy together until 2021, after following separate musical paths. "Fly" opens their 2025 EP Planet Popstar.

title: Lovesick
fact: Wishy is an indie band built around Kevin Krauter (formerly of the band Hoops) and Nina Pitchkites, who first met in high school in Indianapolis but didn't start making music together until years later. "Lovesick," sung by Pitchkites, was released in 2026 as the lead single from the band's second album, Nature's Pill, on the Winspear label.

title: Mona Lisa
fact: Wishy's "Mona Lisa," from 2026's Nature's Pill, is a slacker-pop love song that closes out with a minute and a half of sing-along "oohs" and "aahs" - frontman Kevin Krauter met his bandmates in high school back in Indianapolis.

title: Persuasion
fact: Persuasion is the fourth track on Triple Seven (2024), the debut album by Wishy of Indianapolis. Kevin Krauter teaches drum and guitar lessons, and Nina Pitchkites is a seamstress who makes embroidered merch for the band.

title: Sensational
fact: Wishy's "Sensational" grew out of a bassline Mitch Collins kept noodling on during soundchecks - it's a stylistic left turn from their earlier singles on 2026's Nature's Pill, its music video built from an animated collage of 3,000 cut-outs of the band.

title: See you soon
fact: "See You Soon" is the second single from Wisp's 2024 debut EP Pandora, released via Music Soup/Interscope. Built from a beat originally made by producer Grayskies, the shoegaze track pairs swirling, distorted guitars with Wisp's airy vocals, building toward a cathartic release in the chorus.

title: Your face
fact: "Your Face" was Wisp's debut single, released in April 2023 — the song she's called "the one I owe for everything," since it launched her career. It went viral on TikTok and spent 15 weeks on Billboard's Hot Hard Rock Songs chart, peaking at No. 8, later becoming the lead single on her 2024 EP Pandora.

title: Young, Wild, Free feat. Snoop Dogg & Bruno Mars
Call It a Ritual
fact: Wolf Parade came together in under three weeks - Spencer Krug got a last-minute offer to play a show, recruited guitarist Dan Boeckner, and the two wrote songs together before the band had even rehearsed as a full trio.

title: Dinner Bells
fact: "Dinner Bells," written by Spencer Krug, closes out Wolf Parade's 2005 debut album Apologies to the Queen Mary at over seven minutes long. An earlier, shorter version of the song had already appeared on the band's self-released 2003 EP before this fuller studio take. Modest Mouse's Isaac Brock produced most of the album, which was recorded between Portland, Oregon, and Montreal.

title: Shine A Light
fact: "Shine a Light" is on Wolf Parade's debut album, Apologies to the Queen Mary (September 2005, Sub Pop). It also appeared on the band's self-titled 2005 EP, and the album is now regarded as a landmark of mid-2000s indie rock.

title: What Did My Lover Say? (It Always Had to Go This Way)
You Are a Runner and I Am My Father's Son
fact: This one kicks off Wolf Parade's 2005 debut Apologies to the Queen Mary, which has a cool Modest Mouse connection: Isaac Brock heard the band, loved them, and personally helped record much of the album with engineer Chris Chandler at Audible Alchemy studio in Portland. A stripped-down version of the song had already circulated on the band's self-released 2005 EP before this fuller take became the album's opening statement.

title: You're Dreaming
fact: 'You're Dreaming' is a staccato-organ-driven rocker from Cry Cry Cry, Wolf Parade's 2017 comeback album made after the band's hiatus following 2010's Expo 86. It served as the record's second single.

title: Be All Be Easy
fact: Woods originally released 'Be All Be Easy' on their 2011 album Sun and Shade, then re-recorded it for a 2013 7-inch single to capture the more muscular arrangement it had grown into on tour. That single, backed with a cover of the Kinks' 'God's Children,' marked the studio debut of new drummer Aaron Neveu and served as a farewell recording at Rear House, the home studio the Brooklyn band had used for a decade.

title: Be There Still
fact: 'Be There Still' is track 10 on Woods' 2020 album Strange to Explain, the band's 99th release on their own Woodsist label. An alternate version of the song later appeared on the deluxe edition, More Strange, released the following year.

title: Bend Beyond
fact: "Bend Beyond" is both the title track and opening song of Woods' seventh studio album, released in September 2012. It kicks off a brisk 12-song, 32-minute record from the Brooklyn band, known for releasing music on their own label, Woodsist.

title: Between The Past
album: Between The Past & White Winter Melody
fact: "Between the Past" was released in 2023 as one of two lead singles (alongside "White Winter Melody") announcing Woods' album Perennial. Led by Jeremy Earl, the Brooklyn psych-folk band built the track around Beatles-esque wind instruments and a warm, hymn-like arrangement as the group approached its 20th year together.

title: Bleeding Blue
fact: "Bleeding Blue" is the third track on "Love Is Love," the 2017 album by Brooklyn folk-rock band Woods, who formed in 2005. The song stands out for its horn-gilded arrangement, with Alec Spiegelman on sax and flute and Cole Kamen-Green on trumpet giving it a funkier sound than much of the band's earlier catalog.

title: Can't See at All
album: City Sun Eater in the River of Light
fact: Woods' "Can't See at All" was one of three singles - along with "Sun City Creeps" and "Morning Light" - that led up to 2016's City Sun Eater in the River of Light, the band's follow-up to 2014's With Light and With Love.

title: Creature Comfort
album: City Sun Eater in the River of Light

title: Little Black Flowers
fact: "Little Black Flowers" was released August 30, 2023 as a double single with "Day Moving On" ahead of Woods' album Perennial. It was recorded with longtime producer Jarvis Taveniere at Panoramic House in Stinson Beach, California, with additional sessions in Los Angeles and Stone Ridge, New York.

title: Love Is Love
fact: "Love Is Love" is the title track of Woods' 2017 mini-album of the same name, a six-song set the band wrote and recorded quickly and released on their own Woodsist label. Musically, the song draws as much from Ethiopian jazz as it does from 1960s American rock, giving it a warm, loping feel.

title: Pushing Onlys
fact: "Pushing Onlys" opens Woods' 2011 album "Sun and Shade," a notably poppier, more polished turn for the Brooklyn band. Frontman Jeremy Earl sings the track in his signature falsetto about getting older.

title: Shining
fact: Woods' "Shining," from 2014's With Light and With Love, packs a lot of sound into just two minutes - Pitchfork described its lush arrangement as showing off "darker shades of American Beauty," a nod to the Grateful Dead's classic 1970 album.

title: Its Way With Me
fact: Wye Oak's "Its Way With Me," written by the songwriting duo of Andy Stack and Jenn Wasner, is about learning to feel at peace amid change and things beyond your control - a theme the Baltimore duo has returned to since reinventing their sound around Wasner's bass playing on 2014's Shriek.
