title: Germ Free Adolescents
fact: X-Ray Spex's Germfree Adolescents came out on November 10, 1978, and stood out among punk records of the era for putting saxophone front and center alongside the guitars. Frontwoman Poly Styrene wrote every song on the album, and critics praised her sharp, sing-song melodies over the band's distinctively off-kilter horn section. The Guinness Encyclopedia of Popular Music later named it one of the greatest punk albums ever released.

title: Dear God
fact: "Dear God" was originally tucked away as a B-side to the 1986 single "Grass," but American college radio DJs started flipping the record over and playing it instead, turning it into an unplanned hit that got it added to later pressings of the album Skylarking. The opening and closing vocal lines were actually performed by eight-year-old Jasmine Veillette, the daughter of a friend of producer Todd Rundgren, though in the music video her part is lip-synced by a boy.

title: Jason and the Argonauts
fact: According to frontman Andy Partridge, the song came title-first-in-reverse — he was playing a guitar figure that evoked the feeling of sailing across open water, and "Jason and the Argonauts" was simply the image that fit the mood. The six-minute track, one of the longest on 1982's English Settlement, was recorded at the Manor Studios in Oxfordshire with producer Hugh Padgham.

title: Senses Working Overtime
fact: "Senses Working Overtime," the lead single from XTC's 1982 album English Settlement, became the band's highest-charting UK single at number 10, while the album itself reached number 5 — the commercial peak of XTC's career.

title: The Mayor of Simpleton
fact: Mayor of Simpleton was the first single from XTC's 1989 album Oranges & Lemons and hit number 1 on Billboard's Alternative Songs chart. Andy Partridge started it as a reggae song before scrapping that and rewriting it around a chiming, droning guitar figure.

title: New Beginnings
album: You're Gonna Need A Little Music
fact: New Beginnings is the second single from Yard Act's third album, You're Gonna Need a Little Music (July 17, 2026, Republic Records). The Leeds band recorded it in LA and Leeds with Nine Inch Nails bassist Justin Meldal-Johnsen, and it's the first time they made a record live in the same room.

title: Petroleum
fact: Yard Act's James Smith wrote 'Petroleum' after losing his patience on stage at a gig in Bognor Regis, telling the crowd flat-out he was bored -- a move that got him a stern talking-to from bandmate Ryan Needham. It sent him down a rabbit hole about what touring actually requires, and how fans often want a performed version of honesty rather than the real thing. That idea lands in the song's refrain about the soul needing 'petroleum' just to keep running. It's off 2024's 'Where's My Utopia?', which found the Leeds post-punk band leaning into a more electronic, psychedelic sound.

title: The Trench Coat Museum
fact: 'The Trench Coat Museum' was produced by Remi Kabaka Jr., best known for his longtime work with Gorillaz. Yard Act frontman James Smith wrote it as a reflection on ego, vanity, and how quickly public perception can shift after a band's rapid rise to fame. The accompanying music video leans into that theme, set decades in the future inside a surreal, dystopian museum exhibit.

title: Gold Lion
fact: "Gold Lion," the lead single from Yeah Yeah Yeahs' 2006 album Show Your Bones, got its title from the two Gold Lion trophies won at the Cannes Lions advertising festival by an Adidas commercial that Karen O had sung on, composed by Sam "Squeak E. Clean" Spiegel and directed by Spike Jonze.

title: Hysteric
fact: 'Hysteric,' from Yeah Yeah Yeahs' 2009 album It's Blitz!, is built on a looping guitar riff that owes a clear debt to Blondie's 'Atomic.' Karen O sings the unguarded line 'you suddenly complete me' without a trace of her usual irony, a notably vulnerable turn for a singer known for ferocity. The track closes on a drifting, whistled outro that became one of the album's most distinctive moments.

title: Slave
fact: 'Slave' is track five on Yeah Yeah Yeahs' 2013 album Mosquito, co-produced by Dave Sitek of TV on the Radio and Nick Launay. It's one of several songs on the record built around dub-reggae-influenced rhythm and production techniques, a notable departure from the trio's earlier, more stripped-down punk sound.

title: Soft Shock
fact: "Soft Shock" comes from Yeah Yeah Yeahs' 2009 album "It's Blitz!" and finds Karen O trading her usual yelps for gentle crooning reminiscent of the band's hit "Maps." The track builds from a hushed, atmospheric ballad into a more forceful climax, with Nick Zinner layering in backmasked guitars as the song progresses.

title: Spitting Off the Edge of the World (feat. Perfume Genius)

fact: "2080" is a track from Yeasayer's 2007 debut album All Hour Cymbals, released as a single paired with "Sunrise" on the label We Are Free. The Brooklyn band, formed in 2006 by Chris Keating, Anand Wilder, and Ira Wolf Tuton, built the song's dense, layered sound from a blend of psychedelic, world-music, and funk-inspired textures that drew comparisons to Fleetwood Mac and Animal Collective. NPR featured it as a "Song of the Day" just weeks after its release.

title: Let Me Listen In On You
Sunrise
fact: "Sunrise" opens Yeasayer's 2007 debut album "All Hour Cymbals" and originally served as the b-side to the single "2080." The track builds from choral harmonies and handclaps into a dense, percussion-heavy climax, reflecting the gospel and world-music influences the Brooklyn band wove into their early sound.

title: Anthems for a Seventeen Year-Old Girl
fact: yeule's cover of Broken Social Scene's "Anthems for a Seventeen Year-Old Girl" was recorded for the soundtrack to the 2024 film I Saw the TV Glow. Director Jane Schoenbrun had originally asked yeule to write an original song, but once the two started talking about this Broken Social Scene classic, they agreed a cover was the better fit. yeule's glitchy, digitally warped version speeds up the melody while keeping the emotional core of the original intact.

title: Did I Tell You
fact: "Did I Tell You" first appeared on Yo La Tengo's 1987 album New Wave Hot Dogs, then was re-recorded as a hushed, late-night ballad for their 1990 covers-and-rarities album Fakebook. On the Fakebook version, Ira Kaplan's conversational lead vocal is paired with Georgia Hubley's airy backing harmonies, giving the song an intimate, heart-to-heart feel.

title: Fallout
fact: "Fallout" was the lead single from Yo La Tengo's 2023 album "This Stupid World," which longtime trio Ira Kaplan, Georgia Hubley, and James McNew made entirely by themselves without an outside producer or mixer. They wanted the record to sound as live and unfiltered as their concerts.

title: From a Motel 6
fact: The title "From a Motel 6" is a cheeky riff on Bob Dylan's "From a Buick 6," and the song appears on Yo La Tengo's 1993 album Painful. It's become a fan favorite for the way Ira Kaplan and Georgia Hubley's soft, dreamy harmonies float over slow-building waves of guitar feedback.

title: I'll Be Around
fact: Yo La Tengo's Ira Kaplan and Georgia Hubley are a married couple - they met at a Feelies concert in Hoboken, New Jersey in 1980, married in 1987, and have played together in the band ever since.

title: Is That Enough
fact: "Is That Enough," from Yo La Tengo's 2013 album Fade, pairs the band's melodic songwriting with a full string quartet arranged by Tortoise guitarist Jeff Parker, giving it a lush, Burt Bacharach-style sweep. The accompanying video was directed by TV writer-producer Donick Cary and featured comic actor Fred Willard.

title: Last Days of Disco
album: And Then Nothing Turned Itself Inside

title: Let's Save Tony Orlando's House
album: And Then Nothing Turned Itself Inside
fact: The title of Yo La Tengo's 'Let's Save Tony Orlando's House' comes from a Simpsons episode, 'Marge on the Lam,' in which Troy McClure jokes about telethons including 'Let's Save Tony Orlando's House.' Bassist James McNew, a lifelong Simpsons fan, had a habit of naming the band's wordless instrumentals after random lines from the show, and this one stuck.

title: Mr. Tough
album: I Am Not Afraid of You and I Will Beat You

title: Ohm
fact: "Ohm" opens Yo La Tengo's 2013 album Fade, the first record the band made with producer John McEntire (Tortoise, The Sea and Cake) instead of longtime collaborator Roger Moutenot, who had produced every album since 1993. The title plays on a double meaning: an ohm is the electrical unit of resistance, but it's pronounced like the meditative "om" chant used in Hinduism and Buddhism. Recorded at Soma Studios in Chicago in summer 2012, the seven-minute track builds around a raga-influenced groove and one of guitarist Ira Kaplan's fuzziest solos on the record.

title: Our Way to Fall
album: And Then Nothing Turned Itself Inside
fact: "Our Way to Fall" appears on Yo La Tengo's 2000 album And Then Nothing Turned Itself Inside-Out, built around gently brushed drums, luminous organ, and Ira Kaplan's hushed vocal. The song later soundtracked a scene in the HBO series Six Feet Under, in the season 2 episode "Driving Mr. Mossback."

title: Pass the Hatchet, I Think I'm Goodkind
album: I Am Not Afraid of You and I Will Beat You

title: Periodically Double or Triple
fact: This 2009 track from Popular Songs was one of the first Yo La Tengo songs that could fairly be called 'boogie,' built on a bluesy rhythm and Green Onions-style organ that critics compared to Booker T. & the M.G.'s and Sun Ra. Ira Kaplan's lyrics name-drop both Marcel Proust and Judge Judy, and the song's music video is shot entirely in stop-motion using pieces of fruit.

title: Rickety
fact: "Rickety" is one of only two brand-new originals on Yo La Tengo's 2015 album "Stuff Like That There," a record that revisited the stripped-down, acoustic covers-album concept of their 1990 release "Fakebook." It's been described as a gentle indie-pop song about the ups and downs of a long relationship.

title: Sinatra Avenue Drive
fact: Yo La Tengo's 'Sinatra Drive Breakdown,' from 2023's This Stupid World, is named after a real waterfront boulevard in the band's longtime home base of Hoboken, New Jersey - fittingly, Frank Sinatra's own hometown. Musically it's a noisy, extended jam built on warped, distorted guitar, blending the trio's early jangle-pop roots with denser, heavier riffing. It stands as one of the rawer, more improvisational moments from a band nearing 40 years together.

title: Wasn't Born to Follow
fact: Yo La Tengo's version of "Wasn't Born to Follow" is a cover of the Byrds' 1968 track, originally written by Gerry Goffin and Carole King, released on the band's Sleepless Night EP via Matador. Longtime collaborator Dave Schramm plays lead guitar on the cover, which stays close to the folk-rock feel of the original.

title: Carsick
fact: Youbet is a Brooklyn-based indie rock band fronted by Nick Llobet. "Carsick" was the first song they shared after signing to Hardly Art in late 2023, and it later appeared on the band's debut full-length, Way To Be.

title: I Saw
fact: 'I Saw' appears on Young Fathers' 2023 album Heavy Heavy. Built around the insistent refrain 'I saw what I saw, I keep on walking the line,' the track channels the Scottish trio's themes of resolve and self-belief.

title: Brenda And Diane
fact: "Brenda & Diane" is a single from Young Jesus's album The Fool on Saddle Creek Records. Songwriter John Rossiter based the Springsteen-indebted rocker on a real encounter with two older women who humbled the narrator out of his own sense of superiority and judgment by showing him the fuller, more complex life they were actually living.

title: Football
fact: "Football" is a 2024 single from Trevor Powers' project Youth Lagoon, reuniting him with producer Rodaidh McDonald. Powers has said the song uses sports as a metaphor, inspired by how throwing a ball was one of the few things he and his father connected over growing up, regardless of skill.

title: Lucy Takes a Picture
fact: Lucy Takes a Picture is from Youth Lagoon's 2025 album Rarely Do I Dream (Fat Possum). Trevor Powers built the album around childhood home videos he found in his parents' basement, and he samples the tapes throughout.

title: Ghosts
fact: "Ghosts" is the lead single from zzzahara's 2025 album Spiral Your Way Out on Lex Records, blending influences from 2000s emo acts like Dashboard Confessional and Scene Aesthetic into a stripped-back, vocal-forward arrangement. The accompanying video, directed by Hannah Bon, renders zzzahara in 3D animation trapped in a surreal dream world, complete with singing cats and ghosts spilling out of lava lamps. It's a playful visual counterpoint to the song's moody tone.
